title: sunbird C/C++: record the owner migration decision against measured criteria
description:
Carried over from `IDEAS-cpp-beat-ccache.md` (fbg, deleted 2026-10-14) so the decision it
was leading to is not lost. Everything else in that file landed: 5.0 (sunbird
`ccc1a6f26`, the PCH consumers get the PCH's include path), 5.1 PCH caching (`8522db9`),
5.2 manifest mode with the tracer and absent-deps variants (`a55fc57` and later), 5.3 the
CMake launcher form (`docs/configuration.md`, "Using it from CMake"), 5.4 gcc
`-fpch-preprocess` on the `-E` run (`BuildPreprocessCommand`). The preprocessor-hit
follow-up is vcache-cxx-manifest-pp-hit-state-6ft.

## Why

sunbird's C and C++ compiles still go through ccache (sunbird AGENTS.md: "a hit costs
~15 ms"); only rustc uses vcache. The file's section 6 said vcache is worth switching to
when all of the following hold, with both tools given the fixed include path:

1. case 2 (a worktree's warm build from a store another worktree filled) within 20% of
   ccache;
2. cases 4a (no-op rebuild) and 4b (one-file edit: 1 compile, 216 relinks) within 0.5 s
   of ccache, measured after a host-side `git status` (`buildinfo gather` otherwise runs
   `git status` against an index the container's read-only mount cannot rewrite);
3. case 3 (two worktrees cold at once) keeps its single-flight win;
4. no wrong hits, and the vcache-built tests pass.

## Historical measurements (superseded by the detailed 2026-10-14 notes below)

el10, clang 22, sunbird `ninja all all_tests` at `-j26` in a 30-CPU, 64 GiB slice, each
tool from an empty cache.

- Before the work (fbg `075bc68`): ccache warm 5.5 / 6.3 s; vcache 19.5 s (164 compiles
  could not preprocess; 80 to 100 ms per hit).
- After 5.0 and 5.1 (fbg `78e4a49`): vcache warm 10.5 s, 473 hits.
- After 5.2 (fbg `a55fc57`): vcache warm 8.6 s, 8.0 s on its second run, 6.9 s with the
  daemon; 473 manifest hits, 0 preprocessor runs; children CPU 27 s against ccache's 36 s
  for the whole build. ccache's warm runs: 5.3 to 7.8 s.
- Per hit on the host (`src/daemon/server.cc`): manifest hit 6.3 ms clang, 9.4 ms gcc;
  ccache 7 to 12 ms.
- Criterion 1 is met by the daemon run. Criteria 2 and 3 were not re-measured after
  5.2 (case 4a was 1.47 s against 0.46 s before the `git status` explanation; case 3
  was 49.6 s against ccache's 61 s before any of the work). Criterion 4 held at every
  measurement: 377 of 400 compared objects had identical `.text`, the other 23 differ
  only in `__FILE__` string lengths from ccache's `base_dir`.

## Remaining decision

The 2026-10-14 re-measurement in this bead's notes covers cases 2, 3, 4a and 4b and
reports the four criteria met, with the correctness qualifications listed there. It is
measurement evidence, not an owner decision or a globally enabled launcher switch.
The owner now decides whether to switch, stay, or defer. Repeat only cases invalidated
by a changed binary/toolchain/workload or a material evidence gap, using paired controls. A switch is a sunbird change (its `cmake/ccache.conf` and
launcher: `CMAKE_<LANG>_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=vcache`, plus `CMAKE_<LANG>_LINKER_LAUNCHER`
if links are to be cached), tracked in sunbird.

## Acceptance

The four case results stay recorded with their qualifications. Record the owner's decision:
switch with a sunbird rollout bead; stay on ccache with the reason/tradeoff; or explicitly defer
with the missing evidence/review point. Passing thresholds does not force a switch. No vcache
code change is expected.

## Current evidence and boundaries

The latest recorded round used vcache af2be77, sunbird 73a7f5993, clang 23.1.4. Warm cross-tree results were within 4% of ccache; no-op 0.12–0.13 s vs 0.12 s; one-file edit 6.35 s vs 6.09 s. Concurrent cold builds showed 5–16% wall improvement depending on CPU contention. Cold single-tree wall was 35.8 s vs 25.0 s, and warm vcache system CPU was 3–10 s higher. Retain the detailed raw measurements in notes.

Correctness evidence is qualified: 285/302 tests passed with the same 17 failures in plain builds; only 517 of 525 reported objects were compared, with explained debug/build-path and __FILE__ spelling differences. Before claiming complete correctness coverage, reconcile the eight unpaired objects or explicitly record why they are unavailable, and retain control failure names. Do not turn explained exclusions into a claim that the entire audit passed.

C/C++ compile migration and link-cache enablement are separate decisions. The link cache stays off during this decision unless explicitly evaluated under vcache-trk. No automatic rollout is implied by a measurement threshold, and a source edit that changes linked object bytes still requires relinking.

## Follow-up map and dependencies

- vcache-tsw: measure warm hit CPU before staging digest/memo optimizations.
- vcache-axb: evaluate the stale-manifest -E path for incremental edits.
- vcache-moz: cold-fill single compiler run, P3; keep stale-manifest preprocessing.
- vcache-zfn: trace emission transport, with crash/fallback correctness.
- vcache-trk: verification implementation, devtools switch, then timed host/el10 soak and owner decision.
- vcache-utm: document self-maps and the observed __FILE__ spelling effect.

These are related work, not blockers that must all finish before the compile migration decision. Preserve the owner's warm/incremental priority. Link verification does not depend on mmap tracing or the single-run optimization.

## Reproduction updates

Historical notes retain their original paths and limit values for provenance; they are not current instructions. New scratch/logs belong under /build/$USER/codex-1000/<task>/; inspect whether old scripts still exist and reconstruct the recipe from the recorded settings if not. All build/test/benchmark commands go through ~/bin/build-limited without copying or overriding caps; remove ccache/sccache PATH wrappers before compiler suites. Record current effective limits and actual job counts. Use isolated task-owned trees/stores per tool and attach sunbird worktrees to a beads session before br/commits. Do not reset production stores or discard existing source edits.

Record tool/binary revisions, commands, return codes, counter deltas, VCACHE_LOG diagnostics and object/test comparisons. A real no-op must show no compile/link work. Compare source edits in independent trees with matching contents; classify buildinfo/git-index noise explicitly. Measure at least three interleaved controls when rerunning a timing case. No vcache code, new regression suite or dist rebuild is needed merely to record this decision.

## Names

| Concept | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Compile launcher | CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER; CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER | Existing CMake language-specific knobs |
| Separate link launcher | CMAKE_C_LINKER_LAUNCHER; CMAKE_CXX_LINKER_LAUNCHER | Keeps link policy distinct from compilation |
| Site link policy | FBG_VCACHE_LINK | Shared with the link-verification epic |
| Historical task identity | vcache-232 | Bead IDs cannot be renamed |
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Retain the measured case tables and control failures; reconcile or explicitly explain the eight unpaired objects and any correctness exclusions.
- [ ] Record the owner's switch/stay/defer decision with rationale; switch links a sunbird implementation bead, defer names missing evidence or a review point.
- [ ] Keep compile migration separate from link-cache enablement; refresh only evidence invalidated by changed inputs or material gaps.
notes:
## Re-measurement 2026-10-14 (vcache af2be77 deployed binaries, sunbird 73a7f5993)

Setup: el10 container, clang 23.1.4 (sunbird moved from 22 since the last numbers), sunbird origin/main 73a7f5993,
`ninja -j26 all all_tests` (525 compiles, about 310 links), each container capped at 30 CPUs / 30 GiB
(`HS_BUILD_CPUS=30 HS_BUILD_MEMORY=30g`), launched through `~/bin/build-limited`. `build-limited --print-limits`
today: cpus=64, mem=88G, tasks=8192 (the earlier runs: a 30-CPU, 64 GiB slice shared by everything). So in case 3 the
two containers did not compete for CPU unless capped lower; a 15-CPU-per-container variant is added for that.
vcache: `dist/el10/vcache` + `vcache-fstrace.so` from af2be77 (the tracer fix for the el10 Rust segfault; 755846d
timings were never taken), masqueraded as the compiler (`CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=<build>/.masq/clang++-23` -> vcache,
`SUNBIRD_CCACHE=OFF`), environment from devtools `vcache-env.sh` (live devtools 59435e3): `VCACHE_CXX_MANIFEST=1`
(cxx-manifest key v7), `VCACHE_DAEMON=auto`, `VCACHE_DAEMON_SINGLE_FLIGHT=1`, `VCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=40G`, link cache off.
ccache: the image's /usr/bin/ccache with sunbird's `cmake/ccache.conf` (depend_mode, pch_external_checksum),
`CCACHE_BASEDIR=/code`. Both `SUNBIRD_TU_TIME=OFF`. Every case from an empty, separate scratch store.
Wall = ninja inside the container; CPU = ninja's children user / sys (the vcache daemon is outside that, 1-2 s).
Load average (1-min) before each run 6.3-9.8 (the host's idle floor is about 7); the host was busy between runs and
each run waited for 30 quiet seconds. Two rounds; round 2 interleaves the tools.

Include-path fix: `preprocess failed 0` in every vcache run (ccc1a6f26 holds; 164 failures before).

### Case 2: worktree B clean build from the store worktree A filled (warm)

| run | ccache wall | vcache wall | ccache CPU u/s | vcache CPU u/s | hits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| round 1 warm 1 | 13.20 s | 11.04 s | 14.4 / 17.0 s | 15.5 / 27.3 s | cc 525 direct; vc 525 manifest, 0 miss |
| round 1 warm 2 | 13.30 s | 12.12 s | 14.9 / 20.3 s | 16.6 / 27.4 s | same |
| round 2 warm 1 | 10.96 s | 11.34 s | 15.6 / 21.8 s | 15.7 / 25.1 s | same |
| round 2 warm 2 | 10.24 s | 10.63 s | 15.6 / 22.3 s | 15.4 / 25.4 s | same |
| round 2 warm 3 | 10.71 s | 10.68 s | 15.8 / 21.9 s | 15.4 / 25.3 s | same |

The A fill (cold, one tree): ccache 31.5 / 25.0 s (CPU 7m17+49s / 7m10+47s), vcache 49.7 / 35.8 s
(10m37+1m38s / 8m38+1m20s), plain clang 23.6 s (7m08+42s). vcache's cold build costs 20-45% more user CPU and
40% more wall than ccache's here; not a criterion, but it is what a first build pays.

### Case 3: both worktrees cold at once, one empty store

| variant | ccache A / B | vcache A / B | vcache dedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 CPUs per container (64-CPU slice) | 42.67 / 42.63 s | 40.42 / 40.42 s | 525 hits of 1050 lookups; 525 compiled once |
| 15 CPUs per container | 45.09 / 45.03 s | 38.02 / 37.79 s | same |

CPU per tree: ccache 8m21-8m49 user (1042 / 1036 misses: both trees compile everything), vcache 4m56-5m00 user.

### Case 4a: no-op in the warm tree B after a host-side `git status`

| run | ccache | vcache |
|---|---|---|
| round 2, noop 1 / 2 | 0.12 / 0.12 s (4 edges) | 0.12 / 0.13 s (4 edges) |
| round 1, noop 1 / 2 | 0.17 / 0.12 s | 5.29 / 5.13 s (1 compile, a manifest hit, + 176 links) |

Round 1's vcache no-ops were not no-ops: each rebuilt one TU (served from the cache) and relinked 176 binaries. The
same thing hit ccache's round-1 edit 2 (an extra direct hit + 177 links). It is the buildinfo / git-index effect the
criterion already names, made worse here because both tools' build dirs share one worktree and the ccache edit
step rewrote a source file the vcache tree also builds; it did not recur in round 2 nor in a separate warm+no-op
check. Round 2 is the clean measurement. (A round-2 vcache "noop 3" that rebuilt 1 TU was caused by the ccache
edit step touching the shared source, shown by mtimes; excluded.)

### Case 4b: one-file edit in tree B (core/transport/TcpOrUdsSocket.cc, a static_assert line: 1 compile, 134 links)

| run | ccache | vcache |
|---|---|---|
| round 1 edit 1 / 2 | 5.64 / (6.10, +1 buildinfo compile) s | 5.75 / 5.65 s |
| round 2 edit 1 | 6.09 s | 6.35 s |

### Correctness

- Wrong hits: none. Tree B's vcache objects (all 525 served from A's entries) against a plain clang build of the same
  commit: 517 objects, 513 identical in every non-debug section, 327 identical as whole files (the rest differ only
  in debug info, which names the build dir). The 4 that differ do so only in `.rodata.str1.1`: 2 tests embed the
  build dir name (build-el10vc vs build-el10plain, an artefact of this setup), and 2 treelite TUs whose `__FILE__`
  reads `model_loader/detail/lightgbm.h` instead of `model_loader/./detail/lightgbm.h`. That comes from the
  `-ffile-prefix-map=/code/sunbird_strategy=/code/sunbird_strategy` vcache adds to every compile: a plain compile
  with that flag gives the same string. Same bytes on a hit and on a miss through vcache, so not a wrong hit, but
  vcache-built objects are not byte-identical to plain ones where a path holds `./`.
- Tests: `ctest -LE heavy -j16` in the vcache-built tree B: 285 of 302 pass; the same 17 fail in the plain-built tree
  (python research deps missing in el10, and a host-built Rust example), so no vcache-caused failure.
  (`run_tests.sh --no-build` stops earlier on its own test_test_skip.py failures, unrelated.)

### Criteria

1. Case 2 within 20% of ccache: **met**. Round 2: vcache 11.34 / 10.63 / 10.68 s vs ccache 10.96 / 10.24 / 10.71 s
   (+3.5%, +3.8%, -0.3%); round 1 vcache was faster (11.0 / 12.1 vs 13.2 / 13.3 s). vcache uses 3-10 s more system CPU.
2. Cases 4a and 4b within 0.5 s of ccache: **met**. 4a: 0.12-0.13 s vs 0.12 s (round 2). 4b: 6.35 vs 6.09 s
   (+0.26 s) in round 2, 5.75 / 5.65 vs 5.64 s in round 1.
3. Case 3 keeps its single-flight win: **met, smaller than before**. 40.4 vs 42.7 s (-5%) with 30 CPUs per container
   in today's 64-CPU slice; 37.9 vs 45.1 s (-16%) at 15 CPUs per container, closer to the old shared 30-CPU slice
   (earlier 49.6 vs 61 s, -19%). vcache needs ~40% less CPU per tree there.
4. No wrong hits and the vcache-built tests pass: **met** (see Correctness; note the `./` `__FILE__` difference).

All four criteria hold. The cost not covered by them: a cold single-tree build is about 40% slower in wall time
(35.8 vs 25.0 s) and the warm build spends 3-10 s more system CPU.

### How to rerun

Scripts in /build/$USER/claude-tmp/claude-1000/m232/ (`m232.sh`, `run-main.sh`, `run-round2.sh`, `cmpobj.py`,
`results.log` with every RESULT/CPU/STATS line); requested for pruning after this note, so copy them first.
- Worktrees: `git worktree add --detach /build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/sunbird/m232-{a,b} origin/main`.
- Host env: `FBG_DEVTOOLS_ROOT=$HOME/fbg/devtools HS_BUILD_CPUS=30 HS_BUILD_MEMORY=30g`, one build dir per tool
  (`BUILD_DIR=build-el10cc|build-el10vc|build-el10plain`), stores via `CCACHE_DIR=<scratch>/<store>` (ccache) or
  `SUNBIRD_VCACHE_CACHE_ROOT=<scratch>/<store>` (vcache; `VCACHE_DIR` becomes `<store>/el10`).
- vcache build dir: `mkdir -p <build-el10vc>/.masq && ln -s /code/vcache/dist/el10/vcache <build-el10vc>/.masq/clang++-23`,
  then `~/bin/build-limited ./container.run.sh -q el10 -- ./build.sh --with-tests -DSUNBIRD_TU_TIME=OFF
  -DSUNBIRD_CCACHE=OFF -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/code/sunbird_strategy/build-el10vc/.masq/clang++-23`;
  ccache: same with only `-DSUNBIRD_TU_TIME=OFF`.
- Timed run, inside `container.run.sh -q el10 -- bash -c ...`: ccache `export CCACHE_CONFIGPATH=/code/sunbird_strategy/cmake/ccache.conf
  CCACHE_BASEDIR=/code`; vcache `source /code/sunbird_strategy/scripts/vcache-env.sh && exportSunbirdVcacheEnv
  /code/sunbird_strategy "$SUNBIRD_HOST_REPO_ROOT"`; then `cd $BUILD_DIR && ninja -t clean && <zero stats> &&
  ninja -j26 all all_tests`, stats from `ccache --print-stats` / `/code/vcache/dist/el10/vcache --show-stats`.
- Case 3 releases both containers together through a gate file in the shared store; 4a/4b run `git status` on the
  host first; 4b appends a `static_assert(true, "...")` line and restores the file afterwards.
2026-10-15: vcache-tsw completed compile-only hit attribution (docs/cxx-hit-cost.md). Canonical EL10 B-from-A replay hits 520/520 for both tools. Noncanonical host layout has generated PCH wrapper paths: only 32/522 first-pass manifest hits for vcache (496 total result hits); ccache 0/522. Fully warm replay still shows extra vcache system CPU; shared digest table and lazy scratch follow-ups are vcache-83w and vcache-zs1. No rollout/default decision made.

comments.text: Follow-ups staged 2026-10-15 from the measurement: vcache-moz (one compiler run on a cold-fill miss; closes the cold-fill gap), vcache-zfn (mmap'd tracer log; the miss-path system CPU), vcache-trk (link verify mode and soak; the only lever that beats ccache on the warm build, which is link-bound), vcache-utm (doc the prefix-map ./ effect). A memo-table change for the hit path's system CPU is not staged: the measurement did not attribute that time, so it needs a strace -c of a warm hit first.

comments.author: richard
comments.text: Owner priority 2026-10-15: warm incremental build time over cold build time. Of the follow-ups, the preprocessor evaluation (the -E run on a stale manifest after a header edit) and the hit-path system CPU are the incremental levers; vcache-moz (cold fill) is P3. The one-file edit case (6 s, 1 compile + 134 links) is link-bound on sunbird's side, which no cache can shorten.

title: fstrace: record every traced path as absolute, resolved against the process cwd
description:
# vcache tracer: absolute paths in every record (bead vcache-6h7), version 8

vcache `fbg` at `a489230`; sunbird `origin/main` at `5689732cf`; devtools `origin/main` at `5311975`.

## 0. Owner decisions

- **D1.** The tracer resolves relative paths at emit time, so every R, M, W, D record is absolute. The format and
  kinds are unchanged, because `ReadTraceRecords` refuses an unknown kind.
- **D2.** No pid and no `C <cwd>` record: the whole tree appends to one log, so such a record cannot be attributed.
- **D3.** The cwd is the physical one (`SYS_getcwd`), as the readers' `util::CurrentDir()` is, so keys of a process
  that keeps its cwd stay byte-identical. `PWD` is rejected: it goes stale after `chdir`, `-C` and
  `Popen(cwd=)`, and `fchdir` has no spelling for it.
- **D4.** No cwd cache and no `chdir` interposition; each relative record costs one `SYS_getcwd`, because glibc
  changes the cwd off the PLT. Now: `cwd_prefix()` (`0aef3ef`) does this, but `emit()` does not call it yet.
- **D5.** New readers (`ReadTraceRecords`, sunbird's audit) treat a relative record as an incomplete trace, so an old
  tracer only costs caching. Now: sunbird refuses `!`, malformed lines and unknown kinds (`b8ff67fc4`), but not
  relative records.
- **D6.** A clang `-working-directory` compile (`SetsWorkingDirectory`) records no C/C++ manifest state. The
  preprocessed key still serves it.
- **Q2/D7.** The change bumps `kCxxManifestKeyVersion` and `kLinkKeyVersion` and names them in the commit body. Moot
  part: `db52038` already took v5 and v2, so this change takes `vcache-cxx-manifest-v7` and `vcache-link-v4` (the upstream sync 9495f3d took v6 and v3).

## 1. Why

Readers prefix their own cwd to a relative record, which is wrong once a process changes directory. For
`sh -c 'cd x && cat rel; stat rel; test -e nope'` the deployed tracer (built from `31a24a5`) writes `R\trel`,
`R\t.` and `M\tnope`.

## 2. State at `a489230`

- `src/trace/fstrace.c`:
  - `log_path()` refuses a relative `VCACHE_TRACE_LOG`.
  - `mark_incomplete()` creates `<log>.incomplete`, or falls back to `write_incomplete_sentinel()` (`\n!\n`).
  - `at_path_begin()` names a dirfd before the call; an `AT_FDCWD` relative path reaches `emit()` unchanged.
  - `announce_object()` already uses `cwd_prefix()` and `append_path()`. There is no `chroot` wrapper.
- `src/core/link_trace.cc`: `ReadTraceRecords(log_path, cwd, out)` prefixes `cwd` to relative records.
  `ParseTraceLog(..., cwd, ...)` also uses `cwd` to resolve relative `outputs`.

## 3. Steps and remaining contracts

Step 5 (a relative log refused by the log and the marker) was done in `05b86e0`. Everything else is to do.

- **Steps 1 to 3, `emit(kind, path)`.**
  - When `path[0] != '/'`, write `cwd_prefix()` after the kind and the tab.
  - If it returns 0 (removed cwd, `(unreachable)`, `ERANGE`), call `mark_incomplete()` and return.
  - The tab, newline and length checks cover the whole record, cwd included.
  - The `AT_FDCWD` branch needs no further change.
- **Step 4, `chroot(path)`** (new). With no `log_path()`, call through. Otherwise:
  - Before the call, open the log's directory with `O_PATH | O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`.
  - If `r == 0`, create `<log basename>.incomplete` through that descriptor. If that fails, call
    `write_incomplete_sentinel()`, as `mark_incomplete()` does.
  - Close the descriptor, restore `errno`, and never remove a marker.
- **Step 6, `ReadTraceRecords(log_path, out)`.**
  - Drop `cwd`; a path not starting with `/` returns false.
  - `ParseTraceLog` keeps `cwd`, now only for `outputs`. v5 said it would drop it, which is wrong.
  - `ReadCxxManifestTrace` stops passing `cwd` to it.
  - Update both header comments.
- **Step 8, `RunCompile`.**
  - Before any trace, list or depfile read, `SetsWorkingDirectory(parsed)` sets `manifest_inputs.declined = "the
    compiler changes its working directory"`.
  - The log line becomes `cxx manifest: not recording: the compiler changes its working directory`.
  - Under `derive_key` this stays uncached.
- **D7.** Set `vcache-cxx-manifest-v6` (`compile.cc`) and `vcache-link-v3` (`link.cc`).
- **Step 7, `docs/design.md`.**
  - Known limitations: records are absolute against the physical cwd, and a relative record (an older tracer) is
    refused.
  - Manifest section: list a relative record among the unusable-trace reasons, and replace "`-working-directory` …
    records from the depfile alone" with "records no state".
- **devtools.** `installVcacheTracer` gains `keepPreviousBinary "${binary%/*}/vcache-fstrace.so"`.
- **Commit.** `fix(trace):` with the bumps named, one `Fails first:` line per test, ending `Deploy: vcache`.

## 4. Consequences

### 4.1 and 4.2 Keys and completeness

D7 flushes entries keyed on a mis-attributed path, and the old reader's `//x` for a process in `/`. Headers and
`VCACHE_ROOTS` are unchanged. `testSuntraderStateFile` stays a separate investigation.

### 4.3 sunbird consumer

Done in `b8ff67fc4`:

- refusal of `!`, tab-less lines and unknown kinds;
- trust rules for reads outside the roots, foreign programs and the absent-path cap, with exit 2.

To do: relative records, byte fidelity, and list generation. `plan_reason` and `cmd_plan` still check `is_file()`.

The three steps stay. Under the new tracer, `test_audit_notes_relative_reads_after_a_directory_change` reads an
absolute path under the scratch root (a drop root), so its "do not resolve" note assertion fails.

- **Prep (before the deploy).** Replace that test with `test_audit_records_a_read_after_a_directory_change`.
  - The script runs `cd {self.repo}/sub && cat note.txt`.
  - It expects the list `[repo/sub/note.txt]` and `unchanged`.
  - It skips with "tracer emits relative records" when a traced `sh -c 'cd d && cat f'` writes `R\tf`.
  - Fails first: with the skip removed, the `a489230` tracer gives `[]`.
- **Strict (after the deploy).**
  - Relative records: `audit_entry` marks the trace incomplete on any path not starting with `/`. Drop
    `relative_paths`, `unresolved_paths` and their note; `resolve_traced_path` keeps only its `..` rule.
  - Bytes: split the trace with `read_bytes().split(b"\n")` and skip empty lines. Decode with `os.fsdecode`. Lists
    and the `FileHasher` cache use `surrogateescape` and `\n`. `get_inputs_sha` and `get_listing_sha` hash the bytes.
  - Generation: the first line of a list is `# tracer absolute-paths`. Without it `read_input_list` returns None.
    `plan_reason` and `cmd_plan`'s `waiting_on_audit` use that result, and the test helpers write the header.
  - Remove the skip.
  - Tests (fails first on today's script):
    - a fake-tracer relative record waits on an audit (today it is kept);
    - an unversioned list plans `not-audited` (today `unchanged`);
    - names `a\rb.txt` and one with byte `\xe9` stay inputs (today the trace is incomplete or the input "changed").

### 4.4 Deploy and rollback

Order:

1. Land the sunbird prep commit.
2. Land vcache and devtools.
3. Run `host-setup-buildcache.sh --force`; all three `dist/` trees ship together, keeping `.prev`.
4. Land the sunbird strict change.
5. Re-audit the host and el10.

Rollback:

- **Tracer only, or partial:** relative records are refused; caching is lost, ids go `not-audited`, nothing is
  mis-keyed.
- **All of vcache:** the v5 and v2 namespaces are intact.
- **sunbird strict change:** delete `.teststamps/*.inputs` and `*.hashes`, then re-audit.

### 4.5 Tests

In `tests/integration_test.sh` after the `tracer-stat` block unless stated. `P` is the fixture directory's
`pwd -P`, and "today" means the tracer at `a489230`.

1. **`tracer-cwd`** (new). `sh -c 'cd x && cat rel'` gives one `R\tP/x/rel`. Today it writes `R\trel` (probed).
2. **`tracer-cwd/chdir.c`** (new). The program runs `chdir("a")`, `open("rel")`, `chdir("../b")`, `open("rel")`,
   `fchdir` back to `a`, then `stat("rel")`. Expect two `R\tP/a/rel` and one `R\tP/b/rel`; today both counts are 0.

title: filehash: replace per-input memo files with a shared digest table
description:
Implement the leading optimization identified by vcache-tsw (docs/cxx-hit-cost.md). The host median TU makes 1,685 memo-file syscalls out of 2,986 total; EL10 makes 1,690 out of 3,226. A warm memo read uses open, fstat, two reads, close, in addition to the input identity stat. The measured host median costs 4.96 ms system CPU versus ccache 2.11 ms. A 1–3 ms system-CPU saving is a screening estimate, not a promised improvement.

Keep HashFileMemoized's public contract. Design a bounded shared mapped digest table keyed by the existing complete FileIdentity, retaining content digests, before/after identity checks and the unsettled-file window. Stat identity is an optimization premise, not permission to skip correctness validation. Do not combine this with daemon-side manifest validation or removal of absent probes. Keep the file-memo fallback or another safe rehash fallback for unsupported filesystems, mapping/permission errors, full tables, stale versions and corruption. Explicitly specify cross-process publication, crash recovery, concurrent resize/eviction and mapping lifetime before coding; incomplete entries must never become hits. Measure memory and contention as well as syscall savings.

Use the existing hash/file_memo family and names; version the new memo storage independently. Decide and document whether any cache-key namespace changes; a pure memo representation change should preserve the semantic key only after equivalence tests. Existing file memos must remain harmless across upgrades. No cleanup of unrelated stores is authorized.

Baseline commands, configurations, binaries and logs: /build/richard/codex-1000/cxx-hit-attribution-20261015. Reuse the guarded compile-only replay with fresh output artifact names, running daemon verified and isolated stores. Measure host and EL10; links and setup stay out of warm timings.

Validation and landing: use ~/bin/build-limited for every build/test/benchmark; strip ccache/sccache PATH directories for compiler suites. New scratch goes under /build/$USER/codex-1000 and worktrees under /build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/vcache. Preserve existing work. Demonstrate regression assertions failing on pre-fix code or a targeted mutation, record Fails first lines, run make test, and rebuild deployed binaries when landing a binary change. Read AGENTS.md before implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Document and implement bounded table layout, cross-process publication and crash/corruption fallback without weakening input identity or content checks.
- [x] Failing-first tests cover concurrent readers/writers, truncated or partial entries, stale versions, full table, file replacement, same-size/restored-mtime edits and unsettled writes; no stale artifact is served.
- [x] Counter-verified replay preserves result bytes and hit/miss outcomes; syscall traces show fewer memo-file calls.
- [x] Three interleaved aggregate runs and 20 repeats for small/median/PCH hits compare wall/user/sys, daemon CPU, spread and memory on host and EL10; report actual improvement or reject the design.
- [x] Full gate passes; commit key-version decision and Deploy: vcache, then rebuild deployed binaries.
notes:
Implemented a fixed 3 MiB shared digest table with immutable release/acquire publication, complete identity and checksum validation, and legacy fallback. Protocol and measured tradeoffs: docs/file-digest-table.md. Baseline 76103ca and seven targeted mutations fail the regression assertions. Guarded host/EL10 replays preserve all 522/520 manifest hits and output hashes; median-TU memo calls fall 1685/1690 to 8, aggregate median client system CPU falls 16.5%/27.7%. Full samples and logs: /build/richard/codex-1000/vcache-83w. Development binary/tracer regression passes after the baseline fails table creation. New origin/fbg tracer and build changes are merged; final combined gate and deployment are in progress.
Completed and deployed at d460a2e147d9f20beabd6590c4b622ef957dcebe, Anvil artifact vcache 1.5 for fedora44/el10/ubuntu24/amzn2023/dc-build. Host/el10/dc-build dist stamps and binary/tracer hashes match the published artifacts; installed regressions pass in all three environments. Final gate: 1500 unit, 1341 integration, 93 link verification, 93 Anvil checks and ancillary suites pass. Latest user changes are included. Publication exposed and fixed older-glibc tracer linkage in vcache-zei; daemon timing failures remain separately tracked in vcache-rpf. Link verification soak remains enabled. Logs: gate-tracer-link.log, publish-final.log, deploy-final.log and installed-final-*.log under /build/richard/codex-1000/vcache-83w.
close_reason: Shared digest table implemented, measured, tested, deployed and published.

title: C/C++ hit with -MD finds an entry stored without -MD and writes no depfile
description:
Dependency flags are deliberately left out of the C/C++ cache key so a compile with and without -MD share one entry. But when the entry was stored by a compile without -MD, the blob has no depfile; a later hit from a compile with -MD -MF x.d then writes no x.d and still counts as a hit (MaterializeHit skips the depfile when blob.has_depfile is false and returns true). ninja/make then see no dependency list for that object, so header edits do not rebuild it.

Repro (host, primary bin/vcache): in an empty VCACHE_DIR, `vcache gcc -c t.c -o t.o`, then `vcache gcc -MD -MF t.d -c t.c -o t.o`: t.d does not exist, stats show a hit.

Fix options: treat a hit whose blob lacks a depfile the compile needs as a miss (compile, then store the blob with the depfile so both shapes are served from then on), or carry generates_deps into the key. The first keeps sharing and is a two-line change plus a fails-first integration check.
close_reason: fixed on fbg: a -MD compile recompiles when the shared entry has no depfile

title: tests: separate durable Put latency from lease timing assertions
description: Real disk-backed gates have failed lease tests because PutLeaseBlob uses a 500 ms receive timeout while durable cache writes can take longer. Retained syscall evidence: /build/richard/codex-1000/vcache-83w/daemon-trace.2768944 has a 1.085643 s blob fsync; /build/richard/codex-1000/daemon-lock-errors-20261018/unit-trace.2443138 has 0.528453 s followed by rename and EPIPE after the client deadline. The latter run still passed the stored waiter outcome assertions, identifying a test timing limit rather than a wrong cache result. Preserve durable cache writes. Design deterministic synchronization that separates lease expiration/wakeup assertions from completion of durable storage; keep meaningful protocol/deadlock bounds and show failing-first coverage. Do not simply widen every timeout, retry gates until green, or report tmpfs-only results as disk-backed success. This is independent of the PID-file startup flush addressed by vcache-rpf. Read the retained logs and current tests before implementation; run all builds/tests through build-limited with scratch under /build/$USER/codex-1000.

title: rustc identity memo is keyed on path and size only; a same-size relink reuses the old banner
description:
ResolveRustcFingerprint keys rustc-version-memo-v1 on realpath + size. ResolveCompilerId (C++) adds mtime and its comment explains why: relinking a compiler after a source change routinely lands on the same byte count. Add mtime, bump the memo name to v2. Fails first: a unit test that rewrites the fake rustc with same-size different bytes and a newer mtime and expects a new fingerprint.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified facts: `ResolveRustcFingerprint` (src/rust/rust_compile.cc, anonymous namespace) builds the memo key from `"rustc-version-memo-v1"`, `RealPath(rustc)` and `FileSize(real)` only, then reads `<cache>/compilers/<hex>` if present. `ResolveCompilerId` (src/core/compile.cc) uses `"compiler-version-memo-v2"`, path, size **and** `info.mtime`, with the comment explaining why.

| Behaviour | Before | After | Keep? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same rustc binary, unchanged | memo hit, no `rustc -vV` spawn | memo hit, no spawn | keep: the memo exists to avoid a spawn per crate |
| rustc replaced in place, same size, newer mtime | old banner reused forever, keys collide with the old toolchain's | new memo key, `-vV` re-run, new fingerprint | change (the defect) |
| rustc replaced, different size | new memo | new memo | keep |
| Memo file from v1 present after upgrade | used | ignored (key name changed to `rustc-version-memo-v2`); one extra `-vV` per toolchain, then memoised | change, harmless; old v1 files stay as dead files until `--clear` |
| What travels in the cache key | hash of the banner text | unchanged (mtime is only in the local memo key, never in the cache key) | keep: keys must stay machine-independent so S3 entries share |

Cost: one extra `stat` field already returned by the same `stat` call; zero extra syscalls.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| `rustc` is a rustup proxy symlink | `RealPath` resolves it first (unchanged); mtime of the resolved file |
| mtime unreadable (stat fails) | same as today when size is unreadable: use 0 and carry on, never fail the compile |
| Two toolchains at different paths, same size and mtime | different memo keys via the path (unchanged) |
| Clock set backwards so the new binary's mtime is older | still a different mtime value, so a different key; the rule is "differs", not "newer" |

Naming: memo key prefix becomes `rustc-version-memo-v2`, mirroring `compiler-version-memo-v2`. No other new names.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Integration test, new section `9e. Rust: a rustc rebuilt in place is a new toolchain` in tests/integration_test.sh, skipped when `rustc` is absent:
1. Write two fake rustc scripts of byte-identical length under `$WORK/rustc-swap/`: each is `#!/bin/sh` plus a branch that, when `$1` is `-vV`, prints the real `rustc -vV` output with the `release:` line replaced by `release: 9.9.1` (script A) or `release: 9.9.2` (script B); every other invocation `exec`s the real rustc with `"$@"`. Assert `wc -c` of A equals B.
2. Install A as `$WORK/rustc-swap/bin/rustc`; compile the existing `demo` crate through `"$VCACHE" $WORK/rustc-swap/bin/rustc ...` (same flags as section 9). Expect `misses` = 1.
3. Compile again: `hits` = 1 (memo and entry both reused).
4. Copy B over the same path (`cp`, which keeps the size), then `touch -d '+2 seconds'` it so the mtime differs even on coarse filesystems. Compile again: expect `misses` = 2, and `VCACHE_LOG` shows a `rust key` different from step 2's.
Before the fix step 4 shows `hits` = 2 (the stale banner); that is the fail-first evidence.

- M1 drop `UpdateU64(mtime)` from the memo key: step 4 hits (fails "a rebuilt rustc misses").
- M2 keep mtime but leave the prefix at `-v1`: the test still passes (old v1 files are per-cache, the test uses a fresh cache) — report as "not caught, by design" with that reason.
- M3 put the mtime into the cache key instead of the memo key: an existing unit/integration check that two checkouts share Rust entries must fail (section 9 "second rust checkout hits" if the scripts are copied with different mtimes; if nothing fails, add that assertion and report it).

title: util::ReadFile reads through istreambuf_iterator: 28% of vcache CPU on a warm build
description:
perf on a warm 357-crate build: ReadFile 28%, BLAKE3 17%, memmove 9% of vcache's own CPU, which is 82% of all CPU in that build; the 550 MB asupersync entry takes 1.7 s to serve. Replace with fstat + a single read into a presized string (or mmap for blobs above a threshold) and remove the extra copies in DeserializeBlob/RestoreOutputs where a string_view suffices. Fails first: none applicable (no behaviour change); record the before/after warm wall time and perf share in the commit body instead.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): behaviour diff

Verified: `util::ReadFile` (src/util/fs.cc) builds a `std::string` from `std::istreambuf_iterator<char>`, byte by byte with reallocations. `DeserializeBlob` (src/storage/chain.cc) then copies the body (`data.substr(pos, body_len)`), BLAKE3-hashes it to check the stored digest, and copies each section payload (`body.substr(bpos, len)`). RestoreOutputs (src/rust/rust_compile.cc) copies each file's contents once more (`std::string contents = file.contents;`) before writing. Measured on a warm 357-crate build: vcache is 82% of all CPU; inside vcache `ReadFile` 28%, BLAKE3 17%, memmove 9%; the 550 MB asupersync entry takes 1.7 s to serve.

| Behaviour | Before | After | Keep? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bytes read for a file | all of it | all of it | keep |
| Missing / unreadable file | `nullopt` | `nullopt` | keep exactly; callers branch on it |
| File that grows or shrinks while read | whatever istreambuf saw | read until EOF after the `fstat` size (loop on short reads, stop at 0); a file that shrank returns the shorter content | keep semantics: return what is there, never pad |
| Blob checksum verification on every Get | yes (BLAKE3 of body) | **yes, unchanged** | keep: it is the integrity check; removing it is out of scope and forbidden |
| Copies of a blob body on a hit | read + body substr + per-section substr + restore copy (4) | read once into a sized buffer; sections parsed as `std::string_view` into the body; contents moved, not copied, into BlobFile; RestoreOutputs writes from a `const std::string&` | change |
| Public signatures | `std::optional<std::string> ReadFile(const std::string&)` | unchanged | keep (many callers) |

New failure modes: none allowed. A `read` that returns EINTR is retried; any other error returns `nullopt` as today.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| 0-byte file | returns an empty string (not nullopt) |
| /proc-style file whose `st_size` is 0 but has content (`/proc/meminfo`) | returns the content: when `st_size` is 0, fall back to a read loop with a growing buffer |
| FIFO or other non-regular file | same as today (read to EOF) |
| 550 MB blob | one allocation of the final size |
| Truncated blob / bad digest | `DeserializeBlob` false exactly as today |

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): tests, measurement, mutations

Unit tests (Section `util::ReadFile`, new): empty file -> `""`; 3-byte file -> exact bytes; a 64 MiB file of a repeating pattern -> exact size and BLAKE3 equal to `hash::HashFile`; missing path -> nullopt; `/proc/self/status` -> non-empty and starts with `Name:`. Unit (Section `storage::blob`, extend): a blob with two files round-trips byte-exact; flipping one body byte makes `DeserializeBlob` return false.

Measurement in the commit body (not a test): warm build of a cargo workspace through `bin/vcache`, before and after, using the method in the epic (fresh target dir, warm store), wall time and `perf report --comm vcache --sort symbol` top 5. If you cannot run perf, say so; do not invent numbers.

Mutations to report:
- M1 return the content without the final short-read loop (read exactly `st_size` once): the `/proc/self/status` test fails.
- M2 drop the BLAKE3 check in `DeserializeBlob`: the flipped-byte test fails.
- M3 return nullopt for a 0-byte file: the empty-file test fails.
- M4 parse sections with an off-by-one length: the two-file round-trip fails.
- M5 skip `EINTR` retry: report "not caught, by design" (cannot be triggered deterministically) with that reason.

title: Queued S3 upload is skipped when the disk layer evicts the entry first
description:
UploadWorker re-reads the blob from disk; if DiskStorage::Put's inline LRU eviction removed it, the upload is counted as uploads_skipped and lost. Under cache pressure the newest entries are evicted first, so S3 silently loses exactly the latest work. Fix: the evictor skips keys with a pending/<key> journal marker (the journal is already the pin list). Fails first: an integration test with a tiny disk size and a mock S3 showing uploads_skipped stays 0.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified: eviction is `DiskStorage::TrimGlobal` (src/storage/disk_storage.cc), called from `DiskStorage::Put` when the cache passes its budget and from `Trim()`. It runs in **every** process that writes the disk layer (each compile without a daemon, and the daemon's `HandlePut`), so a pin must be a filesystem fact, not daemon memory. The daemon's journal is an empty file `<cache dir>/daemon/pending/<key>` (`Server::JournalPath`, `StateDir` = `AbsoluteLexical(disk.dir) + "/daemon"`), created by `Enqueue` when the blob is on disk and removed in `FinishUpload`. `UploadWorker` re-reads the blob from disk at its turn; if eviction removed it, `uploads_skipped++` and the upload is lost.

State of one entry with an S3 layer and a daemon:

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| on disk, journalled | trim selects it | **stays** (skipped, pinned) | VCACHE_LOG `disk: kept <n> entries pending upload` once per trim |
| on disk, journalled | upload done or failed for good | on disk, not journalled | journal file removed (unchanged) |
| on disk, not journalled | trim selects it | evicted (unchanged) | |
| journalled, blob gone (removed outside vcache) | worker turn | skipped (unchanged, counted) | |

Invariant: an entry with a `pending/<key>` file is never removed by TrimGlobal. Bound: pinned bytes can exceed the budget transiently; a trim that cannot reach its target because of pins stops at the pins and logs how many bytes stayed pinned.

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Trim with no daemon dir | evict by LRU | identical (one failed `stat` per candidate only when a `daemon/pending` dir exists: check it once per trim) |
| Trim with pending entries | may evict them | skips them |
| `.linkout` sidecars and other non-key files in shards | evicted by LRU | unchanged (their names are not keys; never pinned) |
| `--clear` | removes everything | unchanged: an explicit clear is the user's call |

Cost: one `stat` of `<dir>/daemon/pending` per trim; when it exists, one `access()` per eviction candidate actually removed.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Entry path `<dir>/ab/cdef...` | key = `ab` + `cdef...`; pinned when `<dir>/daemon/pending/abcdef...` exists |
| A pending file for a key whose entry is already gone | ignored |
| Everything pinned | trim removes nothing, logs the pinned count, returns; `Put` still succeeds |
| Read-only cache | no trim (unchanged) |
| Two trimmers at once | unchanged ENOENT accounting; pinned entries counted as kept by both |

Naming: helper `bool DiskStorage::IsPendingUpload(const std::string& entry_path) const`; log marker `disk: kept <n> entries pending upload (<bytes> bytes)`.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `storage::disk trim`): a DiskStorage with max_size 10 KiB; Put keys k1..k4 of 4 KiB each with lru times oldest k1; create `<dir>/daemon/pending/<k1>`; Put k5 (triggers trim): k1 still present, k2 removed, the total is at or below the high water except for pinned bytes. Without the pending file the same sequence removes k1 (control).
Integration (section `11. Daemon uploads survive eviction`, uses tests/mock_s3.py like the existing S3 sections): daemon on, `VCACHE_CACHE_SIZE` small enough that five compiles overflow it, mock S3 with `MOCK_S3_LATENCY_MS=300` so uploads lag behind stores; after the compiles, `vcache --stop-daemon`; `--daemon-status` taken before stop shows `skipped 0`, and the mock bucket holds all five keys.

Mutations:
- M1 ignore the pending file: unit pinned case fails (k1 evicted).
- M2 derive the key from the file name only (drop the shard prefix): unit fails.
- M3 pin every entry when the pending dir exists: the control part of the unit test (k2 removed) fails.
- M4 skip the pinned check only in the ENOENT branch: report whether caught.
- M5 make an all-pinned trim loop forever: the "everything pinned" unit case must time out the test harness; add an explicit bounded check so it fails, not hangs.
close_reason: 25296ca: trim leaves an entry alone while its upload is pending

title: Server::Enqueue dedupes by key, so a manifest re-Put is absorbed by an in-flight upload of the old value
description:
queued_keys_ makes a second Put of the same key a no-op while the first upload is pending; manifests are mutable, so the newer states never reach S3. Fix: generation-aware enqueue (requeue when the value changed) or re-read the disk value at upload time and loop while it changed. Fails first: a unit test that two Puts of one key with different values end with the second value uploaded.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified: `Server::Enqueue` returns true immediately when `queued_keys_` holds the key. `queued_keys_` keeps a key from `Enqueue` until `FinishUpload`, which also covers the time the worker has dequeued the item and is uploading it outside the lock. `UploadWorker` re-reads the disk value at its turn (disk case) or uploads `item.blob` (held case). So a second `Put` of the same key while the first is queued or uploading is absorbed: in the disk case the worker may already have read the old bytes; in the held case `held_` keeps the old blob. Manifests (Rust and dep-scan) are rewritten under one key, so S3 keeps a stale manifest. `FinishUpload` also removes the journal file, so a re-Put's journal is lost.

New state per key: `upload_generation_[key]` (uint64), bumped by every Enqueue of the key; `Upload` carries the generation it was queued or last re-read at.

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| not queued | Enqueue(k) | queued gen=1, journal file created (disk case) | |
| queued gen=g (not yet dequeued) | Enqueue(k) again | queued gen=g+1; held case: held_[k] replaced (held_bytes_ adjusted, capacity check applies to the new size); still one queue entry | |
| in flight at gen=g | Enqueue(k) again | gen=g+1, journal file kept/created | |
| in flight at gen=g, upload done | gen still g | not queued; queued_keys_ erased; journal removed (unchanged) | uploads_done++ |
| in flight at gen=g, upload done | gen now g+1 | **re-queued** with gen=g+1 at the back (disk case re-reads disk; held case uploads held_[k]); journal kept | uploads_done++ (the first upload did happen), VCACHE_LOG `daemon: re-queued <key> (rewritten during upload)` |
| in flight, failed for good | gen changed meanwhile | re-queued as above (the newer value deserves its own attempts) | uploads_failed++ |
| daemon restart | | journal recovery as today; generations start at 1 | |

Invariant: after the last Put of key k returns, the value S3 ends with is that Put's value (or the key is counted failed/skipped), never an earlier one.

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single Put per key (the common case: immutable entries) | one upload | one upload, no extra work |
| Re-Put during queue (held case) | old blob uploaded, new lost | new blob uploaded once |
| Re-Put during upload | new value never uploaded | uploaded after the first finishes |
| held_bytes_ accounting | per first blob | adjusted on replace; never negative |

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Ten re-Puts of one manifest while one upload is in flight | at most one extra upload after it, carrying the last value |
| Re-Put whose new held blob would exceed kMaxHeldBytes | Enqueue returns false as today (HandlePut then uploads synchronously); the old queued item still uploads the old value, then the generation check re-queues nothing because the synchronous upload already wrote the newest; make sure the generation is not bumped when Enqueue returns false |
| Shutdown with a re-queued item | drained like any queued item |

Naming: `upload_generation_`, `Upload::generation`. Log marker above.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `daemon::upload generation`; drive `Server`'s queue functions through a test seam or extract the queue into a small class `UploadQueue` in src/daemon/ with Enqueue/Dequeue/Finish and unit-test that — preferred, it keeps the server change small): (a) Enqueue k; Enqueue k with blob B2 before dequeue; dequeue yields B2 once. (b) Enqueue k (disk case); dequeue (gen 1); Enqueue k; Finish(gen 1) re-queues; dequeue yields gen 2; Finish(gen 2) empties. (c) One Put only: exactly one dequeue. (d) Enqueue returning false for size does not bump the generation.
Integration (section `11b`): mock S3 with latency 500 ms; store manifest value V1, then V2 within 100 ms through the daemon; after `--stop-daemon` the mock bucket's object for the key equals V2.

Mutations:
- M1 keep the early `return true` for queued keys: (a) and (b) fail.
- M2 re-queue without bumping the generation (always re-queue): (c) fails (two uploads).
- M3 unlink the journal in FinishUpload even when re-queued: add an assertion in (b) that the journal file exists after Finish(gen 1); it must fail.
- M4 replace held_ without adjusting held_bytes_: assert held_bytes_ after (a); must fail.
- M5 bump generation on a refused Enqueue: (d) fails.
close_reason: 681d4bb: a refused re-put does not overwrite a newer accepted store

# Reviewer findings on vcache-ae4.4 (eb1ef1d), 2026-10-08: fix after vcache-ae4.7

Reopened. The common rewrite-during-upload case is right and M1-M5 all fail as they should. Fix these in one `fix(daemon): …` commit after vcache-ae4.7, each with a fail-first test, then append to the report and close again. Finding 2 corrects the bead's own pass-2 text: the bead was wrong, not you.

1. **Held blob wins over a newer disk value (medium).** upload_queue.cc (Enqueue: `if (blob != nullptr) item.blob = …`; and the re-queue path). Put V1 while the disk write fails, so V1 is held; Put V2 with the disk write succeeding, so `Enqueue(key, nullptr)`: the queued item and held_[k] still carry V1, and a re-queue after an in-flight upload re-reads held V1. ## What changed

`UploadWorker` and the synchronous put change `uploads_done`, `uploads_failed` and `uploads_skipped` in the same locked section as `Finish` or `Requeue`. `StatusText` copies those counters, and pending, while it holds the lock.

title: RestoreOutputs joins stored file names onto the output dir without a traversal check
description:
A blob file name containing '..' escapes parsed.out_dir on a hit. Harmless with a single-user disk cache; material once blobs come from S3 or a peer. Reject names with '..' components or an absolute path at restore and at capture. Fails first: a unit test that a crafted blob is refused.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): behaviour diff

Verified: `RestoreOutputs` (src/rust/rust_compile.cc) writes `out_dir + "/" + file.name` for every `BlobFile`; `CaptureOutputs` sets `file.name = fs::relative(entry.path(), dir)`. The C++ blob restores only the object and depfile to paths from the command line (not from blob names), and the link cache restores `.linkout` digests to the link outputs it parsed itself. So only the Rust path trusts stored names.

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Name `libfoo.rlib`, `deps/x.d` | written under out_dir | unchanged |
| Name with a `..` component, absolute name, empty name, name with a NUL | written wherever it points | entry rejected as unusable: `RestoreOutputs` returns false before writing anything, VCACHE_LOG `rust: refusing stored file name '<name>'`; the caller already treats false as "unusable entry, recompile" |
| Capture of a file whose relative path would be refused | stored | `CaptureOutputs` returns false (uncacheable, kCaptureFailed) so we never store what we would refuse |

| Name | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `a/b/c.rmeta` | ok |
| `./a.rlib` | ok (normalise, or accept `.` components; decide and test) |
| `../x`, `a/../../x`, `/etc/x`, `` (empty), `a\0b` | refuse |
| `a/..b/c` (dots inside a component) | ok |
| symlink inside out_dir pointing outside | out of scope: note it in the report; RestoreOutputs writes with WriteFileAtomic which replaces the link itself |

Naming: `bool IsSafeOutputName(std::string_view name)` in rust_compile.cc's anonymous namespace (or util/fs.h if you need it in two files).

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `rust::output names`): the table above, one Check per row. Unit: a serialized blob carrying a file named `../escape` fails restore and creates no file outside a scratch out_dir (check the parent dir is unchanged).

title: Concurrent LoadManifest/StoreManifest cycles lose each other's states
description:
Two compiles of one manifest key in different worktrees read the same states, each prepends its own and writes back; the second write drops the first's state. Merge on store (re-read, union by key, cap) instead of overwrite. Fails first: a unit test that two interleaved store cycles leave both states present.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified: two manifests are read-modify-written without a lock. Rust: `LoadManifest` at lookup, then after a miss compile `StoreManifest(cache, key, RecordRustState(fresh, states))` (src/rust/rust_compile.cc), where `states` is the copy read at lookup, seconds or minutes earlier. Dep-scan: the same shape around `PrependManifestState(fresh, entries, &DepManifestEntry::result_key)` in src/core/compile.cc. Two compiles of one manifest key in different worktrees both load the same states, each prepends its own, and the second write drops the first's state. Effect: lost cache effectiveness (the dropped state misses next time), never a wrong hit.

Design (fixed): re-read just before writing and merge. The window shrinks from the compile's duration to the gap between one Get and one Put (milliseconds); the residual race is documented, not closed. No lock: a lock file in the shards would be walked and evicted by TrimGlobal, and a daemon-side merge is a later feature.

Merge rule, both manifests: `result = Prepend(fresh, reread ++ [s for s in loaded if s.key not in reread and s.key != fresh.key])`, then the existing cap `kMaxManifestStates` (= 8, src/core/manifest.h). `reread` failing to load or parse counts as empty (today's behaviour on a corrupt manifest).

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single compile of a key | one Get at lookup, one Put | one Get at lookup, one more Get just before the Put, one Put (one extra Get per miss: disk read of a small manifest, measured cost to report) |
| Two concurrent compiles, different fresh states | one state lost | both kept |
| Manifest hit on a state > 0 (re-record moves it to front) | Put of re-ordered states | same re-read-and-merge path |
| Read-only cache | no Put | no Put, no re-read |
| Cap | kMaxManifestStates = 8 | unchanged |

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| reread contains fresh.key already (another worktree stored the same state) | one copy, at the front |
| reread is corrupt | treated as empty; loaded states still merged |
| loaded is empty (first compile) | result = Prepend(fresh, reread) |
| Both lists at the cap | result capped; fresh first, reread order kept, loaded-only states last |

Naming: one shared helper `MergeManifestStates` in src/core/manifest.{h,cc} beside `PrependManifestState`, templated or overloaded like it; used by both sites.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `core::manifest merge`): the four operational rows, each with exact input lists of keys and exact expected output order.
Integration (section `9f. Concurrent manifest stores keep both states`): simulate the interleaving deterministically, no sleeps: tree A compiles crate version 1 (stores state S1); then, using the manifest key, run tree B's compile of version 2 with `VCACHE_TEST_PAUSE_BEFORE_MANIFEST_PUT=<fifo>` (a test-only hook that blocks on reading the fifo just before the re-read) while tree C compiles version 3 to completion; then release B by writing to the fifo. Afterwards switching back to versions 2 and 3 both hit through the manifest (`rust manifest hit` in the log), with no dep-info run. The hook is compiled in always but inert unless the env var is set; name it in docs/design.md's test section.

Mutations: M1 no re-read (use loaded only): the integration test misses on version 3; M2 merge without dedup: unit row 1 fails (two copies); M3 drop loaded-only states: unit row 2 fails; M4 put reread before fresh: unit order assertion fails; M5 apply only to Rust, not dep-scan: add a dep-scan unit/integration twin; it must fail.
close_reason: ca5b5ee: merge a manifest re-read so concurrent stores keep both states

# Reviewer notes on vcache-ae4.7 (ca5b5ee), 2026-10-08: approved; two hang risks to fix with the vcache-ae4.4 batch

The merge rule, both call sites, timing, read-only path and all M1-M5 are correct (reviewer re-ran them). Fix these in the same follow-up commit as the vcache-ae4.4 findings (or one more small commit), fail-first where possible, and append to the ae4.7 report (the bead stays closed).

1. **A stale fifo hangs the build forever (low).** The `VCACHE_TEST_PAUSE_BEFORE_MANIFEST_PUT` hook (src/core/manifest.cc) opens the fifo with a blocking open and no timeout; an env var left pointing at an existing fifo with no writer blocks every manifest store indefinitely. Open with `O_NONBLOCK`, then `poll` for readability with a bound (60 s), log `manifest: test pause timed out` and carry on. A missing path / regular file / directory should not log "waiting before put" at all. Unit or integration check: a fifo with no writer returns within the bound.
2. **The integration tests can hang instead of failing (low).** `printf x > "$fifo"` (tests/integration_test.sh, the 9f and 14b sections) runs even when the "waits" check failed; if B exited before reaching the pause, the write blocks forever. Write to the fifo only when the waiting check passed; otherwise kill B and record the failure. Bound every such write.
3. **Nits:** add a unit row for a state present in both the loaded and the re-read list; drop `RecordRustState` if it is now test-only (or say why it stays); reuse the lookup's dep-scan parse instead of the inline copy; do not count a media error twice when the re-read and the Put both fail; log "rust manifest: none stored" once on a first compile.

title: cxx preprocessing: measure the -E pipeline on the incremental path and the soundness and speed of faster candidates
description:
Owner priority (2026-10-15): warm incremental build time matters more than cold build time. This is a
measurement task: evaluate the cost of the C/C++ `-E` path and recommend separately scoped changes.
Do not ship a new preprocessor or change the installed binaries as part of it. A no-adoption
conclusion with evidence completes the task.

## Why the `-E` run is on the incremental path (verified 2026-10-18 against fbg 5ab1f15)

- After an edit invalidates a TU's manifest states, `RunCompile` (src/core/compile.cc, near the
  `cold_recording` decision) runs `BuildPreprocessCommand` under the tracer, writes the output to
  `<scratch>/pp.i`, and `HashNormalizedPreprocessedOutput` (src/core/preprocessed.cc) rewrites the
  linemarker paths through the roots and hashes the text. A preprocessed-key hit records a new
  manifest state from that run (`PlanCxxPreprocessRecording`, counter `pp hits recorded`); a miss
  compiles.
- vcache-moz (landed d393550) skips the `-E` run only for a *cold recording* compile: no stored
  manifest, not a PCH producer, **no keyed PCH**, tracer usable. On sunbird that excludes most TUs:
  host `build/` has 383 compile commands of which 344 consume a PCH; el10 `build-el10/` has 525 of
  which 485 do. So on sunbird the `-E` run still precedes every miss of a PCH consumer, cold or not,
  and every stale-state check of every TU.
- Under clang, `-E` does not load the PCH; the command's `-Xclang -include -Xclang cmake_pch.hxx`
  expands the PCH header textually, so the preprocessed text of a PCH consumer carries the whole PCH
  content (nlohmann json extern templates and the rest of `cmake/pch/SunbirdPchDeployed.h`).
- The whole-build figures that motivated this (vcache-232: about 1m30 extra user CPU over 525 TUs,
  about 0.17 s per TU) mix `-E`, tracing and memo work. Measure the `-E` pipeline by itself.
- Manifest states per TU are capped at 8 (`kMaxManifestStates`, src/core/manifest.h): a header that
  takes more than 8 successive edit variants evicts the oldest states, including the baseline.

## Corpus facts (verified 2026-10-18)

| Fact | Host | el10 |
|---|---|---|
| sunbird revision at polish time | 46e858faf (`sunbird` branch); pin the one you use | same tree through `/code/sunbird_strategy` |
| build dir with a deps log | `build/` (clang++-22, 373 objects in `ninja -t deps`) | `build-el10/` (clang 23.1.4 `absent-deps-2`, 517 objects) |
| compile commands / PCH consumers | 383 / 344 | 525 / 485 |
| compiler `-fminimize-whitespace` | present (clang 22.1.8) | present (clang 23.1.4) |
| gcc | 16.2.1 | 14.3.1 |
| strace, perf | both | neither |
| ccache | 4.12.3, `cmake/ccache.conf`: depend_mode, sloppiness pch_defines,time_macros | 4.11.3, same conf |

Third-party candidate availability on this host (no root in an agent shell): no D compiler installed
(`ldc` 1.42.0 is in the Fedora repo; installing it is the owner's call, see stop conditions); `pcpp`
1.30 installs through pip into a venv under the task scratch; simplecpp builds from source with a
C++ compiler; mcpp and tcc are not in the Fedora repos (source builds only). None of them is in the
el10 image. Record a candidate that cannot be built as such, with the reason, and continue.

Feature queries the corpus exercises (`rg` over sunbird, build dirs excluded): `__has_include`,
`__has_builtin`, `__has_feature` in `3rdparty/tomlplusplus/toml.hpp` and in libstdc++, boost and
arrow system headers; `_Pragma` and `__has_cpp_attribute` in 3 first-party files each; `#pragma
once` in 487 files; no `__VA_OPT__`, `#include_next`, `#elifdef`, `__COUNTER__`, `__DATE__`,
`__TIME__` or `__TIMESTAMP__` in first-party code (system headers may still use them).

Headers for the edit matrix, by dependents in the deps log (count the TUs actually invoked, do not
assume these numbers):

| Fan-out | Header | Host | el10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| about 130 | `protocol/types/SymbolId.h` | 138 | about 130 (verify) |
| about 130 | `protocol/types/Price.h` | 123 | verify |
| about 35 | `sunbird/ensemble/EnsembleSnapshot.h` | 38 | verify |
| about 35 | `core/siren/SirenAlert.h` | verify | 39 |
| about 12 | `core/transport/EpollDispatcher.h` | 14 | verify |
| about 12 | `algo/ordex/OrderRejectPolicy.h` | verify | 14 |
| every TU | `protocol/dev/imacros.h` (`-include`d) | 373 | 517 |
| PCH content | `cmake/pch/NlohmannJsonExternTemplates.h` | verify | 486 |
| generated | a wiregen output under `build/protocol/` (pick the one with most dependents) | find | find |
| non-PCH TUs | the 39 (host) / 40 (el10) commands without `-include-pch`, for case (b) below | list | list |

## Candidates and decision rules

| Id | Candidate | What is measured | Adoption bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline-file` | today's traced `-E` into `pp.i`, then normalise and hash | the reference for every ratio | none |
| `baseline-stream` | compiler stdout piped into the normaliser/hasher; a prototype in the task worktree only | identical normalised digests to `baseline-file` on every corpus TU; wall/user/sys; peak RSS of vcache and the compiler; bytes written | 10% of the `-E` pipeline, RSS not above `baseline-file` plus one hash batch |
| `clang-minws` | `-E -fminimize-whitespace` (probe each compiler; do not assume a version) | token sequence and linemarkers against plain `-E`; diagnostics; normalised digest equality or difference | 10%; a changed text needs a key-version decision in the adoption bead |
| `clang-rewrite-includes` | `-E -frewrite-includes` | output size, retained comments and branches; which edits of the matrix it fails to ignore | measured for the record; may only be proposed as a separate *derived* key, never as the preprocessed key |
| `gcc-directives-only` | gcc `-E -fdirectives-only` | same as above, gcc-built TUs only (sunbird builds with clang; measure on vcache's own `tests/` fixtures and say so) | same as above |
| `warp` | facebookarchive/warp, needs a D compiler | builds or not; feature checklist; corpus; speed | corpus clean and 2x `baseline-file` end to end |
| `simplecpp` | danmar/simplecpp | same | same |
| `pcpp` | pip `pcpp` 1.30 (Python; expected slow, included to exercise the checker) | same | same |
| `mcpp`, `tcc` | source builds | same | same |
| `unsound-main-file-only` | the digest of the TU's own source text only, every header ignored (a depend mode without headers) | passes E1; **must fail** the checker on E4 | n/a |
| `unsound-no-absent` | `baseline-file` with absent-path recording disabled | **must fail** the checker on E7 | n/a |
| `unsound-constant` | a candidate that emits a fixed digest | **must fail** the checker on the first semantic edit | n/a |

Third-party candidates receive the compiler's predefined macros from `<compiler> <flags> -E -dM
/dev/null`, memoised the way `SystemIncludeDirs` memoises, the same `-I/-isystem/-include/-D`
flags, and the same roots. A macro dump does not answer function-like feature queries or
target/language state; that gap is what the E5 edit tests.

## Soundness contract

For identical compiler identity, effective flags, environment and root mappings, a candidate key
must change whenever the compiler's normalised preprocessed output or any code-generation input
changes. Extra invalidations lose hits; a missing invalidation can serve a wrong object. Present and
absent dependency discovery, include-search order, PCH identity, compiler builtins, path rewriting
and the changed-during-run safeguards must all be preserved.

Hashing both branches of a conditional a tool cannot evaluate is **not** a sound fallback: a branch
may define macros that change later text, choose includes or alter later conditionals. The sound
fallback for an unsupported or undecidable construct is the real compiler's `-E`, and the fallback
must be observable (a counter and a log line). Corpus success is evidence, not proof: delimit the
supported subset in the report.

## Edit matrix (deterministic; one edit at a time; revert between edits)

| Id | Edit | Where | Compiler digest | Expected sound candidate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | append `// axb E1` comment line | each matrix header | unchanged | unchanged |
| E2 | add a blank line and trailing spaces | each matrix header | unchanged (linemarkers shift: verify, it may change) | same as compiler |
| E3 | add `#define AXB_UNUSED_E3 1` | each matrix header | unchanged | unchanged |
| E4 | add `#define AXB_E4 1` and use it in a declaration in the same header | each matrix header | changed | changed |
| E5 | wrap a declaration in `#if __has_builtin(__builtin_expect)` / `#else` with a different declaration | SymbolId.h and a toml.hpp consumer | changed | changed |
| E6 | swap the order of two `#include` lines | SymbolId.h | changed (linemarkers) | changed |
| E7 | create a header at a path the compile probed and found absent (take it from the TU's manifest state `absent` list) that shadows a real include | one TU per fan-out class | changed | changed |
| E8 | E1 and E4 applied to `cmake/pch/NlohmannJsonExternTemplates.h` | PCH content | E1 unchanged, E4 changed | same |
| E9 | regenerate a wiregen header with one added field | generated header | changed | changed |
| E10 | the same tree at a second worktree path, no edit | two worktrees | unchanged (roots map it) | unchanged |
| E11 | 9 successive E1 variants on one header | SymbolId.h | unchanged each time | unchanged; afterwards the baseline state has been evicted (cap 8): the control re-measures a hit only after one more `-E` |

Record for every (candidate, edit, TU): compiler normalised digest, candidate digest, whether the
candidate fell back, and the dependency set delta. A pair where the compiler digest changes and the
candidate digest does not is a disqualifying counterexample: keep its source, command line and
logs under `counterexamples/<candidate>/<edit>/<tu>/`. Also record false invalidations (candidate
changed, compiler unchanged) and the fallback rate; a candidate that falls back on most TUs cannot
meet the performance bar even if sound.

## Operational cases

| Input class | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Candidate binary cannot be built here (no D compiler, no root) | row in the candidate table with the exact missing requirement; no `sudo`, no system package install; continue |
| Candidate crashes or times out on a TU | counted as a fallback for that TU; after 3 crashes on distinct TUs the candidate is reported as unusable for the rest of the corpus |
| Candidate exits 0 with empty output | treated as a failure, never as a digest |
| Compiler `-E` exits non-zero for a TU (today: `preprocess failed` counter) | the TU is excluded from ratios and listed; the count must match vcache's own counter |
| PCH consumer (90% of TUs) | the candidate gets the `-include cmake_pch.hxx` expansion; a candidate that cannot expand it is a fallback for those TUs, and the report says what share of the build that is |
| PCH producer (`-x c++-header`, 22 on host, 24 on el10) | excluded from the corpus; say so |
| Non-PCH TUs (39 host, 40 el10) | the only TUs that take the cold-recording path; case (b) below is measured on them and the report says so |
| Two worktrees | E10; each store and each candidate's outputs live under the task scratch, never in the production stores (`/build/$USER/cache/vcache/*`) |
| Host load | every timing run is one of at least three interleaved, uninstrumented runs; report min, median, max and the 1-minute load before each; instrumented runs (strace, perf, RSS sampling) are separate and never reported as timings |
| el10 | no strace or perf: timing and RSS (`/usr/bin/time -v` or `/proc`) only; syscall counts come from the host |
| ccache on PATH | strip `/usr/lib64/ccache` for every compiler run |
| Daemon | a private daemon per store (`VCACHE_DAEMON=auto` with a task `VCACHE_DIR`); never the production daemon; counters read from the task store only |
| The `-E` run of a traced compile | the tracer is loaded exactly as vcache loads it; a candidate that cannot be traced records that it cannot supply a manifest state |
| A corpus run interrupted | every result row is appended to `results.jsonl` as it completes, so a rerun resumes by skipping rows already present for the same (candidate, edit, TU, revision) |

## Incremental-build measurements (the numbers the owner wants)

On host and el10, with links timed separately (count linker invocations; report compile and link
time apart), the policy of the installed vcache (cold recording on, verify with `--show-config`):

| Case | Setup | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| control | warm tree, no edit | wall; `manifest hits` equals the TU count; 0 `-E` runs |
| (a) benign edit, preprocessed entries exist | E1 on `SymbolId.h` after a build that went through `-E` (a PCH consumer tree always has) | wall, the number of `-E` runs (equals invoked TUs), `pp hits recorded` delta, 0 compiles |
| (b) first benign edit after a derived-only cold fill | E1 on a header whose dependents are non-PCH TUs only | the `-E` runs miss the preprocessed key and compile; `pp hits recorded` 0; wall |
| (c) semantic edit | E4 on `SymbolId.h` | wall; `-E` runs plus compiles equal invoked TUs |
| (d) same as (a) and (c) on the 35- and 12-TU headers | | same |

For each candidate that passes the corpus, repeat (a) and (c) with the candidate substituted in the
prototype build and report the delta. Keep per-TU small/median/PCH-consumer breakdowns.

## Deliverables

- `results.jsonl` (one row per candidate, edit, TU, platform, revision), `candidates.md` (support,
  build, licence, revision, unsupported constructs), `timings.md` (the tables above with spread),
  `counterexamples/`, the exact environment and command lines, under
  `/build/$USER/claude-tmp/forgrok/vcache-axb/`; the conclusions and tables as a comment on this bead.
- Optional repeatable harness `tests/cxx_preprocess_bench.sh` (not part of `make test`) only if it
  is reusable for the adoption beads; otherwise the runnable recipe in `timings.md`.
- One adoption bead per recommendation that meets its bar, each with scope, tests, fallback
  behaviour, key-version implications and dependencies.

## Names

| Concept | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Compiler command | `BuildPreprocessCommand` | existing |
| Digest normalisation | `HashNormalizedPreprocessedOutput` | existing |
| Candidate ids | as in the candidate table (`baseline-file`, `clang-minws`, ...) | one id per row, used in file names and `results.jsonl` |
| Edit ids | `E1`..`E11` | as in the edit matrix |
| Task scratch | `/build/$USER/claude-tmp/forgrok/vcache-axb/` | agent scratch rule; requested for pruning when done |
| Worktrees | `/build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/vcache/axb`, `.../sunbird/axb-a`, `.../sunbird/axb-b` | agent worktree rule |
| Optional harness | `tests/cxx_preprocess_bench.sh` | follows `tests/concurrent_worktrees_bench.sh` |
| Log marker for a candidate fallback (prototype only) | `cxx preprocess: candidate <id> fell back: <why>` | matches the `cxx manifest:` log register |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every candidate in the table has a recorded build outcome; every accepted candidate passes
  E1-E11 on every corpus TU of both platforms, with its unsupported constructs listed and its
  fallback counted.
- [ ] Each of `unsound-main-file-only`, `unsound-no-absent` and `unsound-constant` makes the checker
  fail on the named edit (E4, E7, first semantic edit) with the counterexample saved; this runs
  before any real candidate result is trusted.
- [ ] `baseline-stream` is byte-identical in normalised digest to `baseline-file` on every corpus
  TU, or its differences are listed per TU.
- [ ] Host and el10 tables with pipeline wall/user/sys, RSS, bytes written, fallback and
  false-invalidation rates, and cases control, (a), (b), (c), (d), compiles and links counted.
- [ ] Recommendations only at the stated bars (2x third-party, 10% compiler-side), each as its own
  bead with a key-version decision; or an evidenced no-adoption conclusion.
- [ ] No change to shipped binaries, production stores or counters; prototypes stay on the task
  branch.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-18): state, time, behaviour diff

- Added the verified facts section: cold recording excludes PCH consumers, which are 90% of
  sunbird's TUs, so the `-E` run is on every miss there, not only on stale states. The earlier text
  implied the cold fill no longer preprocesses.
- Added the 8-state cap and edit E11, since a matrix that cycles more than 8 variants evicts the

- Added the before/after rule for prototypes: `baseline-stream` and `clang-minws` are built on the
