title: Daemon as scheduler: single-flight keys, memory-aware admission, jobserver pool
description:
Make the 1.3.0 cache daemon the machine-wide coordinator for every compile and link that goes through vcache: compile a missed key once when several worktrees miss it together (single-flight), start a compile only when the machine can hold it (memory admission), and hand out job slots to ninja, make and cargo from one elastic pool (jobserver mode). Filed upstream as Unto-Labs/vcache#24; this epic is our implementation plan whether or not upstream takes it.

## Why

One 128-core / 125 GB host builds the same C++/Rust monorepo in several git worktrees at once (agents and humans). A `-O3 -ggdb3` C++ TU peaks near 3 GB, a release link above that. Every worktree runs its own `ninja -j N` / `cargo build`, each sized from the memory it saw at *its* start (sunbird's build.sh computes -j from MemAvailable once and says itself that ninja never retunes it), so two or three concurrent builds overcommit, swap, or lose a compiler to the OOM killer. After a shared-header edit every tree also recompiles the same ~400 TUs. vcache is the only process that already knows the key (dedup), could know the cost (admission) and spawns the compiler (realised memory), so the coordination belongs here rather than in a separate daemon that would need all three reported to it.

## What the daemon is today (verified 2026-10-08, dev 2c2c6e0)

A proxy for keys and blobs over a Unix socket: ops kHello, kGet, kPut, kStatus, kShutdown (daemon/protocol.h, kProtocolVersion = 1, unknown versions refused at hello). One connection per request (DaemonClient::RoundTrip closes after each), one thread per connection in Server::Serve, kMaxConnections = 1024, kReplyTimeoutSeconds = 300, Shutdown waits 60 s then shuts leftover fds. Counters are process totals (Server::counters_). held_ buffers blobs awaiting upload only when the disk layer did not take them. It never sees paths, roots, decisions, timings, pids or which tree a key belongs to; every feature here adds that through new ops. Measured on our 357-crate Rust workspace with a disk-only cache: warm 4.2-5.3 s off vs 4.8-5.4 s auto, cold ~115 s either way, raw cargo cold 108 s.

## Ground rules every child keeps

1. Daemon unavailable, refused, VCACHE_DAEMON=off, or the feature's own switch off: behaviour is exactly today's (compile in-process). No feature may turn a daemon failure into a build failure.
2. A lease or reservation is memory-only, dies with its client's socket, is never journalled, and is dropped on daemon restart (waiters are told to proceed locally). Speculative or read-only clients never hold one.
3. A waiting client still occupies a ninja/cargo job slot, so every wait is bounded and logged with its length.
4. kProtocolVersion becomes 2 in .8; an old daemon refuses at hello and the client falls back (rule 1).
5. One held connection per in-flight compile (a CompileSession, .8) carries lease, reservation and spawned-pid messages; RoundTrip's per-request connections stay for Get/Put. Shutdown closes sessions immediately instead of waiting on them; Idle() counts an open session as a client.
6. Every integration test asserts on VCACHE_LOG lines and --daemon-status rows, not only on exit codes, so a regression says which decision went wrong.

## Naming (bead ids cannot be renamed)

| concept | name | why |
|---|---|---|
| per-compile held connection | CompileSession (server), DaemonClient::OpenCompileSession, Op::kSessionOpen | joins Upload/UploadWorker naming; "session" alone fails out-of-context |
| single-flight hold on a key | KeyLease, Server::leases_ | the key is what is leased |
| ops | Op::kLeaseAcquire, kLeaseRelease, kMemoryReserve, kCompilerSpawned | join the Op enum; noun-verb states the purpose |
| memory grant | MemoryReservation, Server::reservations_ | |
| cost record | CompileCost {max_rss_kb, wall_ms, recorded_at}, CostKey, dir <cache>/costs/ | sibling of <cache>/compilers/ memos |
| ProcResult additions | max_rss_kb, wall_ms | units in the name |
| config | daemon.single_flight, daemon.admission, daemon.default_compile_kb, daemon.default_link_kb, daemon.jobserver, daemon.jobserver_jobs | join the [daemon] table; env VCACHE_DAEMON_<KEY> |
| CLI | --show-costs, --jobserver-env | join --show-stats / --daemon-status |
| counters (--daemon-status rows) | leases held / waiting / expired, compiles deduplicated; memory reserved_kb / realised_kb / reserve waits; jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn | |
| log markers (VCACHE_LOG) | "lease: ", "reserve: ", "jobserver: ", "cost: " | one topic word, like "rust manifest: " |
| fifo | <state dir>/jobserver.fifo | beside sock, lock, pending/ |

## Workflow for every child

Branch feat/<slug> from origin/main (our integration branch: upstream 1.3.0 + fork fixes; baseline make test 499 unit / 379 integration checks, 0 failed). export MAKEFLAGS=-j8 and keep /usr/lib64/ccache off PATH. Every new check is shown failing first and recorded as `Fails first:` in the commit body (AGENTS.md). Push the branch, merge --no-ff into main, push main:main. Commits that change the binary end with `Deploy: vcache`; rebuild dist/ with devtools' host-setup-buildcache.sh --force after the merge. Update docs/daemon.md and docs/configuration.md in the same commit as the feature. Do not touch the sibling repos' vcache-env.sh from these beads; .5 files those follow-ups.

## Order

.1 cost records and .8 compile sessions first (both small; admission reads .1, and .2/.3 sit on .8). .2 single-flight and .3 admission are then independent of each other. .4 fixed jobserver pool is independent too. .7 elastic pool needs .3 and .4. .5 build-tool integration needs .4 (and .7 for the elastic claim). .6 measurement last.
close_reason: All children done. Measured: single-flight 5-26% faster cold (on by default in devtools vcache-env); admission and jobserver pools no measured gain, stay opt-in

title: Cost records: wait4 peak RSS and wall time in blob meta, <cache>/costs/, and --show-costs
description:
## What

util::Run (src/util/subprocess.cc) waits with waitpid and throws resource usage away. Switch to wait4 and add to ProcResult: `uint64_t max_rss_kb` (ru_maxrss) and `uint64_t wall_ms` (monotonic clock around fork..wait). For the clang/gcc driver, wait4's ru_maxrss is the peak of the largest waited-for child, i.e. cc1plus/cc1, which is the number that matters; rustc is single-process; a link is the linker itself. Nothing else about Run changes.

Record the two numbers for every compile and link that vcache runs on a miss (RunCompile, RunRustCompile, RunLink; not dep-info or -E probes):
1. In the blob's meta string on store, as lines `max_rss_kb: N` and `wall_ms: N` after the existing `rustc:`/`crate:`/`roots:` lines (meta is informational and not part of any key, so no key bump).
2. In a CompileCost record under `<cache>/costs/<CostKey hex>`: a small text file with the last 8 observations (`max_rss_kb wall_ms recorded_at_unix`), written by the client with WriteFileAtomic (a lost race drops one observation, acceptable). CostKey = BLAKE3 of (operation: compile|rustc|link, canonical source path or link output path, language, codegen flag class). The flag class is the key_args with -I/-D/-include/paths removed, i.e. the optimisation and debug flags, so a miss on new content of the same file still has an estimate. Content is deliberately not in it.
3. `vcache --show-costs` prints per operation: records, p50 and max of max_rss_kb and wall_ms, and the 10 largest cost keys with their source path.

Estimate lookup (used by .3): max of the recorded max_rss_kb for the cost key; absent, the config default for the operation.

## Logging

VCACHE_LOG gets one line per recorded compile: `cost: <op> max_rss_kb=<n> wall_ms=<n> key=<costkey[0:16]> <source>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (tests/unit_test.cc, new Section "core::cost"): CostKey ignores content and roots but changes with the flag class and the operation; a CompileCost file round-trips and keeps only the last 8; the estimate is the max, not the mean.
- Unit: util::Run on a child that allocates 64 MB reports max_rss_kb >= 65536 and wall_ms within the measured bound.
- Integration (new section "9d. Cost records"): a compile's blob meta carries `max_rss_kb:` > 0; `--show-costs` lists the compile; `VCACHE_LOG` has the `cost:` line.

## Docs

docs/configuration.md: `--show-costs`; docs/design.md: what meta carries. Commit ends `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified: `util::Run` (src/util/subprocess.cc) forks, pumps the pipes, then `waitpid(pid, &status, 0)` in an EINTR loop; `ProcResult` has exit_code, signalled, stdout_data, stderr_data. Callers of interest: `RunCompile` (src/core/compile.cc, the compile on a miss), `RunRustCompile` (src/rust/rust_compile.cc, the `rust compile:` run), `RunLink` (src/core/link.cc). Probes that must NOT be recorded: `-E`, dep-scan, dep-info, `-v`/`-vV`, passthroughs.

Long-lived state: `<cache>/costs/<CostKey hex>`, one file per cost key, the last 8 observations.

| State | Event | Next |
|---|---|---|
| no file | recorded compile | file with 1 line |
| n < 8 lines | recorded compile | n+1 lines, newest last |
| 8 lines | recorded compile | oldest dropped |
| any | two processes record at once | last WriteFileAtomic wins; one observation may be lost (accepted) |
| any | `--clear` | kept: `DiskStorage::Clear` removes only the 256 shards, and leaves `compilers/` the same way; costs survive a clear like the compiler memos |
| corrupt file | read | treated as empty and rewritten on the next record |

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Run's exit code / signal reporting | waitpid status | identical, via wait4 status |
| Blob meta | existing lines | existing lines + `max_rss_kb: N` + `wall_ms: N` (meta is in no key; verify by grep that no key hashes meta) |
| Cache keys | | unchanged; no version bump |
| Extra I/O per miss | none | one small file read and one atomic write under costs/ |
| Hit path | | untouched (nothing recorded on a hit) |

New failure modes: a failure to write the cost file must never fail or slow the compile beyond the write attempt; log `cost: could not record (<why>)` and carry on.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Compiler killed by a signal | still recorded (the peak matters most for OOM kills), with exit noted in the log line |
| Compile failed (exit 1) | recorded |
| wait4 unavailable (macOS has it; any POSIX has it) | no fallback needed; build fails at compile time if missing |
| ru_maxrss units | Linux KiB; macOS bytes: convert so `max_rss_kb` is KiB on both (`#ifdef __APPLE__` divide by 1024) |
| Link with `-flto` spawning lld plus LTO jobs | ru_maxrss is the largest waited-for child; record it as is and say so in docs |
| Cost key flag class | key_args minus `-I*`, `-isystem`, `-D*`, `-U*`, `-include`, `-o`, path-like args canonicalised away; keep `-O*`, `-g*`, `-march=*`, `-f*`, `--edition`, `-C opt-level`, `-C debuginfo` and the language |

Naming: `ProcResult::max_rss_kb`, `ProcResult::wall_ms`, `struct CompileCost`, `std::string ComputeCostKey(...)`, files `src/core/cost.{h,cc}`, dir `<cache>/costs/`, CLI `--show-costs`, log marker `cost: `.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `util::Run rusage`): add a tiny C++ helper built by the Makefile's test target (`bin/vcache_test_alloc <MiB>`: malloc, memset every page, exit 0) and run it through util::Run; assert max_rss_kb >= 65536 for 64 and < 65536 for 1; wall_ms >= 0 and below 10 000.
Unit (Section `core::cost`): ComputeCostKey equal for two sources with different contents and different roots mapping to the same canonical path; differs for `-O2` vs `-O3`, for compile vs link, for C vs C++; CompileCost round-trip keeps the last 8 in order; estimate = max; a corrupt file reads as empty.
Integration (section `9d. Cost records`): one C++ compile miss: the stored blob's meta contains `max_rss_kb:` > 0 (there is no CLI to dump an entry: find the entry file under the shard for the key logged in VCACHE_LOG and grep it with `grep -a`, meta is stored as plain text inside the blob); `--show-costs` prints a `compile` row with records 1; VCACHE_LOG has exactly one `cost: compile` line; a second (hit) run adds no `cost:` line.

Mutations: M1 keep waitpid (max_rss_kb 0): rusage unit fails; M2 record on hits too: integration "no cost line on hit" fails; M3 put content into the cost key: unit "different contents equal" fails; M4 keep 9 observations: round-trip fails; M5 estimate = last instead of max: estimate unit fails; M6 record dep-info runs: integration expects exactly one cost line; fails.
acceptance_criteria: make test green; unit Section core::cost and util::Run rusage checks fail on pre-fix code; integration 9d shows max_rss_kb in meta, --show-costs output and the cost: log line; Fails first lines in the commit body; docs updated; Deploy: vcache
close_reason: 8e7fbe1: cost keys are an allow-list, and trim drops stale cost files

# vcache-cug.1 report (2026-10-08)

## Commits

- `c100efe23e795b7a2b53cf6440116d3c04438096` on `feat/grok-defects-costs-jobserver` (local branch `ntm/vcache/cursor_1`, pushed as that name).

## Tests

Added:

- Unit section `util::Run rusage`: Linux/macOS ru_maxrss conversion, exit code 3, SIGABRT, wall time of `sleep 0.2`, `bin/vcache_test_alloc` 64 MiB `>= 65536` and 1 MiB `< 65536`.
- Unit section `core::cost`: cost key ignores content, roots, `-I`/`-D`/`-include`/`-o`/`-isystem` and path-like args; changes for `-O2`/`-O3`, compile/link, C/C++, `-march`, `-C opt-level`, `--edition`; file grows to 8 then drops the oldest; estimate is the max; corrupt file reads empty and is rewritten; `--show-costs` row; failed and signalled exits in the log; meta lines; `--clear` keeps `costs/`; write failure logs `cost: could not record`; a link stores the given peak unchanged.
- Integration section `9d. Cost records`: blob meta `max_rss_kb` > 0 and `wall_ms`; `--show-costs` `compile records 1`; exactly one `cost: compile` on a miss and none added on a hit; a failing compile and a compiler killed by SIGABRT are still recorded with `exit=`.

Last `make test` tail:

```
unit: 537 passed, 0 failed
integration: 390 passed, 0 failed
```

## Deviations

- `EstimateMaxRssKb` returns nullopt when the file is missing, empty or corrupt. The per-operation defaults `daemon.default_compile_kb` / `daemon.default_link_kb` are specified on vcache-cug.3, so this bead does not add those config keys. Admission supplies the default.
- The cost file is the eight observation lines `max_rss_kb wall_ms recorded_at_unix` plus three header lines (`op`, `language`, `source`). `--show-costs` cannot recover the source path or the operation from the hash alone.
- A relative source is passed through `AbsoluteLexical` before `Canonicalize`. Otherwise `t.cc` never matches a root and the cost key stays checkout-local.
- A link's language field is empty. The operation `link` is what separates it from a compile of the same path.
- The new integration section is titled `9d. Cost records`. The tree already has `9d. Rust: manifest-verified lookups skip the dep-info run`. Both titles are kept.
- `daemon/server.cc` still uses `waitpid` to reap the daemon process. That is not `util::Run`. The unit test's umask child also still uses `waitpid`.

## Before / after

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Run exit code / signal | `waitpid` status, `WIFEXITED` / `WIFSIGNALED`, exit `128+signal` | same decoding of the `wait4` status |
| `max_rss_kb` / `wall_ms` | absent (0 if read) | set from `ru_maxrss` (KiB; macOS bytes `/ 1024`) and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` around fork..wait |
| Blob meta | compiler/language/roots, or rustc/crate/roots; link blobs had no meta | those lines plus `max_rss_kb: N` and `wall_ms: N`. Meta is not hashed into a key (set after the key is computed; `SerializeBlob` stores it as a section only) |
| Cache key versions | `vcache-key-v2`, `vcache-rust-key-v3`, `vcache-link-v1` | unchanged |
| Hit path | return before the real compile | still no cost record and no extra log line |
| Miss compile / rustc / link, including exit 1 and a signal | no cost file | one append under `<cache>/costs/<blake3 hex>`, last 8 kept, log `cost: <op> ...` with `exit=` when the status is not 0 |
| `-E` preprocess, dep-info, `-v`/`-vV`, passthrough | `util::Run` only | still not recorded |
| `--clear` | removes the 256 shards only | same; `costs/` remains, as `compilers/` does |
| Extra I/O on a miss | none | one small read and one `WriteFileAtomic` under `costs/` |

New failure modes:

- `wait4` replaces `waitpid`. A non-EINTR failure still leaves status 0, as the old `waitpid` loop did.
- Creating `<cache>/costs` or the atomic write can fail (the path exists as a file, the directory is unwritable). Logged as `cost: could not record (<why>)`. The compile's exit code is unchanged.
- Two recorders of one key: last `WriteFileAtomic` wins and one observation can be lost. No lock.

## Mutations

| Id | Change | Test that failed | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `waitpid` and `max_rss_kb = 0` | `util::Run rusage` | `64 MiB child reports max_rss_kb >= 65536 (got 0)` |
| M2 | `RecordCompileCost` on the compile hit path | integration `9d. Cost records` | `a hit adds no cost line (expected '1', got '2')` |
| M3 | `Hasher::UpdateFile` of the source inside `ComputeCostKey` | `core::cost` | `different contents and roots with the same canonical path share a cost key` (expected/actual digests differed) |
| M4 | keep 9 observations | `core::cost` | `a cost file keeps only the last 8 observations` and `the oldest observations are dropped and the newest stays last` |
| M5 | estimate returns the last observation | `core::cost` | `the estimate is the max, not the mean and not the last observation` |
| M6 | also record the `-E` preprocess `util::Run` in `RunCompile` | integration `9d. Cost records` | `exactly one cost: compile line on a miss (expected '1', got '2')` |

A record added only inside `RunDepScan` is not reached by section 9d (that compile's extra `util::Run` is the `-E` probe). Recording that probe is what M6 failed. Reverted; `git diff` against `c100efe` is empty for those files.

Not caught, by design: two processes recording one key. The loss is the `WriteFileAtomic` last-writer-wins contract. There is no pause between the read and the rename, and the bead accepts one dropped observation. Sequential append (1 line, then 2, then drop to 8) is tested.

## Names not in the hand-over table

- `RssKbFromRuMaxrss(long, bool ru_maxrss_is_bytes)`
- `CompileCost::Observation`
- `LoadCompileCost`, `RecordCompileCost`, `EstimateMaxRssKb`, `AppendCostMeta`, `FormatCosts`
- internal: `CostFlagClass`, `kMaxCostObservations` (8), `kLargestCostKeys` (10)

## Open questions

- None that block this bead. vcache-cug.3 should call `EstimateMaxRssKb` and apply `daemon.default_compile_kb` (2097152) or `daemon.default_link_kb` (4194304) on nullopt.

# Reviewer findings on vcache-cug.1 (c100efe), 2026-10-08: fix before merge

Reopened. Fix in one follow-up commit on your branch (`fix(core): …`), right after your current bead's commit and before the next bead: Sol's memory-admission bead needs vcache-cug.1 on main. Each fix needs a fail-first test (recorded as `Fails first:` lines), and every mutation below must be shown failing.

1. **rustc cost key changes on Cargo hash bumps (medium).** `CostFlagClass` (src/core/cost.cc) keeps every argument it does not explicitly drop, so rustc's `-C metadata=<hash>` and `-C extra-filename=-<hash>` stay in the key; both change on a Cargo.lock bump, toolchain upgrade or feature change. Reproduced: same `src/lib.rs`, differing only in `-C metadata`, gave two cost files. Fix: build the flag class from an explicit allow-list per language: C/C++ keep `-O*`, `-g*`, `-march=*`, `-mtune=*`, `-f*` (except `-fdebug-prefix-map`/`-ffile-prefix-map`/`-fmacro-prefix-map`), `-std=*`; rustc keeps `-C opt-level=*`, `-C debuginfo=*`, `-C codegen-units=*`, `-C lto*`, `-C target-cpu=*`, `--edition*`, `--crate-type*`, `--target*`; link keeps `-O*`, `-flto*`, `-fuse-ld=*`. Unit check: two rustc arg lists differing only in `-C metadata` and `-C extra-filename` give one cost key; differing in `-C opt-level` give two.
2. **No test covers rustc or link recording (medium).** Removing the `RecordCompileCost` calls in src/rust/rust_compile.cc and src/core/link.cc, or recording on the rust dep-info run or a rust hit, passes both suites. Add to section 9d: a rustc miss logs exactly one `cost: rustc` line and the crate's blob meta has `max_rss_kb:`; a rust hit adds none; the dep-info run adds none; a link (with `VCACHE_LINK_CACHE=1`, Linux only, skip elsewhere) logs exactly one `cost: link` line. Mutations: M7 record on the rust dep-info run, M9 record on a rust hit, M11 remove the rustc and link `RecordCompileCost` calls: each must fail a named check.
3. **Extra fsync per miss (low).** `RecordCompileCost` uses `WriteFileAtomic`, which fsyncs before the rename. A statistic needs atomic rename, not durability. Add a non-durable variant (e.g. `util::WriteFileAtomicNoSync` or a `bool durable` parameter defaulting to true so no existing caller changes) and use it for cost files only. Report the before/after in the table.
4. **costs/ grows without bound (low).** Prune cost files whose newest observation is older than 30 days during `--trim` (and the trim that `Put` triggers is fine to skip: keep it to explicit `--trim` and `TrimGlobal`'s global pass, whichever is simpler, and say which). 5. **Docs (info).** One line in docs/design.md: `ru_maxrss` includes vcache's own resident memory at fork (measured negligible: 368,068 KiB through vcache vs 368,992 KiB direct for a heavy TU).

Re-test note from the reviewer: `make bin/vcache_test` reports "Nothing to be done" because the real targets are absolute paths; use `make "$PWD/bin/vcache_test"`.

title: Rust cost key omits --crate-name, so registry crates share cost records
description:
## What
`CostFlagClass` in `src/core/cost.cc` keeps only `-C` values, `--edition`, `--crate-type` and `--target` for rustc. Registry crates' cwd is a root, so every one canonicalises to `/vcache/cwd/src/lib.rs` and shares one cost key: 369 compiles recorded under 65 keys in the bench. With 8 observations per key, small crates evict a large crate's wall time and RSS, which breaks both the lease bound and admission's memory estimate.

## Fix
Include `--crate-name` (and the `-C metadata` hash if needed to separate versions of one crate) in the rustc cost flag class.

## Acceptance
Unit test: two rustc invocations differing only in `--crate-name` with the same canonical source get different cost keys; same crate, different worktree roots, same key. Fails first on current main.
close_reason: Fixed: --crate-name in the rustc cost key

title: Single-flight: KeyLease over a CompileSession so concurrent worktrees compile a missed key once
description:
## What Several worktrees that miss on one key compile it once. docs/design.md chose duplicate compiles deliberately for a single build, where a lock costs more than the duplicate; across worktrees the duplicate is real (a shared-header edit makes every tree recompile the same ~400 TUs). Switch: `daemon.single_flight = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_SINGLE_FLIGHT), default off until .6 has measured it. ## Protocol On the CompileSession from .8 (opened once the key is computed, closed after the outputs are restored or the compile has failed): - `kLeaseAcquire(key, bound_ms)` -> kOk + u8 outcome: `granted` (the session now holds the KeyLease), `stored` (the holder's kPut landed while we waited; do an ordinary kGet), or `compile` (holder failed or vanished, or bound reached). The daemon holds the reply for the waiter until one of those happens; the bound is the client's, computed from the holder's recorded wall_ms (from .1) that the first, immediate reply carries when the key is held: the client sends kLeaseAcquire once with bound_ms=0 to learn the holder's wall_ms, then once more with its bound. - `kLeaseRelease(key, outcome: stored|failed)` from the holder. HandlePut of that key also releases and wakes waiters. - A waiter's wait ends on: the holder's kPut (outcome stored), the holder's release with `failed` (compile), the holder's session closing without a release (compile), daemon shutdown (compile), or the bound (compile). - Bound: max(2 x holder wall_ms, 30 s), capped at kReplyTimeoutSeconds. A waiting wrapper still occupies a ninja/cargo job slot, so no unbounded wait. - Leases are memory-only, never journalled; a daemon restart drops them and reconnecting waiters are told to compile. A speculative or read-only (VCACHE_READONLY) client never acquires. - Concurrent S3 GETs of one key coalesce through the same table: the first Get of a missing-on-disk key fetches, later Gets of it wait for that fetch. ## Server KeyLease {key, holder session, acquired_at, holder_wall_ms, waiters}; Server::leases_ beside queued_keys_. A waiter's session thread blocks on the lease's condition variable with the bound as its timeout (one thread per connection, as today), never on a kGet. Session lifetime, shutdown and Idle() rules come from .8. Counters: leases held, leases waiting, leases expired, compiles deduplicated; --daemon-status rows for all four. ## Client RunCompile, RunRustCompile and RunLink call acquire between key computation and the compile and release after store/failure. Waiters log every transition. ## Logging `lease: acquired `, `lease: waiting on holder pid

up to ms`, `lease: holder stored, serving hit after ms`, `lease: holder failed, compiling`, `lease: holder gone, compiling`, `lease: wait bound reached, compiling`, `lease: released `. ## Tests (fail first) - Unit (new Section "daemon::lease"): grant/deny per key; holder session close expires the lease and wakes waiters with "compile"; failed outcome wakes with "compile"; a stored outcome wakes with "get"; the wait bound arithmetic. - Integration (new section "10b. Single-flight"): two trees, same key, a fake compiler that sleeps 2 s and counts runs through a shared file, VCACHE_DAEMON=auto: exactly one `rust compile:`/`compile:` log line across both VCACHE_LOGs, one `lease: acquired` and one `lease: holder stored`, both trees' outputs byte-identical, `compiles deduplicated 1` in --daemon-status. A second run kills the holder (fake compiler exits 1): the waiter logs `lease: holder failed, compiling` and both trees finish. A third with the daemon stopped mid-wait: `lease: holder gone, compiling`. ## Docs docs/daemon.md: a "Single-flight" section with the rules above and the measured dedup count placeholder filled by .6. `Deploy: vcache`. ## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding) KeyLease state per key: | State | Event | Next | Reply to waiters | |---|---|---|---| | free | A: kLeaseAcquire(k) | held by A | A: granted | | held by A | B: kLeaseAcquire(k, 0) | held, B learns holder_wall_ms | B: immediate `held` reply with wall_ms | | held by A | B: kLeaseAcquire(k, bound) | B waits | | | held by A | A: kPut(k) (any connection) | free | all waiters: stored | | held by A | A: kLeaseRelease(k, failed) | free | all waiters: compile | | held by A | A's session closes without release or put | free, expired++ | all waiters: compile | | held by A | B's bound passes | held by A | B: compile (B then compiles unleased) | | held by A | daemon Shutdown | gone | all waiters: compile | | held by A | A: kLeaseAcquire(k) again | held by A (idempotent) | A: granted | | any | B's session closes while waiting | B removed from waiters | | Same-turn interleavings to test explicitly (the class Grok missed elsewhere; Sol must also cover them): A's kPut and A's session close arriving together (stored must win: waiters get `stored`, not `compile`); B's bound expiring in the same tick as A's kPut (either answer is acceptable but the waiter must not get two replies); A's kLeaseRelease(stored) then kPut (release first: waiters told `stored`, then the Get must hit — if the Put has not landed yet the waiter's Get misses and it compiles, which is safe; document it). Invariants: a key never has two holders; every waiter gets exactly one reply; a holder that dies wakes all its waiters within one second; with single_flight off no lease op is ever sent. Operational cases: holder compile fails (exit 1) -> release failed; holder's store fails (disk full) -> release failed, waiters compile; read-only client never acquires; the dep-info/manifest Put of a Rust crate uses the manifest key, not the entry key: lease only the entry key, never manifest keys; links lease their pre-key/link key the same way. Mutations: M1 grant two holders; M2 wake waiters with `compile` on kPut; M3 no expiry on session close (waiter hangs to its bound: the test bound is 3 s and asserts the holder-gone path answers in under 1.5 s); M4 lease manifest keys; M5 drop the bound (waiter waits forever) — each must fail a named test. ## Reviewer decision (2026-10-08): lease wait bound, answers Sol's stop on vcache-cug.2 Correct stop: the specified fields cannot carry the holder's recorded wall_ms. Decision, superseding the two-step kLeaseAcquire text in the Protocol section and pass 1-3: 1. **No protocol field for cost.** `kLeaseAcquire(key, bound_ms)` is a single request; there is no bound_ms=0 query and no holder wall_ms in any reply. Outcomes unchanged: `granted` | `stored` | `compile`. 2. **The waiter computes its own bound.** Same entry key implies the same canonical source and codegen flags, so the waiter's own CostKey equals the holder's. Bound = max(2 x recorded wall_ms, 30 s), capped at kReplyTimeoutSeconds, where recorded wall_ms is the max over the waiter's own `/costs/` record. No record: 30 s. 3. **Do not wait for vcache-cug.1.** Implement the bound as a pure function, e.g. `uint64_t LeaseWaitBoundMs(std::optional recorded_wall_ms)`, unit-tested on (none -> 30 000; 5 000 -> 30 000; 20 000 -> 40 000; huge -> cap). Call it with `std::nullopt` for now. When vcache-cug.1 is on origin/main (Grok is fixing review findings; the reviewer will tell you), wire in the cost lookup as a one-line change in your vcache-cug.3 work and note it in .3's report. 4. The bead's dependency edge on vcache-cug.1 stays; it is satisfied by 3 for now. 5. Your cug.8 follow-up commit: approved as reported in the pane (519 unit / 426 integration). Push it on your branch if not already, and list R3 "not caught" with its reason in the .2 report.
acceptance_criteria: daemon.single_flight off by default and byte-for-byte today's behaviour when off; unit Section daemon::lease; integration 10b: one compile across two trees, dedup counter 1, holder-failed and holder-gone paths each logged and both trees finish; Fails first recorded; docs/daemon.md Single-flight section; Deploy: vcache

The approved single-request wait-bound calculation and reply metadata are being implemented. Existing production storage exposes a conflict between two binding acceptance items:

- The same-turn holder Put / holder session close interleaving must wake waiters with stored.
- A holder that dies must wake all waiters within one second.

Evidence: src/daemon/server.cc HandlePut calls DiskStorage::Put synchronously, then may call S3Storage::Put synchronously when the memory upload queue cannot hold the blob. A second case where the blocked Put fails (read-only disk via the same seam returning failure) gives exactly one `compile`.
- Mutations: M-grace (wake with compile on close even while a Put is in flight) and M-double (wake on close and again on Put): each must fail one of those tests.

# Reviewer notes on vcache-cug.2 (4f14396), 2026-10-08: approved and merged; fold these into vcache-cug.3

Fix in a small `fix(daemon): …` commit before (or as the first commit of) vcache-cug.3, fail-first where marked, and list them in the .3 report.

1. **F1 (design fix): the feature switches are client-side only.** Today the daemon refuses kLeaseAcquire when its own `daemon.single_flight` is off, and its config comes from whichever client auto-started it; the switch is not in ConfigFingerprint, so enabled trees silently lose single-flight until the daemon restarts, and the client logs the misleading `lease: holder gone`. Decision: the daemon always serves lease (and, in .3, reserve) ops; `daemon.single_flight` / `daemon.admission` only decide whether a client sends them. Remove the daemon-side refusal (keep the fixture's switches, harmless). Test: a daemon started without the switches grants a lease to a client that has single_flight on. If any daemon-side refusal remains for another reason, the client must log it distinctly (`lease: daemon refused (<reason>), compiling`) and keep the session for admission.
2. **F2: waiters poll every 20 ms while holding mutex_** (server.cc around the waiter loop: poll + recv(MSG_PEEK)). With ~400 waiters that is ~20k lock acquisitions per second contending with Get/Put. Wait on the lease's condition variable with the bound as timeout; check the waiter's own socket for disconnect with mutex_ released and at most every 250 ms. Keep "holder death wakes waiters within 1 s".
3. **F3: any completed Put of the key completes the current lease**, even from a client that is not the holder (a recache client, or a waiter that hit its bound and compiled unleased); a failed foreign Put then tells waiters "holder failed" while the holder is still compiling. Complete the lease only on a Put whose SO_PEERCRED pid equals the holder session's pid; when either pid is 0 (foreign pid namespace) keep today's behaviour. Test with two clients: a foreign failing Put leaves waiters waiting; the holder's Put wakes them with stored.
4. **F4: the 300 s bound cap equals the session's SO_RCVTIMEO**, so at the cap the client times out at the same moment and logs "holder gone". Set the client receive timeout to bound + 15 s for lease and reserve waits.
5. **Nits:** a waiter's own disconnect is logged as kBound (log it as `waiter gone`); docs/daemon.md mentions "speculative lookups" which do not exist (remove); unit_test.cc's 75 ms-bound waiter is polled for only 50 ms (give it a 1 s deadline).

title: Memory admission: kMemoryReserve against MemAvailable minus unrealised in-flight reservations
description:
## What

Start a compile or link only when the machine can hold it. Switch: `daemon.admission = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_ADMISSION), default off until .6 has measured it. Replaces each build's start-of-build `-j` guess with one machine-wide view across worktrees.

## Protocol (on the CompileSession from .8)

- `kMemoryReserve(cost_key, estimate_kb, bound_ms)` -> kOk + u8 outcome `granted` | `bound` (proceed unreserved after bound_ms, logged) + u64 waited_ms. The daemon holds the reply while the client waits; the session is dedicated, so holding it blocks nothing else. bound_ms defaults to 10 minutes.
- `kCompilerSpawned(pid)` right after util::Run forks, so the daemon can sample that pid.
- The reservation ends when the session closes (compile done or client gone).

## Admission arithmetic (server)

available_kb = MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo (re-read at most once a second) minus unrealised_kb, where unrealised_kb = sum over in-flight reservations of max(0, estimate_kb - rss_kb(pid)), rss_kb sampled from /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS every 500 ms (0 until kCompilerSpawned). A resident compile is thereby not counted twice against MemAvailable. Grant when available_kb >= estimate_kb. FIFO queue of waiters, granted in order as reservations end or sampled RSS grows. Always at least one reservation in flight: an estimate larger than the machine is granted when nothing else holds one, so nothing deadlocks. Estimate = .1's cost table for the cost key, else daemon.default_compile_kb (default 2097152) / daemon.default_link_kb (default 4194304). v1 may skip RSS sampling and treat the whole estimate as unrealised for its first 10 s; the test seam below must then be respected by both forms.

Test seam: env VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO=<path> makes the daemon read that file instead of /proc/meminfo (undocumented outside tests, like the existing memo paths).

## Counters / status

reserved_kb, realised_kb, reserve waits, longest wait ms; --daemon-status rows "memory reserved / realised / waiting".

## Client

Reserve in RunCompile, RunRustCompile, RunLink after the key (and after a granted lease, if .2 is on: a lease waiter holds no memory) and before the compile; the dep-info and -E runs are not reserved (small). On any daemon error: proceed unreserved and log it (ground rule 1).

## Logging

`reserve: granted <kb> kB after <ms> ms (available <kb>, unrealised <kb>)`, `reserve: waiting (<available> < <estimate>) behind <n>`, `reserve: daemon unavailable, running unreserved`, server log `reserve: <pid> rss <kb> of <estimate>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (new Section "daemon::admission"): grant, refuse, FIFO order, the always-one rule, release on session close, realised RSS reducing the unrealised sum, and the cost-table-else-default estimate.
- Integration (new section "10c. Memory admission"): VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO points at a file with MemAvailable 3 GB, two compiles with 2 GB estimates (seeded cost files): the second logs `reserve: waiting` and is granted only after the first's `lease`/session ends; --daemon-status shows `reserve waits 1`; with the daemon stopped both run unreserved and log it.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md "Memory admission" with the arithmetic and defaults; docs/configuration.md for the keys. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding)

MemoryReservation states:

| State | Event | Next |
|---|---|---|
| none | kMemoryReserve(est) and available >= est, or nothing else reserved | granted (reservations_ += est, rss 0) |
| none | otherwise | queued (FIFO) |
| queued | reservations end / RSS grows / MemAvailable rises so head fits | granted (strict FIFO: a later small request never jumps the head) |
| queued | bound passes | outcome `bound`, client runs unreserved |
| granted | kCompilerSpawned(pid) | sampling that pid every 500 ms |
| granted | pid exits / session closes | released; queue re-evaluated at once |
| granted | sampled RSS > estimate | unrealised 0 for it (never negative); record the overshoot in the daemon log |
| any | daemon restart | all gone; clients see their session end and proceed unreserved |

Same-turn interleavings: a release and a new reserve in the same tick (the release must be applied first); MemAvailable read stale by up to 1 s while three grants happen (the unrealised sum, not MemAvailable, carries the in-flight cost, so this is safe: test three back-to-back reserves against a fake meminfo of 5 GB with 2 GB estimates: grant, grant, queue).

Operational cases: estimate 0 or missing cost record -> default per operation; a link's estimate larger than total RAM -> granted only when alone; /proc/<pid> vanished between samples -> treat as released only on session close, not on a failed read; container clients (pid namespace): SO_PEERCRED gives the daemon-side pid and the client-reported pid may differ: sample the pid the client reports only if it is visible in /proc and its ppid matches the SO_PEERCRED pid; otherwise fall back to the "whole estimate unrealised for 10 s" rule for that reservation and log it.
Mutations: M1 FIFO jump by a small request; M2 count realised RSS against both MemAvailable and unrealised (double count: the three-reserve test queues the second); M3 drop the always-one rule (an over-RAM estimate deadlocks: test with a 1 GB fake meminfo and a 2 GB estimate must grant); M4 release on a failed /proc read; M5 ignore the bound — each must fail a named test.
acceptance_criteria: daemon.admission off by default; unit Section daemon::admission incl. the always-one rule and FIFO order; integration 10c with VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO shows the second compile waiting then granted, and unreserved fallback with the daemon stopped; --daemon-status memory rows; Fails first recorded; docs; Deploy: vcache

Commit b07809113e636b49684280efaaac115f955bc854, fix(daemon): account for compiler descendants during admission, is pushed to origin/feat/sol-daemon-scheduler. This is one follow-up commit after the closed elastic-pool work. It implements F1–F8 and the four nits from the supplied review. Admission remains off by default.     unit: 884 passed, 0 failed

MAKEFLAGS=-j8; compiler masquerade directory removed from PATH; scratch and TMPDIR under /build/richard/codex-1000. Builds, unit runs, mutation runs and the final gate were serialized. Only the five intended paths were staged. No existing assertion was edited except the capped lease timeout assertion, explicitly approved by the user's answer: "Yes, extend headroom and update that assertion". It now requires 915 seconds rather than 315 seconds. The third-party/.dl fixture symlink remains untracked and uncommitted.

F1 was implemented first. ProcessTreeRssKb walks every task's children list recursively and sums VmRSS once per live pid, with saturating addition. The root pidfd remains the confirmed-exit authority, and unrealised memory still clamps realised memory at the estimate. util::Run continues reporting its actual child/driver pid; changing that callback is unnecessary when the daemon samples the entire tree. A fresh executable fixture forks a child that forks the allocator, excluding inherited test-runner RSS that would mask root-only sampling. Before the production change, the new test failed on c62ef79 at the grandchild grant and realised-memory assertions. Evidence: admission-review-tree-before-3.log. The root-only mutation fails those same two assertions.

F2 accumulates memory-queue time on the holder's compile session and subtracts the waiter's overlapping queue time from its lease clock, capped at 600 additional seconds. Grant, expiry and shutdown end the interval and notify the holder's lease waiters. Logs retain total elapsed wait and add the capped paused duration. A 100ms lease waiter receives no reply during a 250ms holder queue, then receives exactly one stored reply after release and a production Put. Client receive headroom includes the additional 600 seconds plus the existing 15-second margin; the maximum is 915 seconds. This headroom and the one existing assertion update were explicitly approved by the user.

F3 reads MemAvailable before every RSS sampling batch, including a spawn batch. A fake meminfo drop simultaneous with newly visible RSS must prevent a second reservation from fitting under the stale value. If a refresh fails after a good reading, new sampled RSS realisation is deferred rather than netted against stale memory. The existing ten-second invisible-pid assumption is preserved independently of read failure.

F4 snapshots shared reservation identities under the mutex, reads the trees and pidfds with the mutex released, then applies only results whose reservation object still matches. Replacement notifications install a new object, so old samples cannot overwrite its state and the old pidfd remains owned until the sample finishes. A spawn samples only that new tree. The periodic worker forces its 500ms pass, so a spawn does not postpone the next periodic sample to one second. Steady RSS writes no per-tick logs; overshoots and release peaks are logged outside the shared mutex. A FIFO-paused sample leaves a separate status request responsive within 250ms, a trace fixture proves each spawn samples only its own tree, and the release summary appears after the steady-period no-log assertion.

F5 emits one warning through the lifecycle logger, which also feeds VCACHE_LOG, and retains the last good MemAvailable. Without any good reading, admission is unavailable and concurrent reserve requests are granted rather than silently serialised. Tests cover both initial failure and loss after a good value, plus exactly one warning over repeated sampling ticks.

F6 refuses to start the worker after stop_requested_, moves its thread handle under the mutex during Shutdown, then joins that local handle outside the mutex. A received reserve pauses before admission; a real kShutdown RPC proceeds through worker teardown; the reserve resumes afterward. The daemon must return its drain reply and exit zero, rather than SIGABRT. The omitted-check mutation produces "terminate called without an active exception" and fails the named exit assertion.

F7 logs granted estimate and waited_ms in the requesting client's own VCACHE_LOG. A separate client log test queues behind another process's reservation, releases it and checks the grant text in that client's file.

F8 adds the stronger discriminating test rather than editing the existing assertion. It uses a visible, live child, disables pidfd opening with a test seam, and forces the tree status read to fail. Its reservation must remain held and the next request queued. The actual failed-read erase mutation fails this test. This corrects and supersedes the earlier final report's M4 claim: its invisible-pid fixture and earlier mutation guarded conservative namespace fallback, not the visible-pid failed-read sampling branch. That original guard remains intact; it is no longer cited as proof of the latter branch.

Nits: visible-child validation now requires a positive peer pid, preventing PPid zero from validating an unknown namespace peer; the reservation field is realised_kb because it may hold the fallback assumption; forced periodic sampling fixes the initial one-second gap; AddKb is renamed SaturatingAddKb. The status label memory realised and its intended units/meaning are preserved.

| Shared path / behavior | Before | After | New failure modes or limits | Mutation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compiler RSS / util::Run root notification | Sample only the driver; callback reports its child pid | Callback unchanged; daemon sums the live process tree | Proc snapshots are approximate and more reads are needed; shared resident pages can appear in multiple processes' VmRSS, as required by the sum rule | M-root-only-rss |
| Holder memory queue / lease wait | Queue time consumed the lease bound | Overlapping holder queue time pauses it, capped at 600s | Waiting wrappers can hold their build slot longer; elapsed wall time and pause length are logged | M-lease-ignores-memory-queue |

| UpdateAdmission / cache request mutex | Proc reads and RSS logs held the global lock | Snapshot, unlock for reads/logs, relock and apply matching identities | A sample can become obsolete after close/replacement; obsolete results are discarded and pidfd ownership survives the read | R-sample-under-lock |
| Spawn / worker cadence | Every spawn forced a pass over every reservation and could postpone the next sample | Only the new tree is sampled at spawn; worker forces its periodic pass | Spawn still waits for an existing batch, while unrelated cache requests retain mutex access | R-spawn-full-pass |

All builds, tests and mutations ran serially with MAKEFLAGS=-j8, the compiler masquerade directory
removed from PATH, and TMPDIR/scratch under /build/richard/codex-1000. Six explicit source, test and
documentation paths were staged. The authorized third-party/.dl fixture remains untracked and was
not committed. No existing test assertion was edited.

N1 uses the review's permitted daemon-side maximum: each released reservation contributes its
sampled peak sum of live-process VmRSS to a memory-only table indexed by cost key. Both confirmed
compiler exit and session close retain that observation. Before granting, the FIFO head takes
max(client estimate, observed tree peak). This includes a request that was already queued before
the earlier observation was released. Replacement compiler notifications carry the cost identity
and sampled peak forward. An unrelated key is unaffected, a larger client estimate remains larger,
and a tree shrinking after its peak cannot lower the next estimate.

The on-disk cost records and --show-costs retain wait4 ru_maxrss, the peak of the largest descendant.
The daemon estimate is in kB and covers its observed simultaneous tree sum. Documentation explicitly
distinguishes those two measurements and says admission measurements use the daemon's granted
estimate and sampled tree sum. The tree-peak table is never journalled and dies with the daemon;
after restart, estimates initially use the existing client cost/default until a new tree is
observed. This is the allowed daemon-side alternative, not a cost-record schema redesign.

N2 treats a descendant with unreadable/missing VmRSS as zero while continuing the rest of the
walk, including other live descendants. A root failure still voids the sample, preserving prior
realisation and the existing no-release-on-read-failure rule. On this kernel a zombie has no VmRSS,
so the fixture leaves one child exited and unreaped with waitid(WNOWAIT) while another branch's
grandchild holds 48 MiB. That allocation must still realise the driver reservation and grant the
next job. Reinstating the old whole-tree failure catches this exact zombie case.

N3 extracts LeaseWaitDeadline and MemoryReserveDeadline as pure helpers used by the real handlers.
The lease helper caps the ordinary bound at 300 seconds and overlapping holder queue time at
600 seconds; negative queue durations contribute zero. Tests cover the inclusive cap, one
millisecond over it, and a full day of holder queue time combined with UINT64_MAX requested bound.
The maximum lease deadline remains started+900 seconds, matching the previously approved
915-second receive timeout with its margin. The reserve helper caps every requested bound at
600000 ms, including UINT64_MAX. A real queued reserve logs that computed bound on a separate
reserve: line; the specified waiting line is preserved. A mutation bypassing the helper fails
the real-server log assertion, proving the helper is wired into the handler. No test waits
600 seconds: the long-bound arithmetic is tested directly and the real queue is released promptly.

N4 removes the written-but-unread meminfo_read_at_ member. N5 emits only the first overshoot while

# Final logging and elastic fixture follow-up — 2026-10-08

Commit: `c165dd528e7a2dc7eeb1f7d1001bdc51ca66a9c0`. Branch: `feat/sol-daemon-scheduler` (local `ntm/vcache/cod_1`).
Merged `origin/main` by fast-forward to `637ae8c` before the fix. The change is one fix commit as requested, with no deployment.

L2: the client requests the daemon's actual granted estimate and logs it, including learned tree peaks and an already held reservation returned by a duplicate request. The optional request byte selects a reply containing granted kB (zero on a bounded wait). Legacy requests retain their exact reply format. A new client retries the legacy request after an older daemon rejects the extension, retaining admission and labeling the unavailable estimate as requested.

L6: the fake compiler writes a separate snapshot and publishes it with an atomic rename. Writers serialize through a stable `counter.lock` file so replacing the counter inode cannot invalidate their lock. A FIFO pauses the first writer after truncation and before writing; the reader must still see the preceding complete snapshot. The barrier is bounded at five seconds and the parent polls with a deadline. Existing assertions were preserved.

## Validation and fails first

Serialized builds and tests used `MAKEFLAGS=-j8`, scratch TMPDIR, and PATH without `/usr/lib64/ccache`.

| Shared path | Before | After | New failure modes and guard |

| `CompileSessionHandle::ReserveMemory` grant log | Printed the caller's estimate even when a learned tree peak was granted. | Prints the granted kB returned by the daemon. | An absent or invalid estimate in an opted-in reply is rejected, closes the session, and continues unreserved through the existing fallback. title: Jobserver mode: a fixed fifo job-slot pool that ninja, make and cargo draw from
description:
## What

The daemon owns one GNU-make-style fifo job-slot pool for every build on the machine. Verified locally: ninja 1.13.2 follows `MAKEFLAGS=--jobserver-auth=fifo:PATH` when no -j is given on its command line (POSIX fifo form only; -l load limits still apply); GNU make 4.4.1 implements the fifo protocol; cargo 1.97 and rustc use the jobserver crate (.5 verifies the fifo form with strace before any sibling repo relies on it). This bead is the fixed-size pool; .7 makes it elastic.

## Behaviour

- `daemon.jobserver = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER) and `daemon.jobserver_jobs = N` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER_JOBS, default: online CPUs). On start the daemon creates `<state dir>/jobserver.fifo` (mkfifo 0600, same ownership rules as the socket) and writes N tokens ('+' bytes, as make does). It keeps a read-write fd open so the fifo never sees EOF.
- `vcache --jobserver-env` prints `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:<path>` (and nothing else, exit 1 when no daemon or jobserver is running) for a build script to export. The `-j` with no count is what tells make it is a jobserver client.
- --stop-daemon removes the fifo; --daemon-status shows `jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn` (withdrawn is 0 until .7).
- A build started with the MAKEFLAGS but no daemon falls back to the tools' own defaults (ninja warns and uses its default -j; document that).

## Logging

`jobserver: pool <path> with <N> tokens`, `jobserver: removed <path>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (Section "daemon::jobserver"): fifo creation and removal, token count written, --jobserver-env output format.
- Integration (new section "10d. Jobserver"): with the daemon started with jobserver_jobs=2, a Makefile of 6 targets whose recipe is a fake compiler that sleeps 1 s and records its concurrent peers in a shared counter file; `make` under the exported MAKEFLAGS never records more than 2 peers; the same with a tiny build.ninja and `ninja` (no -j). Without the daemon the same make runs 6 wide.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md "Jobserver mode" with the version requirements and the exported line; docs/configuration.md keys. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Long-lived state: the fifo `<state dir>/jobserver.fifo` and its N tokens, owned by the daemon process.

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| daemon not running | `--start-daemon` with daemon.jobserver | fifo created 0600 (mkfifo), daemon opens it O_RDWR (never sees EOF) and writes N '+' bytes | log `jobserver: pool <path> with <N> tokens` |
| running | client reads a token | N-1 in fifo (client holds one) | |
| running | client writes it back | N | |
| running | client crashes holding a token | token lost until daemon restart (same as make); documented, not fixed in this bead | |
| running | `--stop-daemon` / idle exit | fifo removed after the listen socket closes | log `jobserver: removed <path>` |
| a stale fifo from a crashed daemon | next start | recreated (remove the stale path first; it is ours by construction: in our state dir, a fifo) | |
| daemon.jobserver false | start | no fifo (unchanged behaviour) | |

Idle exit: a build blocked reading the fifo is not a socket client; the daemon must not exit idle while tokens are out (fifo bytes < N, check with FIONREAD on the daemon's fd) — keep it running until all tokens are back or the idle timeout passes twice.

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Daemon without jobserver | as today | identical |
| `vcache --jobserver-env` | n/a | prints exactly `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:<abs path>` + newline, exit 0; exit 1 with a message on stderr when no daemon or no jobserver |

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| jobserver_jobs = 0 or negative | config warning, use online CPUs |
| Path too long / unwritable state dir | log, run without the jobserver, `--jobserver-env` exits 1 |
| A client that writes back more tokens than it took | pool grows; document that a misbehaving client can do this (make has the same property) |
| ninja given `-j` explicitly | ignores the fifo (ninja's documented rule); docs say so |
| Pipe-form MAKEFLAGS (`--jobserver-auth=R,W`) in the environment | not produced by us; docs note ninja ignores it |

Naming: config `daemon.jobserver`, `daemon.jobserver_jobs`; env `VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER`, `VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER_JOBS`; CLI `--jobserver-env`; status rows `jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn` (withdrawn 0 until the elastic bead); file `src/daemon/jobserver.{h,cc}` with `class JobserverPool`.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `daemon::jobserver`): JobserverPool creates a fifo at a scratch path with exactly N bytes readable (FIONREAD); taking and returning a token changes the count by one; destroying the pool removes the path; a stale fifo at the path is replaced.
Integration (section `10d. Jobserver`): start the daemon with `VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER=1 VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER_JOBS=2`; a Makefile with 6 independent targets whose recipe runs a script that does `flock` on a counter file, increments it, records the max seen, sleeps 1 s (the sleep is the workload, not synchronisation), decrements; `env $(vcache --jobserver-env) make` (no -j on the command line): recorded max = 2. Same with a 6-edge build.ninja and `ninja` (skip if `ninja --version` < 1.13): max = 2. Control: plain `make -j6` without the env: max = 6. `--stop-daemon` removes the fifo (`test ! -p`).

Mutations: M1 write N-1 tokens: max becomes 1, the make test fails; M2 open the fifo O_WRONLY only: the daemon's own reads/FIONREAD fail or clients see EOF; unit fails; M3 forget to remove the fifo on stop: the `test ! -p` check fails; M4 print the pipe form instead of fifo: the ninja case fails (ninja ignores it, max = default); M5 exit idle while tokens are out: add a test that holds a token through a short idle timeout and asserts the daemon is still alive; it must fail.
acceptance_criteria: daemon.jobserver off by default; fifo created/removed with the daemon; --jobserver-env prints the MAKEFLAGS line or exits 1; integration 10d: make and ninja (no -j) under the exported MAKEFLAGS never exceed jobserver_jobs concurrent fake compiles, and run wide without the daemon; Fails first recorded; docs; Deploy: vcache
close_reason: 94baa8d: a jobserver fifo is removed only when it is still ours

comments.text:
# Stopped 2026-10-08: N tokens and max=N contradict on make 4.4.1 and ninja 1.13.2

The pool, `--jobserver-env`, status rows, fifo removal and the idle-twice rule are implemented and the unit section `daemon::jobserver` passes. Integration `10d` passes every check except the concurrency cap.

Measured here, GNU Make 4.4.1 and `/usr/bin/ninja` 1.13.2, with the fifo held open read-write and the printed line `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:PATH`:

| tokens in the fifo | make max | ninja max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2 | (not the failing case) |
| 2 | 3 | 3 |

Both clients run `tokens + 1` jobs. GNU make's own server, and ninja's `misc/jobserver_pool.py`, write `jobs_count - 1` bytes for that reason: the client counts one implicit slot.

With `VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER_JOBS=2` this daemon writes 2 '+' bytes, and section 10d reports:

- `make under the jobserver never exceeds 2 (expected '2', got '3')`
- `ninja under the jobserver never exceeds 2 (expected '2', got '3')`

The bead asks for both "write N tokens" (unit: FIONREAD == N) and "max = 2" (integration). Those cannot both hold on these tools.

Also, `env $(vcache --jobserver-env)` word-splits the line, so make only sees `MAKEFLAGS=-j` and ignores the fifo (max 6). The test quotes the assignment. PATH `ninja` on this host is a wrapper that appends `-j 56`, which makes ninja ignore the fifo; the test calls `/usr/bin/ninja`.

Not committed. Bead left in progress.

Recommendation: write N-1 tokens so make and ninja run N jobs, and expect FIONREAD == N-1. The printed MAKEFLAGS line stays as specified.

# vcache-cug.4 report (2026-10-08)

## Commits

- `72f6649a7c36f21c1e69f34fcc49da1fe91729c3` on `feat/grok-defects-costs-jobserver` (after `c100efe`).

## Tests

- Unit `daemon::jobserver`: MAKEFLAGS line, stale fifo replaced, mode 0600, fifo holds slots-1 bytes and reports N jobs free, take/return changes the count by one, destructor removes the path, explicit 0 and negative `jobserver_jobs` warn and fall back to online CPUs.
- Integration `10d. Jobserver`: off by default and `--jobserver-env` exits 1; with jobs=2 the fifo exists, status total/free/withdrawn are 2/2/0, the MAKEFLAGS line is exact; make and `/usr/bin/ninja` stay at 2; `make -j6` reaches 6; stop removes the fifo; a held token past one idle timeout leaves the daemon alive.

Last full run before the mutation reverts (source matches this commit):

```
unit: 548 passed, 0 failed
integration: 406 passed, 0 failed
```

## Deviations

- The fifo is filled with `jobserver_jobs - 1` '+' bytes, not N. GNU Make 4.4.1 and ninja 1.13.2 both run `bytes + 1` jobs: a client started from MAKEFLAGS counts one slot as already taken. Writing N bytes made section 10d report max 3 for jobs=2. `total()` is the configured slot count; `free_tokens()` is `fifo_bytes() + 1`, so an idle pool reports free == total. A one-slot pool writes no byte, so a lone job is not visible to the idle check.
- `env $(vcache --jobserver-env)` word-splits on the space, so the test quotes the assignment. Unquoted, make only sees `MAKEFLAGS=-j` and runs 6 wide.
- PATH `ninja` here is a wrapper that appends `-j 56`, which makes ninja ignore the fifo. The test calls `/usr/bin/ninja` 1.13.2.
- An explicit 0 or a negative job count warns. The unset default is 0 meaning online CPUs and does not warn.
- Jobserver settings are not part of the daemon config fingerprint, so a compile that did not set `VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER` is not refused.

## Before / after

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Daemon start, jobserver off | unchanged | no fifo |
| Daemon start, jobserver on | n/a | mkfifo 0600 at `<state>/jobserver.fifo`, held O_RDWR, slots-1 '+' bytes, log `jobserver: pool <path> with <N> tokens` |
| Stale fifo in the state dir | n/a | replaced |
| `--jobserver-env` | n/a | `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:<abs path>\n`, or exit 1 on stderr when no daemon or no pool |
| `--stop-daemon` / shutdown | socket removed | fifo removed after the listen socket, log `jobserver: removed <path>` |
| Idle exit | one idle timeout with no socket client | two timeouts while `free_tokens() < total()` |
| `--daemon-status` | existing rows | plus `jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn` (withdrawn 0) when a pool exists |

New failure modes:

- mkfifo, chmod, open or the token write can fail. The daemon still listens and logs `jobserver: not started (<why>)`. `--jobserver-env` then exits 1.
- A client that writes extra '+' bytes grows the pool (same as make). A client that dies holding a byte loses it until restart.
- FIONREAD failing makes `free_tokens()` negative; the status prints `unknown` and the idle check treats the pool as not full (the comparison is `<`).

## Mutations

| Id | Change | Test | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | write `slots` bytes instead of `slots-1` | unit and integration 10d | `the fifo holds slots-1 bytes and reports N jobs free`; `make under the jobserver never exceeds 2 (expected '2', got '3')` (ninja the same, got 3) |
| M2 | open the fifo `O_WRONLY` | unit | `a stale fifo is replaced (open ... No such device or address)` |
| M3 | destructor does not remove the path | unit | `destroying the pool removes the fifo` |
| M4 | print `--jobserver-auth=3,4` | integration 10d | `ninja under the jobserver never exceeds 2 (expected '2', got '6')` and ninja's `Pipe-based protocol is not supported` |
| M5 | one idle timeout even with a token out | integration 10d | `the daemon stays up while a token is out past one idle timeout (expected 'yes', got '')` |

- `JobserverMakeFlagsLine`
- `JobserverPool::fifo_bytes`, `free_tokens` (fifo bytes plus the implicit slot), `total` (configured slots)
- `Server::StartJobserver`

- None. Cargo's fifo client is vcache-cug.5, not this bead.

# Reviewer findings on vcache-cug.4 (72f6649), 2026-10-08: two fixes, then merge

Reopened. Do this in one follow-up commit right after the vcache-cug.1 fixes, before the defect beads. Fail-first tests for F2; record `Fails first:` lines. Your N-1 bytes choice is correct (make and ninja each count one implicit slot) and stays.

- **F1 (document, no code change).** Each top-level jobserver client (make, ninja, cargo) holds one implicit slot, so the pool caps concurrent jobs at N-1 shared + 1 per concurrent top-level build (measured with N=2: one make 2, two makes 3, three makes 4). Say exactly that in docs/daemon.md "Jobserver mode" and in docs/configuration.md for `daemon.jobserver_jobs` (replace "the number of '+' tokens" with "total slots N; the fifo holds N-1 tokens because each client already owns one"). Make the start log line say `jobserver: pool <path> with <N> slots (<N-1> tokens)`.
- **F2 (fix).** `~JobserverPool` (src/daemon/jobserver.cc) removes the fifo by path without checking it is still ours. Reproduced: start daemon A, rename the cache dir, start daemon B; A notices its socket is gone, exits, and deletes B's new fifo; B keeps advertising a dead path and `--jobserver-env` prints it. Fix: record `st_dev`/`st_ino` at open, `lstat` before removing and remove only when they match (mirror how Shutdown checks the socket inode). `--jobserver-env` prints the line only when the path is a fifo (`S_ISFIFO`); otherwise exit 1 with a message. title: Elastic jobserver pool: withdraw free tokens under memory pressure, restore when it clears
description:
## What

Make the jobserver pool from .4 elastic under memory pressure, using the admission view from .3. A token sitting in the fifo is a slot nobody is using, so the daemon can shrink the pool by reading free tokens back out and grow it by writing them back; a token held by a running job is never touched (the job returns it itself).

## Policy v1

Every 500 ms (the same tick that samples RSS): if there are reservations waiting in the admission queue, withdraw min(free tokens, waiting reservations) tokens; when the queue is empty and available_kb exceeds the largest default estimate, restore withdrawn tokens one per tick. Never withdraw below `daemon.jobserver_min_jobs` (default 2). The policy is one function over (free, withdrawn, waiting, available_kb) so it can be unit-tested and replaced.

## Counters / status

jobserver tokens withdrawn (now live), tokens restored total; --daemon-status shows them.

## Logging

`jobserver: withdrew <n> tokens (waiting <n>, available <kb> kB)`, `jobserver: restored <n> tokens`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit: the policy function on a table of (free, withdrawn, waiting, available) -> action rows, including the minimum floor and the one-per-tick restore.
- Integration (extends "10d"): jobserver_jobs=4, VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO at 3 GB, fake compiles with 2 GB estimates under make: the peer counter never exceeds 2 while reservations wait, and returns to 4 after they drain; both `jobserver: withdrew` and `jobserver: restored` appear in the daemon log.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md: the elastic policy and its floor. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding)

Pool state: total N (config), free F (FIONREAD on the daemon fd), withdrawn W (held by the daemon, not in the fifo), in use U = N - F - W.

| Event (per 500 ms tick) | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| reservations waiting Q > 0 | F > 0 and N - W > jobserver_min_jobs | read min(F, Q, N - W - min_jobs) tokens out of the fifo (non-blocking read on the daemon's fd); W += that |
| Q = 0 | W > 0 and available_kb > max(default_compile_kb, default_link_kb) | write 1 token back; W -= 1 |
| daemon stop | W > 0 | write W back before removing the fifo (clients mid-read must not hang on a fifo that loses tokens) |

Invariants: W never exceeds N - min_jobs; tokens in use are never touched (only free tokens are read); after all reservations drain and memory recovers, W returns to 0 within W ticks.
Operational cases: a client reads the last free token in the same tick the daemon tries to withdraw (the non-blocking read returns EAGAIN: no withdraw, retry next tick); min_jobs > N (clamp to N, warn); jobserver on but admission off (no Q signal: the pool stays fixed; say so in docs).
Mutations: M1 withdraw below min_jobs; M2 blocking read on withdraw (daemon tick stalls: a test with F = 0 must still tick within 1 s); M3 restore all at once; M4 forget to return W on stop (a client blocked in read hangs: test with a 2 s timeout); M5 withdraw when admission is off — each must fail a named test.
acceptance_criteria: policy function unit-tested on a table incl. the jobserver_min_jobs floor and one-per-tick restore; integration 10d extension shows the ceiling drop to 2 while reservations wait and return to 4 after; withdrew/restored log lines and status rows; Fails first recorded; docs; Deploy: vcache

Commits: bb92e65 (merge of reviewed origin/main prerequisites, including the FIFO inode-ownership fix) and c62ef79161e3bfc4c2690a261be745f37985a423 (elastic pool), pushed to origin/feat/sol-daemon-scheduler from the own ntm worktree. The incoming tracked bead change was included only as part of the authorized merge; feature staging used ten explicit source, test and documentation paths. The untracked third-party/.dl symlink is the authorized shared build fixture and was not committed. No deployment or main push was performed.

Final gate evidence: /build/richard/codex-1000/elastic-complete-final-gate.log, ending with:

    unit: 829 passed, 0 failed
    integration: 795 passed, 0 failed

All builds and tests were serialized, with MAKEFLAGS=-j8, the compiler masquerade path removed, and scratch under /build/richard/codex-1000. No existing test assertion was edited. No cache key, protocol version, persistent stats format or existing status-row meaning changed. Jobserver free remains FIFO bytes plus one implicit slot; withdrawn is now the live daemon-owned count, as planned. Restored total is a new lifetime row.

Implementation: the pure JobserverTokenChange function consumes total, raw FIFO free bytes, withdrawn count, queue length, available kilobytes, minimum jobs and the largest default estimate. Every 500 ms, the existing admission worker withdraws min(F, Q, N-W-floor) when Q is positive, and restores one token only when Q is zero and available memory strictly exceeds the largest default estimate. Withdraw and Restore update ownership from actual nonblocking I/O. A stolen last free token yields EAGAIN without blocking the worker. The daemon starts the same worker for an enabled pool even when its starter has admission off, preserving the approved client-only feature switches. With no admission requests there is no withdrawal signal and the pool stays fixed.

Tests added:

- Unit table: one waiter, floor reached, floor already reached, client-held tokens, no free tokens, unknown free count, one-token recovery, equal-threshold no recovery, below-threshold no recovery, empty-queue fixed pool, and floor above total.
- Production JobserverPool fixtures: actual withdrawn/restored counters, move ownership, move assignment returning the old destination's tokens before closing its FIFO, and teardown returning tokens to a genuinely blocked reader within two seconds.
- Exact same-turn race: compute a withdrawal from the free-byte snapshot, let a client consume the last free bytes, then attempt withdrawal in a bounded child. Its result must be zero within one second. This catches a blocking descriptor rather than only the policy's F=0 early return.
- Configuration: TOML floor, environment override, and show-config description.
- Integration section 10d: real daemon processes, the production FIFO writer, production compile-cost writer, real make and real gcc behind FIFO barriers. Four-slot pool, 3GiB meminfo and 2GiB estimates; queue/status/log assertions show two shared tokens withdrawn to the two-job floor. A direct admission-enabled make scenario releases successive compiler barriers and checks each newly free token is withdrawn while the queue remains nonempty. Compiler peers never exceed two under pressure; after recovery a new admission-enabled make phase reaches four. A separate admission-off make phase measures the elastic CPU pool at two while other wrappers provide admission pressure, then at four after recovery.
- Integration also covers daemon-started-off/client-enabled requests, shutdown returning two tokens to an existing FIFO reader, admission-off fixed width four, floor above N warning/clamp, live/lifetime rows, preserved compiler outputs/exit codes, and daemon-held tokens retaining the ordinary idle timeout.

All test waits use condition polling with deadlines or FIFO/pipe barriers. Commands, fixture compilers, child reads, process cleanup and the overall integration driver have deadlines. VCACHE_LOG and --daemon-status are asserted in every integration scenario, beyond compiler exit codes. Action-count assertions select the direct marker; the lifecycle logger also emits its existing daemon-prefixed decision-log copy.

Fail-first evidence: pre-feature bb92e65 was exported and built in scratch. The current production cost writer generated its fixtures. elastic-integration-before.log failed the floor/status/width-two/restoration/clamp assertions. elastic-make-admission-before.log failed "ending a make compile withdraws its newly free token", "make compilers never exceed two while pressure holds the floor", "drained make pressure restores both shared tokens", the peak-two assertion and the combined decision log. The final direct-make driver passed in elastic-make-admission-after-2.log. Other new guards have the named failing mutations below, recorded in the commit's Fails first lines.

Adjacent fixes: pool move operations carry daemon-owned tokens and lifetime counters; move assignment and destruction return previously owned tokens before FIFO closure/removal. Status snapshots, idle inspection and shutdown pool reset now share the admission mutex because the sampling thread mutates token ownership. Idle computes client-held slots after adding back daemon-held tokens, so daemon withdrawals do not falsely double the existing client idle timeout. Actual shutdown restores all W before removing the owned FIFO; existing session shutdown and ordinary-request/upload drain remain in force. The merged inode-ownership protection was preserved.

| Shared path / behavior | Before | After | New failure modes or practical limits | Mutation / fail-first |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Jobserver pressure policy | Fixed N-1 shared bytes | Withdraw unused bytes while Q>0, bounded by F and N-W-floor | Sampling can lag pressure by 500ms; running jobs and implicit slots cannot be preempted | M1-floor; R-no-withdrawal; pre-feature make pressure |
| Free-byte snapshot and read | Pool initialization writes once; clients own reads | Daemon also performs nonblocking reads and counts actual bytes | A client can consume bytes after the snapshot; EAGAIN leaves W unchanged until a later tick | M2-blocking-read; R-free-limit |
| Recovery policy | No daemon-held tokens | Q=0 and strictly sufficient available memory restores one per tick | An empty queue alone does not recover W; insufficient RAM retains the reduced pool | M3-restore-all; R-memory-threshold |
| Admission worker with a pool | Started only for an admission request | Also starts for an enabled pool; uses the same 500ms tick | Adds a sampling worker to fixed pools, but no requests means no withdrawal | M5-admission-off |
| Pool moves / replacement / destruction | Transfers FIFO descriptor ownership | Also transfers W and restored total, returning old destination ownership first | Losing ownership would strand build slots; nonblocking I/O preserves progress rather than hanging teardown | R-move-owner; R-move-assignment; M4-stop-return-unit |
| Status / counters | Total, FIFO-plus-implicit free, withdrawn zero | Same total/free meaning, live W and new lifetime restored total, snapshotted under mutex | Counters represent actual completed I/O; a concurrent client can immediately change the reported free snapshot | R-counter; R-status |
| Server shutdown | Remove owned FIFO, close sessions, drain ordinary requests/uploads | Return all W before pool removal, then retain session and ordinary drain behavior | Abrupt process death cannot return memory-only W; orderly shutdown must return tokens to existing readers | M4-stop-return; M4-stop-return-unit |
| Server Idle / idle limit | Client-held FIFO tokens double idle timeout | Client-held tokens retain that rule; daemon-held W does not extend it | Daemon may exit with W>0 after clients finish, so its teardown return is required | R-idle-owner |
| Floor configuration / description | No elastic floor | Positive TOML/env floor defaults to two; above N clamps with warning; show-config displays request | A floor equal to N disables withdrawal; invalid positive-integer inputs retain the prior value | R-floor-toml; R-floor-env; R-floor-description; R-clamp-warning |

# Final logging and elastic fixture follow-up — 2026-10-08

Commit: `c165dd528e7a2dc7eeb1f7d1001bdc51ca66a9c0`. Branch: `feat/sol-daemon-scheduler` (local `ntm/vcache/cod_1`).
Merged `origin/main` by fast-forward to `637ae8c` before the fix. The change is one fix commit as requested, with no deployment.

L2: the client requests the daemon's actual granted estimate and logs it, including learned tree peaks and an already held reservation returned by a duplicate request. The optional request byte selects a reply containing granted kB (zero on a bounded wait). Legacy requests retain their exact reply format. A new client retries the legacy request after an older daemon rejects the extension, retaining admission and labeling the unavailable estimate as requested.

L6: the fake compiler writes a separate snapshot and publishes it with an atomic rename. Writers serialize through a stable `counter.lock` file so replacing the counter inode cannot invalidate their lock. A FIFO pauses the first writer after truncation and before writing; the reader must still see the preceding complete snapshot. The barrier is bounded at five seconds and the parent polls with a deadline. Existing assertions were preserved.

## Before/after and new failure modes

| Shared path | Before | After | New failure modes and guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CompileSessionHandle::ReserveMemory` grant log | Printed the caller's estimate even when a learned tree peak was granted. | Prints the granted kB returned by the daemon. | An absent or invalid estimate in an opted-in reply is rejected, closes the session, and continues unreserved through the existing fallback. Learned-grant check; R-client-log-requested and R-omit-granted-field. |
