title: CompileSession: one held connection per in-flight compile, protocol version 2
description:
## What

The shared scaffolding that single-flight (.2) and memory admission (.3) both build on, landed once so neither has to guess which comes first: a CompileSession, i.e. one held connection per in-flight compile, and protocol version 2.

## Protocol

- kProtocolVersion 1 -> 2. An old daemon refuses a v2 client at hello and the client falls back in-process; a v1 client is refused by a v2 daemon the same way (today's rule, unchanged).
- New op `Op::kSessionOpen` (after kHello on a fresh connection): marks the connection as a CompileSession. Reply kOk. Later ops on it (added by .2 and .3) may have their reply held by the daemon while the client waits; every held reply has a client-side bound and the daemon never holds a reply on a non-session connection.
- The session ends when the client closes the socket (outputs restored, compile failed, or the client died). Everything a session holds (added by .2 and .3) is released then.
- DaemonClient::OpenCompileSession(config) returns a session object whose destructor closes it; RoundTrip's one-connection-per-request behaviour is unchanged for Get/Put.

## Server

Sessions are tracked in Server::sessions_ (fd, client pid from SO_PEERCRED, opened_at). Shutdown closes sessions immediately with Status::kError "daemon shutting down" instead of waiting on them; Idle() counts an open session as a client; kMaxConnections = 1024 still bounds sessions plus requests, which covers -j-many compiles. Counter: sessions open; --daemon-status row "compile sessions N".

## Client

RunCompile, RunRustCompile and RunLink open a session only when daemon.single_flight or daemon.admission is on (both off: no session, no new connection, so a daemon-off or unaware build is byte-for-byte today's). On any session error the compile proceeds as if there were no daemon and logs `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing`.

## Logging

`session: opened`, `session: closed after <ms> ms`, `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (Section "daemon::session"): a v1 hello is refused by a v2 daemon with the version named; a session survives a request on another connection; closing the fd ends the session; Shutdown with an open session returns without waiting the 60 s.
- Integration (new section "10a. Compile sessions"): with daemon.single_flight on and a running daemon, one compile logs `session: opened` and `session: closed`; with the daemon stopped mid-compile the compile still finishes and logs `session: daemon unavailable`; `compile sessions 0` in --daemon-status after the run.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md: a "Compile sessions" paragraph under the protocol description. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding)

State of one CompileSession:

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | client opens socket, kHello v2 ok, kSessionOpen | open (sessions_ has fd, pid via SO_PEERCRED, opened_at) | client log `session: opened` |
| open | client closes fd | closed; everything it holds released (leases, reservations, added later) | daemon log line; client `session: closed after <ms> ms` |
| open | client process killed | same as close (the kernel closes the fd); the session thread sees EOF/ECONNRESET | |
| open | daemon Shutdown | daemon sends kError "daemon shutting down" if a reply is pending, closes fd; does not wait 60 s for it | client proceeds in-process, logs `session: daemon unavailable (daemon shutting down), continuing` |
| open | idle timer | Idle() returns false while any session is open | |
| none | v1 client hello to v2 daemon | refused, reason names both versions | client falls back (unchanged rule) |
| none | daemon absent / refused | no session; compile proceeds | `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing` once per compile |

Operational cases: `-j128` worktree build = up to 128 sessions plus requests, below kMaxConnections = 1024 (state it in docs); a client that opens a session then never sends anything holds one thread until it closes (no timeout in this bead: a compile can legitimately take an hour); two sessions from one pid (link and compile in one process? vcache is one process per invocation, so at most one; assert it).
Mutations: M1 keep kProtocolVersion 1: the v1-refused unit test fails; M2 Shutdown waits on sessions: the "Shutdown returns promptly" test fails (bound it at 2 s); M3 Idle() ignores sessions: a test that holds a session over a 1 s idle timeout and expects the daemon alive fails; M4 open a session when both switches are off: the integration test asserting no `session:` line with both off fails; M5 leave the fd in sessions_ after close: `compile sessions 0` assertion fails.
acceptance_criteria: kProtocolVersion == 2; unit Section daemon::session (v1 refused, session survives other requests, fd close ends it, Shutdown does not wait); integration 10a logs session: opened/closed and daemon-unavailable fallback; compile sessions row in --daemon-status; Fails first recorded; Deploy: vcache

Reviewer note on vcache-cug.8 (09d71ce): approved for merge. Fold these into vcache-cug.2's first commit (or a small fix commit before it), with fail-first tests where marked, and list them in .2's report:
1. Shutdown can accept a session after the broadcast: kSessionOpen only refuses on stop_requested_, which SIGTERM and the socket-replaced path never set. title: Single-flight: a lease waiter with no cost record gives up after 30 s and recompiles
description:
## What
`src/daemon/client.cc` bounds a lease wait at 30 s when the key has no cost record (else max(30 s, 2 x recorded wall)). On cold multi-worktree builds the waiter on the longest compile (an 83 s Rust crate, a 29 s C++ test TU) gives up at 30 s and compiles the key itself, adding the full 30 s to its critical path. docs/daemon.md "Results" shows single_flight making cold Rust builds 10-30 s slower for this reason.

## Fix direction
While the holder's session is still open and alive, keep waiting (the holder is making progress); bound only on holder death or a much larger ceiling. Keep the existing caps on the client receive timeout consistent.

## Acceptance
A test where the holder compiles for longer than 30 s with no cost record: the waiter takes the holder's result and does not compile. Re-run the bench's 2-worktree cold Rust row: single_flight no slower than off.
close_reason: Fixed: no-record lease waits up to the reply timeout

title: cxx key: an unkeyed .gch that appears or is rebuilt with its header unchanged is invisible to the -E key
description: The manifest state rejects correctly when a .gch appears or changes beside a plain-#include header, but the preprocessor (-E) key then computes the same hash as before, since -E does not load the PCH under gcc without -fpch-preprocess, and the old object is served. Pre-existing on 40511b7; found by the absent-deps review on 2026-10-13. The branch's tests change the header as well, which hides it. Options: key the .gch that gcc would pick up (the unkeyed-.gch search already finds the candidates) by its bytes or its .vcache-key when present; or decline the compile when an unkeyed .gch sits beside an included header.
close_reason: Merged PCH-aware GCC preprocessing and key v5. Baseline 14e51b4 fails all four stale-PCH cases; the new hidden-incbin guard was also shown failing before its fix. Full gate: 1409 unit and 1186 integration checks passed.

title: cxx manifest: absent probes from a compiler with the absent-deps-1 marker, without the tracer
description:
Record C/C++ manifest inputs from a compiler that lists its absent probes itself, without the tracer.

The devtools gcc and clang builds carry a local patch (devtools `3rdparty/gcc_absent_deps.patch`, and the clang equivalent) that makes the compiler report what the tracer records today:

- `-fabsent-deps=FILE` writes every path the preprocessor looked for and did not find, one per line in byte order: each search directory tried before the one that supplied a header, each `__has_include` that found nothing, each `.gch`/`.pch` probed beside a header, and each nonexistent include directory. Paths are as the preprocessor formed them (relative ones against the compile's cwd). gcc writes nothing when the input is already preprocessed; clang's driver forwards the option only to the preprocessing step.
- `-M`/`-MD` output lists a header `__has_include` found (gcc; clang already did) and every precompiled header the compiler read (gcc: accepted or rejected; clang: the `-include-pch` file).
- The banner carries the marker `absent-deps-1` after the version: gcc `gcc version 16.1.0 (GCC) absent-deps-1` (`-v`) and `gcc (GCC) 16.1.0 absent-deps-1` (`--version`); clang `clang version 22.1.8 absent-deps-1`.

Acceptance:

1. When the compiler banner vcache already memoises for the fingerprint (`compiler-version-memo-v2`, from `<compiler> -v`) contains the token `absent-deps-` followed by a version number vcache knows (1), the recording compile runs without `LD_PRELOAD` of the tracer and with `-fabsent-deps=<scratch>` added beside the `-MD -MF <scratch>` vcache already adds. The state's files come from the depfile, its absent paths from the absent-deps file (canonicalised through the roots like the files; stored as the highest missing ancestor as today). The gcc `__has_include` decline and the unkeyed-`.gch` search do not run for such a compiler, in either mode.
2. A path in the absent-deps file that exists at record time is a bug in the compiler and must not be stored (a state with an absent path that exists would never hit); log and fall back to the tracer.
3. Without the marker, behaviour is unchanged (tracer, then depfile fallback).
4. `cxx_manifest_trace = false` still records from the depfile alone, with the absent-deps file when the marker is present.
5. Tests (fail first): a stub compiler whose `-v` prints the marker and that writes a given absent list; the shadowing case, the `__has_include` flip, the `.gch` appearing, a nonexistent `-I` that gets created; the marker absent -> tracer used (assert on the log line); the version token `absent-deps-2` unknown -> tracer used.
6. Measure on the host with the devtools gcc and clang once rebuilt: record cost and hit cost on `src/daemon/server.cc` against the tracer path (section 5.2 numbers), and say in the commit body which is cheaper.

Docs: `docs/design.md` "The C/C++ manifest" (the third input source), `docs/configuration.md` (`cxx_manifest_trace` table gains the row for the marker case).
close_reason: Landed on feat/cxx-manifest-absent-deps: a compiler with absent-deps-1 records manifest states from -fabsent-deps= without the tracer (switch cxx_manifest_absent_deps); a listed path that exists declines the state (no tracer fallback: the compile already ran). Tests in integration section 19b and unit core::cxx manifest absent-deps list; numbers in IDEAS 5.2.

title: C/C++ manifest: record absent include probes through vcache-fstrace.so to close the shadowing hole
description:
The C/C++ manifest (`cxx_manifest`, `src/core/cxx_manifest.cc`, `RunCompile` in
`src/core/compile.cc`) records a state from the compile's depfile. A depfile names the
files the compile read, not the paths the preprocessor probed and did not find, so a new
header that would be found earlier on the include path than a recorded one is invisible:
a lookup can still hit with the old answer. ccache's direct and depend modes have the same
hole; `docs/design.md` ("The C/C++ manifest", "The shadowing hole") documents it.

`vcache-fstrace.so` already records absent paths as `M` lines for the link cache
(`src/core/link_trace.cc`). Run the recording compile under the tracer, store each probed
and absent path in the state (a new line kind in `RenderCxxManifest`, so bump the
`vcache-cxxmanifest-1` header), and reject a state on lookup when any of those paths now
exists.

Acceptance:
- An integration test: compile with `-I first -I second`, header in `second`; second
  compile hits through the manifest; create the same header in `first`; the next compile
  misses and its object uses the new header. The test fails on the code before the change.
- The lookup cost stays one `stat` per absent path; measure it on a PCH consumer with
  hundreds of probes.
- Without the tracer (no `vcache-fstrace.so`, macOS), states are recorded as today and the
  hole stays documented.
close_reason: Landed on feat/cxx-manifest-trace (c4696e7): the recording compile runs under vcache-fstrace.so; states keep absent paths (vcache-cxxmanifest-2) and a lookup rejects a state when one exists. server.cc hit +0.5 ms clang++ (535 absent paths), +0.2 ms g++ (484); Boost TU under g++ now records and hits in 9.8 ms. Without the tracer states come from the depfile as before.

title: C/C++ manifest: record a state on a preprocessor hit, from a traced -E run
description:
vcache `fbg` at `53c947f` (source unchanged since `a489230`). Version 2, 2026-10-14.

## Why

A manifest state is recorded only on a miss, after the real compile ran (`RunCompile`,
"what the compile read, for the manifest"). A lookup whose manifest key has no matching
state but whose preprocessor key hits (`try_hit(key, "")`) is served by the preprocessor
and records nothing, so the TU pays for `-E` on every lookup until its next real miss.
`docs/design.md` lists this under Known limitations ("A preprocessor hit records no
manifest state"). Cases that reach it:

- a header edited only in a comment or whitespace: the state's digest is stale, the
  preprocessed text is unchanged;
- a clang PCH rebuilt with different bytes and no `<pch>.sum` or `<pch>.vcache-key`
  beside it (`PchIdentity`, `cxx_manifest.cc`): the manifest key changes, the
  preprocessor key does not;
- an entry stored by a tree with `cxx_manifest = false` (`VCACHE_CXX_MANIFEST=0`), or by
  a vcache before the manifest existed.

## Mechanism: trace the -E run, not the linemarkers

Version 1 proposed reading the files from the preprocessed text's linemarkers, as
ccache's direct mode does. Rejected. A state is `{result_key, files, absent}`
(`CxxManifestState`), and `absent` holds the paths the include search probed and did not
find, so a header created at one is caught by `FindAppearedPath`. Linemarkers name only
the files that were read: a state built from them would carry no absent set and silently
drop the shadowing protection, and `#embed` / `__has_embed` reads have no linemarker.
Upstream's `03e7d7e` ("use a compile's trace only when it shows the include search")
makes the same point for traces.

Instead, run the preprocessor under the tracer, with a depfile, and feed the same three
sources through the `ReadCxxManifestInputs` path a miss uses:

1. When a state could be recorded (`!manifest_key.empty()`, not `read_only`, not
   `recache`) and the manifest did not serve, `BuildPreprocessCommand` adds
   `-MD -MF <temp>/pp.d` (gcc accepts `-MD` with `-E`; no `-MT`, the depfile is not
   kept), and the `-E` run gets `VCACHE_TRACE_LOG=<temp>/pp-trace` and
   `LD_PRELOAD=<tracer>` exactly as the real compile does (`CxxManifestTracer`,
   `WithoutPreloadRefusals`). The comment at `records_manifest` saying the `-E` run stays
   untraced on purpose goes.
2. If `try_hit(key, "")` serves (and `key != manifest_unserved_key`), record a state
   `{key, files, absent}` from `pp.d`, the `-E` trace, and, with no tracer and
   `CompilerWritesAbsentList`, the absent list the `-E` run wrote. Verify first that the
   absent-deps patch honours `-fabsent-deps=` under `-E`; if not, the no-tracer path
   records from the depfile alone, with the gcc `__has_include` and `.gch` declines a
   miss applies.
3. The same declines as a miss apply unchanged: a time macro, a file modified at or
   after `started_ns`, a gcc `.gch` an `#include` can reach without a trace,
   `-working-directory` (vcache-6h7 D6), an incomplete or malformed trace, ld.so refusing
   the preload. `scan_incbin` stays false: the preprocessor key already refused
   `.incbin`.
4. On a preprocessor miss the `-E` trace and depfile are discarded; the real compile's
   stay the source, so a miss records exactly what it records today.
5. Never record from the hit blob's stored depfile: it came from the tree that stored
   the entry and may have been written with `-MMD`.
6. Log `cxx manifest: recorded a state from the preprocessor run`; a decline keeps the
   existing `cxx manifest: not recording: <reason>`. Add a counter beside
   `Counter::kManifestHit` (`src/core/stats.h`) so `--show-stats` shows how often a hit
   records.

Differences between an `-E` trace and a compile trace, accepted:

- clang `-E` does not load a PCH (gcc `-fpch-preprocess` does). The PCH is in the
  manifest key already (keyed sidecar or bytes), and `keyed_pchs` are stripped from a
  miss's depfile too, so a state without the PCH file matches a miss's state. Check
  whether clang `-E -MD` names the PCH in `pp.d`; either way the manifest key covers it.
- The `-E` run writes no object, so there is nothing to scan for `.incbin`; see 3.

Cost: one `LD_PRELOAD` and a few hundred trace records per `-E` run that follows a
manifest miss. A tree that hits through the manifest pays nothing new.

## Key versions

The state format and both keys are unchanged, so no bump. If the implementation changes
`CxxManifestState` or what a state records, bump `kCxxManifestKeyVersion`
(`vcache-cxx-manifest-v5` today; vcache-6h7 takes v6, so coordinate) and say so in the
commit body.

## Acceptance

A new block in `tests/integration_test.sh` section 19. A TU includes `h.h`; compile 1
misses and stores a state. Then edit a comment in `h.h`.

- Compile 2: `hit on disk` 1, `preprocessor skipped` 0,
  `recorded a state from the preprocessor run` 1.
- Compile 3: `preprocessor skipped` 1 and `preprocess:` 0 in the log.
- Fails first on `a489230`: compile 3 logs `hit on disk` and `preprocessor skipped` 0.
- Under gcc with `VCACHE_CXX_MANIFEST_TRACE=0`: compile 2 logs
  `recording from the depfile` and compile 3 still skips the preprocessor.
- `make test` at 0 failures. `docs/design.md` drops the Known-limitations entry and
  describes the traced `-E` run in the manifest section.
- Commit `feat(core):` with one `Fails first:` line per test, ending `Deploy: vcache`.
notes:
2026-10-14 implemented on feat/manifest-pp-hit at 0e44776 (base 089e543), pushed; not merged to fbg.
Built: BuildPreprocessCommand takes a depfile and absent-list path. When a state could be recorded (manifest key, not read-only, not recache) PlanCxxPreprocessRecording gives the -E run -MD -MF <scratch>/pp.d and the tracer (VCACHE_TRACE_LOG=<scratch>/pp-trace), or without a tracer and CompilerWritesAbsentList, -fabsent-deps=<scratch>/pp-absent. ld.so refusals are stripped from the -E stderr. On try_hit(key, "") at the lookup stage, ReadCxxPreprocessorRunInputs feeds them through ReadCxxManifestTrace / ReadCxxAbsentList / ReadCxxManifestInputs (scan_incbin false) and StoreCxxManifest stores {key, files, absent}; log "cxx manifest: recorded a state from the preprocessor run", counter Counter::kManifestRecordedOnPreprocessorHit shown as "pp hits recorded" under "manifest hits". The lease-wake try_hit does not record (the peer recorded its state).
Deviations: CxxManifestTracer split into UsableCxxManifestTracer (quiet, returns the reason) plus the logging wrapper, so the -E setup logs nothing and a miss's log is unchanged; the fallback reason is logged only on a hit. StoreCxxManifest returns bool so the counter counts stored states only. Extra declines in the -E plan: -working-directory ("the compiler changes its working directory", same wording as 6h7 D6; the -E run then gets no depfile/trace/list) and a compile whose dependency flags are not -MD (parity with the miss's "writes no -MD dependency file").
Found against the merged tree: kCxxManifestKeyVersion is already v6 (the bead said v5); no bump made. A comment-only edit leaves the preprocessor key unchanged, so the recorded state names the same result key as the stale one and replaces it ("stored 1 states", next lookup "state 1 of 1"), not a second state.
-fabsent-deps= under -E: the devtools gcc-16 (16.2.0 absent-deps-1) and clang-23 (23.1.4 absent-deps-1) both write the list under -E; gcc's -E list with -fpch-preprocess equals the -c list (.gch probes included; without -fpch-preprocess the .gch probes are missing). clang -E -include-pch reads the PCH's source header instead of the PCH; its list matches -c. /opt/infra/bin/clang-22 lacks the patch.
Existing assertions changed: section 19 "and its -E run does not" -> the -E run runs under the tracer; 19b "only the recording compile is given -fabsent-deps=" -> 2/1/1 (compile and -E); unit TestStats counts eleven positional counters.
Gate: make test 1442 unit / 1285 integration, 0 failed (baseline 1442 / 1254).
close_reason: Landed on fbg via feat/manifest-pp-hit 0e44776: the -E run is traced (or given the compiler's absent list) with a depfile, and a preprocessor hit records a state from it; counter 'pp hits recorded'; no key bump. Gate 1442 unit / 1285 integration, 0 failed. Deploy pending with vcache-6h7.

title: cxx manifest: the trace drops absent probes that end in /.., so a clang shadowing through <sub/../a.h> serves a stale object
description: IsIgnoredPath in src/core/link_trace.cc:53 drops trace records whose path ends in /... clang resolves #include <sub/../a.h> by probing first/sub/.. before second/sub/../a.h, so the absent probe that would catch a header appearing in first/ is dropped from the state and the old object is served. Found by the absent-deps review on 2026-10-13 (scratchpad absent-deps-review.md): the compiler's -fabsent-deps= list gets this case right, the trace does not. Fix: keep the record as a path (lexically normalised or as spelled, like the list does) and store it as the highest missing ancestor; add the <sub/../a.h> shadowing case to integration section 19 for clang, failing first.
close_reason: Keep trailing /.. probes and invalidate old C++ manifests with key v4. Regression fails on 20fc57b; full gate passes 1395 unit and 1183 integration checks.

title: dep-scan key keeps a path joined to its flag verbatim, so -I/abs/inc splits scans per checkout
description: DepScanKeyArgs (src/core/compile.cc) calls RootMap::Canonicalize on each whole argument, and Canonicalize matches only an argument that is itself a path under a root. A dependency scan (-M/-MM without -c) from a CMake build carries -I/abs/inc joined, so two checkouts never share a scan manifest although docs/design.md and the dep_scan section of docs/configuration.md say they do. The preprocessor key is unaffected (-I and -D are not in it). Fix: canonicalise the path part of joined path flags (-I, -isystem, -iquote, -idirafter, -include, -imacros, -F, -L, -fsanitize-ignorelist= and friends) in DepScanKeyArgs; bump kDepScanKeyVersion; a test with one scan in two trees under VCACHE_ROOTS. Reproduce first: one -M command run in two worktrees with VCACHE_LOG set shows two different dep-scan keys.
close_reason: Dep-scan v4 canonicalizes joined include and path flags without changing macro values. Baseline 597eb90 fails 13 joined-flag checks and the cross-checkout scan hit; full gate passes 1409 unit and 1184 integration checks.

title: fstrace: refuse a dirfd that resolves to a '(deleted)' name and resolve it before the real call
description:
## Why

`resolve_at_path` in `src/trace/fstrace.c` reads `/proc/self/fd/<dirfd>` **after** the real `openat`/`fstatat`/
`faccessat` returned. Two consequences: (1) a directory removed in between resolves to `<path> (deleted)` and the
tracer records that string as a filename, which readers then hash as absent; (2) another thread can close and reuse
the descriptor, or rename the directory, between the call and the readlink, so the record names the wrong
directory. Found by the triangulated review of vcache-6h7 (section 6.5).

## What

- Resolve the dirfd before the real call, on a stack buffer, and emit after it with the pre-resolved prefix. The
  result still names the directory the call used when the descriptor was valid at call time; a close-and-reuse race
  between the two remains the process's own race and is documented.
- Treat a readlink result ending in ` (deleted)` as unresolvable: `mark_incomplete` and emit nothing, like a failed
  readlink today.

## Acceptance

- Integration check with a C fixture: open a directory fd, remove the directory, `openat(fd, "x")`: the trace has no
  record naming `(deleted)` and `<log>.incomplete` exists. Fails first: the current tracer records
  `M	<dir> (deleted)/x` and no marker.
- Negative control: the existing `openat(dir, "value")` `R` record is unchanged.
- `make test` at 0 failures. Commit body ends with `Deploy: vcache`.

## Non-goals

Pinning the directory identity (device and inode) into the record; paths remain the trace's identity.
notes: Implemented in 95bd043 on fix/tracer-defects (not pushed, not merged).
close_reason: Implemented on fix/tracer-defects (0d1503d, 05b86e0, 95bd043, 0aef3ef, db52038) plus the review fix 4244722; merged into fbg as 7c0e548 with 1410 unit / 1215 integration checks at 0 failures; dist/{host,el10,dc-build} rebuilt from 31a24a5 and installed 2026-10-14.

title: fstrace: announce a shared object loaded by a relative name instead of dropping its L record
description:
## Why

`announce_object` in `src/trace/fstrace.c` returns early when `dlpi_name` does not start with `/`, so a shared
object loaded through a relative `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` entry or a relative `DT_RUNPATH` never gets an `L` record. The
link manifest treats `L` records as toolchain inputs, so a rebuilt relative-path library leaves old link entries
servable. Found by the triangulated review of vcache-6h7 (section 6.4).

## What

- Resolve a relative `dlpi_name` against the process cwd with `SYS_getcwd` at announce time and emit the absolute
  path, the same resolution vcache-6h7 adds to `emit`; if `getcwd` fails, `mark_incomplete` rather than drop the
  record. An empty `dlpi_name` (the main program) stays excluded as today, as does the tracer itself.
- Keep the `dlpi_addr == self_base()` exclusion.

## Acceptance

- Integration check: a traced program loaded with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=lib` (relative) against a small shared object
  built in `$WORK` yields `L	$WORK/lib/libprobe.so`. Fails first: no `L` record for it on the current tracer.
- Negative control: the absolute `L` records of libc are unchanged.
- `make test` at 0 failures. Commit body ends with `Deploy: vcache`.

## Non-goals

`dlopen` after the constructor ran (not announced today, documented limitation).
notes: Implemented in 0aef3ef on fix/tracer-defects (not pushed, not merged).

title: fstrace: build the .incomplete marker path without silent truncation and record when it cannot be created
description:
## Why

`mark_incomplete` in `src/trace/fstrace.c` copies `VCACHE_TRACE_LOG` into a `VCACHE_RECORD_MAX` buffer with a
`sizeof path - 12` bound, so an over-long log path is silently truncated and the marker is created under a
different name that `TraceMarkedIncomplete` never finds. A failed `openat` for the marker is ignored. The comment
argues that losing the marker is safe because a tracer that cannot write "produces no process records either",
which is false once an earlier process of the tree has already written `P` records into the same log. Found by the
triangulated review of vcache-6h7 (section 6.3).

## What

- If the marker path does not fit, do not truncate: fall back to writing a sentinel record that readers treat as
  incomplete (a line consisting of `!` alone, which `ReadTraceRecords` already rejects as malformed since
  `line.size() < 3`), so the trace is refused rather than trusted. Document in `ReadTraceRecords` that a `!` line is
  the tracer's explicit incomplete sentinel.
- Also write that sentinel when the marker `openat` fails for any reason, so the two failure channels back each
  other up.
- Replace the comment's safety argument with the real one: the sentinel in the log is the backstop for a missing
  marker.
- `ensure_log` and `mark_incomplete` refuse a relative `VCACHE_TRACE_LOG` (treat as unset) so neither the log nor
  the marker lands in whatever cwd the process has at the time (vcache-6h7 section 3.5 asks for the same; land it
  here, first).

## Acceptance

- Integration checks: (a) a `VCACHE_TRACE_LOG` of 4090 bytes makes a traced `cat missing` leave a `!` line in the
  log and `ReadTraceRecords` (via the link cache's decline reason) refuse it; (b) a marker directory made read-only
  after the log is opened yields the `!` sentinel; (c) a relative `VCACHE_TRACE_LOG` produces no log and no marker.
  Fails first: (a) creates a truncated-name marker and the log is accepted; (b) accepts the log; (c) writes the log
  into the cwd.
- `make test` at 0 failures. Commit body ends with `Deploy: vcache`.

## Non-goals

Changing how readers locate the marker (`TraceMarkedIncomplete` stays).
notes: Implemented in 05b86e0 on fix/tracer-defects (not pushed, not merged).
close_reason: Implemented on fix/tracer-defects (0d1503d, 05b86e0, 95bd043, 0aef3ef, db52038) plus the review fix 4244722; merged into fbg as 7c0e548 with 1410 unit / 1215 integration checks at 0 failures; dist/{host,el10,dc-build} rebuilt from 31a24a5 and installed 2026-10-14.

title: fstrace: a positive short write tears a record; mark the trace incomplete instead of retrying the suffix
description:
## Why

`emit` in `src/trace/fstrace.c` writes one record with `SYS_write` in a loop: a positive short write advances
`written` and writes the remaining suffix. Between those two writes another process of the traced tree can append
its own record to the shared O_APPEND log, so the completed record is torn across another one and no `.incomplete`
marker is created. `ReadTraceRecords` then rejects the malformed line (or, worse, parses two half-records as valid
paths). The comment above `emit` attributes atomicity to `PIPE_BUF`, which governs pipes and FIFOs; the log is a
regular file, where `O_APPEND` serialises each whole `write` call but says nothing about two calls. Found by the
triangulated review of vcache-6h7 (section 6.2).

## What

- Treat a positive short write as a failure: `mark_incomplete()` and return, as the loop already does for a
  negative return other than `EINTR`. Keep the `EINTR` retry only when nothing was written (`r < 0`).
- Fix the comment: one record is one `write`; `O_APPEND` on a regular file makes each call atomic with respect to
  other appenders; a short write would break that and is made loud.

## Acceptance

- Unit test in `tests/unit_test.cc` or an integration check: with the log on a file that limits the write (e.g.
  `ulimit -f` sized so a record straddles the limit, or a FIFO reader that reads a few bytes at a time if a
  regular-file short write cannot be forced on this host), the tracer leaves `<log>.incomplete` and the log holds
  no partial record. If no short write can be forced deterministically, the test checks the code path through a
  compile-time hook (`VCACHE_FSTRACE_TEST_SHORT_WRITE=<n>` env read only in test builds) that truncates the first
  write to `n` bytes. Fails first: on the current tracer the record is written in two pieces and no marker exists.
- `make test` at 0 failures. Commit body ends with `Deploy: vcache`.

## Non-goals

Changing the record format or the record size limit.

title: Merge upstream/main (ports of the fork's work) into fbg; keep our cache-key versions higher
description:
Evaluated 2026-10-14 against fbg `bc74338` and `upstream/main` `927fd2d`.

## Owner decisions

- **D1. Merge, not rebase.** `git merge upstream/main` into `fbg`, as AGENTS.md prescribes.
  A rebase would replay each of our feature commits against upstream's rewrite of the same
  feature, rewrite `fbg` (force push, devtools `VCACHE_BRANCH=fbg`, every worktree) and
  end in the same tree.
- **D2. Cache-key versions: keep ours higher.** Upstream's rewrite numbers its tags below
  ours (`vcache-key-v2` vs our v5, `vcache-cxx-manifest-v3` vs v5, `vcache-link-v1` vs v2,
  `vcache-rust-key-v4` vs v5, `vcache-rust-manifest-v2` vs v3, `vcache-depscan-v2` vs v4).
  Taking upstream's constants would let the deployed binary read entries in the shared
  stores under `/build/<user>/cache/vcache/` that our older binaries wrote under the same
  tag with different rules. Our numbers are the floor. Each key whose rule the merge
  changes (upstream keys on the driver's environment, header maps and clang `--config`
  contents; our tracer wave changed the manifest and link keys) goes to the next number
  above ours: key v6, cxx-manifest v6, link v3, depscan v5, rust-key v6, rust-manifest v4.
  The commit body names every bump, before `dist/` is rebuilt.

## Why

Upstream merged its own ports of nearly all fork work on 2026-10-12 (PRs #26 to #30,
"Port Richard Geary's ..."), so the trees are close:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Fork-only commits | 192 (145 non-merge); 55 byte-identical upstream; ~45 of the rest beads or docs |
| Upstream-only commits | 136; the ports plus 24 genuine upstream changes |
| Tree difference | 57 files, +3526/-1643; ~2,300 lines without beads/AGENTS.md, half tests |
| Trial `git merge-tree` | 19 conflicted files, 109 hunks: compile.cc 29, design.md 20, configuration.md 13, daemon.md 9; add/add on cost.{cc,h}, cxx_manifest.{cc,h}, jobserver.cc; both test suites merge cleanly textually |

## Resolution policy

For each conflicted file take upstream's version, then re-apply the fork-only deltas:

1. **Absent-deps compiler list** (`cxx_manifest_absent_deps`: `e3ff76a`, `c8d357e`,
   `895bb5a`, `b4e32d2`, `b6fb38a`, `5d3e456`, `21c8778`, `e969ccd`, `a8a1ddf`, `fee288a`,
   `191d172`, `daf75bc`, `ca3a7fe`, tests `be4e4e2`, `3c2c713`). Upstream has none of it.
2. **Tracer defect wave** (`db52038`, `0d1503d`, `05b86e0`, `95bd043`, `0aef3ef`,
   `4244722`). Upstream's `a462505` overlaps the stat-family part; the short-write marker,
   the `!` line, dirfd-before-call, relative `dlpi_name`, `fdopendir` and `openat2` are
   ours alone.
3. **Five fixes** closed in `7460205`: `7730282` assembly vs object entries, `dd75da6`
   missing parent-directory probes, `0a1ad61` joined dep-scan paths, `5dff7ad` Rust
   artifact paths, `511b918` the gcc PCH key. Check each against upstream `79c1fd9` and

title: daemon: preserve readiness replies across interrupted and short writes
description: SignalReady in src/daemon/server.cc makes one write and ignores its result. title: Link hit: refresh .linkout mtime, verify the clone instead of the source; AGENTS.md daemon note is stale
description:
Three pre-existing defects found by the reflink plan review (IDEA-reflink-compile-outputs.md, section 10). Branch fix/linkout-hit, worktree /build/richard/claude-tmp/worktrees/vcache/linkout-hit.

1. src/core/link.cc MaterializeOutputs never refreshes the mtime of <shard>/<digest>.linkout on a hit. DiskStorage::Get refreshes the entry's mtime, and eviction (DiskStorage::TrimGlobal) is oldest-mtime-first over every file in the shards, so under trim pressure a hot link output is evicted before its entry and every later hit on that entry fails digest verification and relinks. Refresh the stored file's mtime (utimensat with AT_FDCWD, nanosecond-now) on every hit, before the hash so a trim that starts during the hash sees a fresh file. A failed refresh is logged and ignored.

2. MaterializeOutputs hashes the stored file (hash::HashFile) and then clones it (util::CloneFile) into place. Between the two the stored file can be evicted or replaced, so the bytes verified are not necessarily the bytes published. Clone first to a private temp name in the output directory, hash the clone (a reflink shares the source's extents at the moment of cloning, so this verifies exactly what will be published), then rename the temp onto the output; on mismatch remove the temp and fail the hit as today. Keep the executable-bit handling and its umask rule unchanged.

3. AGENTS.md "Gotchas" says the daemon (VCACHE_DAEMON=auto) is off in every repo's vcache-env.sh. ~/fbg/devtools/scripts/vcache-env.sh exportVcacheEnv now exports VCACHE_DAEMON=auto with VCACHE_DAEMON_SINGLE_FLIGHT=1 by default (FBG_VCACHE_SINGLE_FLIGHT defaults to 1), citing docs/daemon.md Results. Rewrite the gotcha to say what is true now and keep the refused-client note (upstream #23).

Rules: AGENTS.md applies in full. Each code fix needs a test that fails first on the pre-fix code (tests/integration_test.sh has link sections; for the mtime refresh assert the .linkout mtime moves on a hit; for clone-then-verify a mutation such as corrupting the stored file between hash and clone, or a unit-level test if MaterializeOutputs is factored to allow it); record `Fails first:` lines in the commit body; the doc change is exempt. Run `make` and `make test` through ~/bin/build-limited with MAKEFLAGS=-j8 and /usr/lib64/ccache removed from PATH. Commit in upstream style (`fix(link):`, `docs:`), body ending with `Deploy: vcache` for the code commit. Do not edit src/util/fs.cc or src/rust/rust_compile.cc; other agents own them. Push the branch to origin; do not merge to fbg and do not touch .beads.

title: cxx manifest: skip preprocessing only for a cold recording compile
description:
Owner priority (2026-10-15): warm incremental builds take precedence; this cold-fill optimization remains P3. This description incorporates the owner's amendment in comment 61. Preserve the stale-manifest preprocessor path and its recording counter.

The el10 measurement used sunbird 73a7f5993, clang 23.1.4, 525 TUs: plain clang 23.6 s wall / 7m08 user, ccache 25.0 s / 7m10, vcache 35.8 s / 8m38. These whole-build figures motivate attribution, not a proof that preprocessing explains the entire gap. Today src/core/compile.cc preprocesses before a miss, but already supports DeriveCxxResultKey when preprocessing exits 1. CxxManifestState.result_key can name either key family.

## Behavior

- A valid manifest state with a usable result remains a hit with no compiler run.
- With no usable stored manifest states, a nonempty manifest key, writable caching, a supported recording compile and a usable tracer, run the real compile once, record its complete inputs, and derive the result key. Skip the -E invocation; do not fake a preprocessor failure to reach this branch.
- If stored states exist but are stale, retain the traced -E lookup. A preprocessed-key hit still calls PlanCxxPreprocessRecording and increments Counter::kManifestRecordedOnPreprocessorHit. A preprocessed-key miss compiles and stores normally.
- A matching state whose result is missing, corrupt, or lacks required outputs also retains the existing preprocessor fallback. Empty, undecodable and absent manifests may use the cold path, but media errors must remain visible and obey error_on_cache_media_failure.
- Do not expand the optimization to untraced/absent-list-only runs in this bead. Preserve their current fallback, manifest-off behavior, read-only/recache contracts, dependency scans, PCH builds/consumers, depfile replay and compiler diagnostics.
- Prove before skipping -E that a recording compile can run (including -MD vs -MMD and working-directory restrictions). If the actual trace is incomplete/refused or input recording is unsafe, return the fresh compile's real status/output without storing a derived result or new state. Keep volatile-input, changed-during-compile and .incbin checks that the derived-key path needs.
- Keep single-flight: cold callers reserve by the manifest identity; a waiter reloads and validates the leader's state before deciding to compile. Lease release and admission must work on every exit.
- Count a deliberate cold miss and a real compiler failure truthfully; skipped preprocessing must not increment preprocessor-failure statistics.

## Key compatibility and the first benign edit

No key bump is intended: reuse the existing manifest schema, derived-key family and preprocessed-key family unchanged. If implementation changes any hashed input or serialization meaning, bump that matching version instead. Do not remove the preprocessor-hit feature or its counter.

A cold fill stores only a derived-key result. Therefore the FIRST comment-only edit can run -E and still compile, because the corresponding preprocessed-key entry may not yet exist. After that entry is seeded, another benign edit can hit through -E and record a state; the next unchanged lookup hits the manifest. Preserve both cases in tests and documentation rather than promising that every benign edit immediately hits. A result under each key family is an accepted duplication, and preprocessed-mode sharing remains possible for preprocessed-key entries.

## Verification and measurements

Unit coverage should exercise any extracted path-selection decision and counter behavior without adding a public API solely for tests. End-to-end coverage in tests/integration_test.sh must prove:
1. Fresh-store recording compile has one compile invocation, zero preprocess: lines, correct outputs, and a byte-identical cross-directory manifest hit.
2. A stale state still runs -E; distinguish the first unseeded benign edit from a seeded preprocessed hit, then verify state recording and the next no--E hit.
3. A real header edit, newly present absent dependency and rebuilt PCH invalidate correctly; missing result, read-only, recache, unusable tracer and incomplete trace obey the contracts above.
4. Concurrent cold requests compile once with single-flight enabled; failed compilation preserves exit status/diagnostics and stores no result.

Adjust existing preprocessor-hit fixtures deliberately to seed the preprocessed entry; do not weaken their assertions. Fails-first evidence must name the cold invocation count or a broken routing/recording invariant.

Repeat the cold, warm cross-tree, no-op and one-file-edit recipes from the recorded vcache-232 setup, with current wrapper limits and fresh interleaved controls. Target cold wall and user CPU within 10% of the paired ccache baseline; report misses of that target and residual costs rather than claiming a guaranteed win. Warm/incremental changes need reported spread and no unexplained regression. Check el10 tracer loading (cargo --version under the deployed tracer) and record binary revisions. Update docs/design.md, docs/configuration.md and README.md's manifest explanation together.

## Names

| Concept | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Existing derived result key | DeriveCxxResultKey | Joins the Cxx family in vcache::core |
| Existing state result reference | CxxManifestState::result_key | Allows both established key families |
| Preprocessor recording | PlanCxxPreprocessRecording; Counter::kManifestRecordedOnPreprocessorHit | Preserve the existing behavior and statistics |
| Historical task identity | vcache-moz | Bead IDs cannot be renamed |

Run every build, test and benchmark through ~/bin/build-limited, including commands in sibling repositories. Remove ccache/sccache directories from PATH before compiler suites; do not override wrapper limits or increase parallelism. Put new scratch, fixtures and logs under /build/$USER/codex-1000/<task>/; new worktrees under /build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/<repo>/<name>, from the appropriate integration ref (origin/fbg for vcache). Attach sunbird worktrees to a beads session before br or commits. Preserve existing work and follow AGENTS.md removal/overwrite approval rules.

For each new or changed regression assertion, show the defect against the pre-fix revision or a targeted mutation, then show the corrected result. Record the named failing assertion and revision/mutation in the implementation commit's Fails first line. Keep detailed command, configuration, status, counter deltas and VCACHE_LOG evidence; timing alone is not proof. Run the full make test gate before pushing. Binary-changing commits end with Deploy: vcache and rebuild dist/host, dist/el10 and dist/dc-build.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Implement the behavior and compatibility contract in the description without losing existing paths.
- [x] Unit and end-to-end regression assertions have recorded fails-first evidence, including injected failure cases.
- [x] Paired measurements and detailed logs quantify the gain and remaining costs.
- [x] Full limited make test passes; documentation and required dist deployments are complete.

All three dist variants rebuilt; installed host/EL10 each pass 50 GCC/Clang checks, dc-build passes 25 GCC 11 checks. EL10 cargo preload passes. dc-build Clang 3.4 rejects the same prefix-map flag before and after; unsupported compiler explicitly recorded. Paired three-round 523-object Sunbird measurements and limitations are in docs/cxx-cold-recording.md; the ccache cold target was missed, with no overall speedup claim. All byte comparisons and warm-hit checks pass. Evidence: /build/richard/codex-1000/cold-recording-20261016/.

comments.text: Amended 2026-10-15 after review: do NOT make derived keys the only miss path. Split by whether a manifest exists for the key. (a) No manifest stored: one compiler run under the tracer, derived result key; this is every TU of a cold fill, where an -E run can hit nothing. (b) Manifest stored but every state stale (the edit case): keep today's path, traced -E first, a preprocessed-key hit records the state (vcache-cxx-manifest-pp-hit-state-6ft stays reachable and its counter stays), a miss compiles. A comment-only header edit shared by N TUs then costs N preprocessor runs, not N compiles. No key bump: a state's result_key may already be either kind (cxx_manifest.h). A TU may hold one duplicate entry over its life (derived from the cold fill, preprocessed from a later edit); accepted. Acceptance stays, plus: a check that a stale-manifest miss still logs 'preprocess:' and a no-manifest miss does not, fails first. title: fstrace: interpose the stat family the tracer misses (stat64, lstat64, fstatat64, statx, __xstat)
description:
## Why

`src/trace/fstrace.c` interposes `stat`, `lstat`, `fstatat`, `access`, `faccessat`, `readlink`, `opendir` and the
`open` family, but not `stat64`, `lstat64`, `fstatat64`, `statx`, `readlinkat`, `fdopendir`, `openat2` or the legacy
`__xstat`, `__lxstat`, `__fxstatat` (and their `64` variants) that binaries built against pre-2.33 glibc headers
call. On this host (glibc 2.43) `stat dir/f`, `ls -l dir/f` and Python `os.stat("dir/f")` leave no record at all,
while `test -f dir/f` and `cat dir/f` record `R`. Verified 2026-10-13 with `LD_PRELOAD=bin/vcache-fstrace.so
VCACHE_TRACE_LOG=<log>`. A probe that is not recorded is an input missing from the C/C++ manifest state, the link
manifest and the sunbird test audit, so a later hit can be unsound. Found by the triangulated review of vcache-6h7
(see that bead's section 6.1).

## What

- Add wrappers, each routed through the existing `emit_result` / `emit_at_result` helpers so the R/M/W rules are
  shared: `stat64`, `lstat64`, `fstatat64`, `statx` (path + flags + `AT_EMPTY_PATH` handling like `fstatat`),
  `readlinkat`, `fdopendir` (emit `D` for the descriptor's path via `/proc/self/fd`, as `resolve_at_path` does),
  `openat2` (path relative to dirfd, `how->resolve` ignored for recording), and `__xstat`, `__xstat64`, `__lxstat`,
  `__lxstat64`, `__fxstatat`, `__fxstatat64` (drop the version argument, same emit).
- Keep the rule that only success records `R` and only `ENOENT` records `M` (vcache-wdn tracks whether
  that rule should change; do not change it here).
- `errno` and the return value of the real call survive the wrapper unchanged, as in the existing wrappers.

## Acceptance

- `tests/integration_test.sh` tracer section: under the tracer, `stat dir/f`, `ls -l dir/f` and
  `python3 -c 'import os; os.stat("dir/f")'` each produce an `R` record naming `dir/f`; `stat dir/missing` produces
  `M`. A C fixture calls `statx`, `fstatat64`, `readlinkat`, `fdopendir` and `__xstat` (declared `extern`) and each
  yields its record. Fails first: all of these yield no record on the current tracer (the probe above).
- Negative control: the existing `definitely-missing` `M` record and the `openat(dir, "value")` `R` record are
  unchanged.
- `make test` at 0 failures. Ends the commit body with `Deploy: vcache` (the shared object ships in dist/).

## Non-goals

glibc-internal opens (locale, gconv, nss) that never cross the PLT; raw syscalls; static binaries. Those stay
unobservable to an LD_PRELOAD tracer and are documented in `docs/design.md`.
notes: Implemented in db52038 on fix/tracer-defects (not pushed, not merged); also bumps kCxxManifestKeyVersion v5 and kLinkKeyVersion v2.

title: Rust hit replays artifact-notification paths from the original compile's temp dir
description: On a Rust manifest hit the cached rustc JSON notifications (--json=artifacts) name the original compile's staging path under the cache dir (e.g. /build/<user>/cache/vcache/host/tmp/vcache-rs-<pid>.../out/libfoo.rmeta) instead of the real output directory. The staging dir is under no root, so roots.LocalizeText never rewrites it. Cargo appears to use only the `emit` field today, so no breakage was observed, but any consumer reading the artifact path gets a path that no longer exists. Seen while tracing a feedreplay hit on 2026-10-10. Fix: rewrite the staging prefix to the output directory when storing (canonical placeholder) and localize on restore, like the depfile; add an integration check that the replayed artifact path equals the real out dir.

title: Rust output placement: umask-aware execute bits, no symlinks, no raw .d; exclusive CloneFile temp; WriteFileAtomic checks close
description:
Four pre-existing defects found by the reflink plan review (IDEA-reflink-compile-outputs.md, section 10), all on the path that places Rust compile outputs. Branch fix/output-placement, worktree /build/richard/claude-tmp/worktrees/vcache/output-placement.

1. src/util/fs.cc WriteFileAtomic ignores the result of close(fd). A delayed write error can surface only there, and today it is followed by the rename, so a short or corrupt file is published as if written. Check close; on failure unlink the temp and return false with that errno (see the saved_errno discipline already in the function).

2. src/util/fs.cc CloneFile names its temp `<to>.tmp.<pid>` and opens it O_CREAT|O_TRUNC without O_EXCL. Two processes in different PID namespaces sharing a store, or a stale temp, collide and truncate each other's temp. Use a mkstemp-style exclusive temp beside the destination, exactly as WriteFileAtomic does (including the fchmod to DefaultFileMode()), and create the destination's parent directory first as WriteFileAtomic does. Keep the reflink -> copy_file_range -> streamed-copy ladder and the no-hardlink rule unchanged.

3. src/rust/rust_compile.cc RestoreOutputs adds S_IXUSR|S_IXGRP|S_IXOTH unconditionally when a file is executable. Under a strict umask that publishes a 0711 binary other users can run but not read. Add a util helper (fs.h/fs.cc) that adds execute only where DefaultFileMode() allows read, with the logic now inline in src/core/link.cc MaterializeOutputs (do not edit link.cc; a separate bead migrates it), and use the helper in RestoreOutputs.

4. src/rust/rust_compile.cc CaptureOutputs uses directory_entry::is_regular_file(), which follows symlinks, so a symlink in the stage dir is captured through its target. Use symlink_status / lstat: a symlink or any non-regular entry makes capture fail (kCaptureFailed, passthrough, as today for other capture failures).

5. src/rust/rust_compile.cc CaptureOutputs stores a .d that fails core::ParseDepFile raw, with the stage-dir path inside, and a later hit in another checkout writes that path as the rule target. Do not store raw dep-info. The compile's outputs must still be placed and the build must still succeed; the entry must not be stored; record a decision reason (src/core/reason.h) so --show-stats explains it.

Rules: AGENTS.md applies in full. Every fix needs a test that fails first on the pre-fix code (unit tests in tests/unit_test.cc, integration in tests/integration_test.sh); record `Fails first:` lines in the commit body. Run `make` and `make test` through ~/bin/build-limited with MAKEFLAGS=-j8 and /usr/lib64/ccache removed from PATH. Commit in upstream style (`fix(rust):`, `fix(util):`), one or more commits, body ending with `Deploy: vcache`. Push the branch to origin; do not merge to fbg and do not touch .beads.

title: tests: attribute a recurrence of the historical daemon startup failure
description:
The original failures at merge 915156d were not reproduced during vcache-uo3: six instrumented full unit runs and 1000 isolated starts passed. Deterministic injection proved false failures on interrupted poll/read and missing startup diagnostics; those defects are fixed. Do not infer that they explain the historical failures.

The diagnostics-first path explicitly allowed by vcache-uo3 is complete. This deferred follow-up preserves the remaining historical-attribution question. Resume when a normal gate produces a retained SessionDaemon startup failure. Inspect startup.txt, the daemon log, section, elapsed time, child status and ready-pipe error before choosing a fix. The fixture preserves its directory on failure and still kills/reaps its child. See docs/daemon-test-readiness.md and /build/richard/codex-1000/daemon-ready-20261016 for prior evidence.

Do not create artificial host contention, retry the gate until green, widen deadlines or claim the historic failure was explained merely because injected faults pass. Reproduce the newly observed cause with a deterministic failing-first case, fix the responsible path, retain the failing and passing evidence and run make test. Use build-limited for every build/test, strip ccache/sccache PATH wrappers, keep scratch under /build/$USER/codex-1000, follow AGENTS.md and rebuild dist if production code changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Capture an actual normal-gate startup recurrence with the retained diagnostics.
- [x] Establish a confirmed startup-blocking cause and add a deterministic failing-first regression; preserve uncertainty about attribution of individual older failures.
- [x] Fix the confirmed cause and pass the full disk-backed gate without retry masking.
notes:
Normal gate recurrence during shared digest table work at baseline 76103ca: /build/richard/codex-1000/vcache-83w/gate.log has three retained SessionDaemon timeouts (whM4kU, 6r0XI1, yIjEI1), 22 total unit failures including dependent assertions and Put timeouts. First two retain a complete PID in .vcache-tmp-* with no renamed pid; third has pid, socket and listening log. Child was alive at 2001–2002 ms and reaped by fixture. One diagnostic strace unit run (daemon-diagnostic.log, daemon-trace.*) had no startup failures but reproduced bound-versus-Put failure: child 2768944 fsync of the cached blob took 1.085643 s, exceeding its 500 ms Put timeout. This establishes slow durable I/O for that Put failure; PID fsync is a candidate for the retained startup failures, not proven attribution. No deadline widened and no daemon code changed. Evidence retained for follow-up.
During the lock-error fix on 2026-10-18, gate.log failed the compound memory-queued holder Put assertion. A diagnostic unit run reproduced the separate holder key Put failure: unit-trace.2443138 records blob fsync taking 0.528453 s, then rename and EPIPE after the 500 ms client deadline. All daemon startups passed in both runs; this is further evidence of the existing disk-I/O test limitation, not startup-timeout attribution. Logs retained at /build/richard/codex-1000/daemon-lock-errors-20261018/. No deadlines or assertions changed; further gates use a private tmpfs test directory while retaining disk-backed failure evidence.
2026-10-18 review: not stale. The current code still durably flushed the informational PID before listening. A single normal disk-backed full gate at 60203a3, traced without injected delays or added load, passed but recorded daemon PID 1008595 spending 2.025114 s in fsync of its temporary PID, immediately followed by rename to daemon/pid and serving. A unit-fixture PID flush took 1.598923 s. This directly demonstrates a startup blocking mechanism longer than the two-second fixture deadline; it does not retrospectively prove every older timeout had that cause. Evidence: /build/richard/codex-1000/rpf-review-20261018/baseline-gate.log, baseline-trace.1008595 and pid-flush-observations.json. New narrowly targeted flush-stall regressions fail first on 60203a3 in both harnesses; the unit fixture fails at 2002 ms. The fix preserves atomic PID publication but disables only that fsync; file-lock ownership and durable cache writes are unchanged. gate-fixed.log passes the complete ordinary disk-backed gate on its first post-fix run: 1564 unit, 1342 integration, two 16-case startup suites and ancillary checks. No timeout widening, tmpfs substitution or retry masking. Separate durable blob Put timing failures remain open as vcache-98b. Publication and installed checks follow landing; evidence remains in this task directory.

Historical per-instance attribution remains qualified; the independent Put timing issue is tracked separately.

title: Compiles with -S and with -c share a preprocessor key, so -S can be served an object
description:
`ComputeKey` in `src/core/compile.cc` hashes `key_args`, and `args::Parse` drops `-c` and
`-S` from them (they set `compile_only` / `assemble_only` and are re-added by
`BuildCompileCommand`). Nothing else in the key tells the two apart, so the same source
and flags compiled with `-S` hit an entry a `-c` compile stored and get an object where
an assembly file was asked for.

Reproduced on `a433d2a` (`fbg`) with gcc 16:
  vcache gcc -O2 -c t.c -o t.o; vcache gcc -O2 -S t.c -o t.s
  -> the second is a disk hit and `file t.s` says "ELF 64-bit LSB relocatable".

Fix: hash a marker for the output kind in `ComputeKey` (the C/C++ manifest key already
does, in `CxxManifestKeyArgs`) and bump `kCacheKeyVersion`, since the key derivation
changes. Test: the two commands above miss twice and `t.s` is assembly text; show it
failing on the code before the fix.
close_reason: Output kind participates in the v4 compile key; bidirectional regression fails on 98184ae and passes after the fix. Full gate: 1395 unit and 1182 integration checks passed.

title: Scratch dir sweep keys on age alone; DiskStorage::Get passes dirfd 0 to utimensat
description:
Two pre-existing defects found by the reflink plan review (IDEA-reflink-compile-outputs.md, section 10). Branch fix/scratch-liveness, worktree /build/richard/claude-tmp/worktrees/vcache/scratch-liveness.

1. src/storage/disk_storage.cc DiskStorage::Get refreshes the entry mtime with `::utimensat(0, path.c_str(), nullptr, 0)`. dirfd 0 is stdin; it is ignored for an absolute path but resolves a relative VCACHE_DIR against whatever stdin is. Use AT_FDCWD. Check every other utimensat in src/ for the same mistake.

2. src/util/fs.cc RemoveStaleScratchDirs removes every child of <cache>/tmp whose top-level directory mtime is older than kStaleScratchSeconds (6 h, src/storage/disk_storage.cc). A running rustc writing files that already exist does not update that mtime, so a compile over six hours loses its stage dir under another process's trim; DiskStorage::Put calls the sweep on every shard budget crossing. Replace the age-only rule with a liveness rule: util::MakeScratchDir embeds the owner pid in the directory name (for example `<prefix><pid>-XXXXXX`), and the sweep never removes a directory whose owner process is alive (kill(pid, 0) == 0, or errno == EPERM). A directory whose owner is dead may be removed after a short grace period; a directory without a parseable pid (old naming) keeps the six-hour rule. Keep the sweep cheap: one readdir plus one kill per directory.

Rules: AGENTS.md applies in full. Each fix needs a test that fails first on the pre-fix code (tests/unit_test.cc has scratch-dir tests already; extend them, and for the utimensat fix a unit test with a relative cache dir and stdin not a directory, or a mutation if that cannot be arranged); record `Fails first:` lines in the commit body. Run `make` and `make test` through ~/bin/build-limited with MAKEFLAGS=-j8 and /usr/lib64/ccache removed from PATH. Commit in upstream style (`fix(storage):`, `fix(util):`), body ending with `Deploy: vcache`. Another agent is editing WriteFileAtomic and CloneFile in src/util/fs.cc at the same time: keep your hunks to MakeScratchDir / MakeTempDirUnder / RemoveStaleScratchDirs and their declarations. Push the branch to origin; do not merge to fbg and do not touch .beads.

title: Masquerade recursion: vcache and ccache exec each other forever when ccache's dir is on PATH
description:
## What
`util::FindInPath` skips only candidates whose realpath is vcache itself. With `/usr/lib64/ccache` on PATH after the masquerade dir, `g++` (vcache) resolves the real compiler to ccache's `g++`; ccache in turn skips only itself and runs the first other `g++` on PATH, the vcache link. The two exec each other without end, an unbounded process chain that made a 128-core host unresponsive for hours (integration section 8, run without ccache stripped from PATH).

## Fix
- vcache: export a hop counter (e.g. `VCACHE_MASQUERADE_DEPTH`) to the compiler it runs in masquerade mode; when vcache is entered with it already at a small limit (2), print one error naming the PATH candidate chain and exit non-zero instead of exec'ing.
- Optionally also skip known compiler wrappers (a candidate whose realpath basename is ccache or sccache) and say so in docs/.
- tests/integration_test.sh: remove ccache/sccache dirs from PATH at the top, and run the suite with a task limit, so a regression fails instead of hanging the host.

## Acceptance
Integration test: masquerade `g++` with a fake wrapper dir ahead of the real compiler whose `g++` execs the next `g++` on PATH (ccache's behaviour) exits non-zero within a second with the recursion error, and spawns fewer than 10 processes. Fails first on current main (under `timeout 5` and a pids limit).
close_reason: Fixed: hop counter in masquerade mode refuses at four; suite strips ccache/sccache from PATH

title: link cache: implement verification and gather evidence for an opt-in rollout
description:
The link cache in src/core/link.cc (kLinkKeyVersion = vcache-link-v4) is off by default while it earns trust. Existing integration tests cover cross-checkout bytes, map files/-Xlinker forms, corrupt sidecars, output ageing and absent-path tracing. vcache-232 measured about 310 links per build and 134 after one source edit, with link caching off. Warm hits can help unchanged link inputs, but changed object content still requires a real link; do not promise to eliminate all edit-triggered relinks.

This epic preserves the requested verify mode, devtools switch and two-week host/el10 soak. Track implementation, environment integration and evidence separately so code can land without pretending a two-week observation has already completed. Link caching remains opt-in and off by default; enabling ordinary hits after the soak is the owner's decision.

## Verify contract

VCACHE_LINK_VERIFY=1 (config link_verify) affects eligible hits when link_cache is enabled. It must run the real link under the existing tracer and return fresh outputs, fresh diagnostics and the real exit status on every attempted verification. Do not materialize cached outputs or replay cached stderr into the caller's paths before that link. Cache candidate bytes/metadata needed for comparison must remain stable despite concurrent eviction or replacement.

Compare the complete expected output set (main binary and map/other declared side outputs), contents and executable metadata. Use content digests for efficient comparison as appropriate, with test fixtures proving byte differences are caught. Missing/corrupt sidecars are ordinary unusable cache candidates, not semantic mismatches. A valid candidate plus successful fresh link either verifies or mismatches. A failed fresh link is a verification error, never a verified hit and never a fallback to the cached binary. The fresh link's ordinary failure/output policy applies.

Track separate append-only Counter entries for verified, mismatch and verification error so old positional stats remain compatible. Define existing hit/miss accounting explicitly: verification is a real link, not a served cache hit. Preserve admission/single-flight ownership and ensure a waiter cannot bypass verification after another process fills the entry. read_only does not write repairs; recache bypasses the candidate lookup; link_cache=false ignores verify with a documented effective configuration.

A mismatch keeps the fresh output and logs candidate/fresh digests, keys, output names, original command, toolchain, roots and trace outcome through VCACHE_LOG. Replace the candidate only through the ordinary fully validated fresh store path; a failed/incomplete trace must not bless a replacement. Retain enough evidence to reproduce mismatches before subsequent runs replace entries. Non-deterministic links count as mismatches too and require explanation, not an automatic exception.

## Implementation, integration and soak

- vcache-trk.1, core implementation: configuration, comparison, counters, logging, error/concurrency behavior, docs and comprehensive unit/e2e tests.
- vcache-trk.2, devtools integration: FBG_VCACHE_LINK=verify|on|off, default off; verify exports cache=1/verify=1, on exports 1/0, off exports 0/0. Clear stale exported values on mode transitions and follow the existing devtools precedence contract.
- vcache-trk.3, soak (blocked by both): deploy and record revisions, run real sunbird worktree churn on host and el10 in verify mode for at least 14 days, with hundreds of successful verifications on EACH store. Record start/end/delta counters, resets, coverage, elapsed days and representative commands. Any mismatch stops the soak and creates a reproducer/fix bead; restart the evidence window after the fix.

Require zero mismatches AND zero unexplained verification errors. Compare sunbird run_tests.sh --audit on both platforms with controls; record pre-existing failures separately. After clean verification, run a controlled ordinary-hit build and audit on each platform without changing global defaults, to prove the materialization path as well as fresh-link correctness. Record the owner decision and the linked sunbird rollout bead if enabled. Neither elapsed time alone nor zero mismatches with zero verifications is success.

## Verification strategy

A planted mismatch must be internally checksum-consistent (matching blob/sidecar digests and a valid manifest) yet contain stale output for otherwise matching inputs. Merely corrupting stored bytes exercises existing corruption detection and cannot prove semantic verification. Cover matching output, main-output mismatch, map-only mismatch, fresh-link failure, missing/corrupt candidates, incomplete trace, read-only, recache and concurrent lease waiters. Unit tests cover config/precedence and old/new stats formats. End-to-end fixtures compare fresh bytes, diagnostics, executable metadata, status and exact counter deltas. Record fails-first against pre-feature code or focused mutations.

No result-key bump is required solely for an observational verify mode. If key/manifest meaning changes, apply the matching version bump. Binary-changing commits end with Deploy: vcache; rebuild all three dist targets before starting the soak.

## Naming table

| Concept | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| User configuration | link_verify; VCACHE_LINK_VERIFY | Joins link_cache / VCACHE_LINK_CACHE |
| Site policy | FBG_VCACHE_LINK=verify\|on\|off | devtools exportVcacheEnv family |
| Counters | Counter::kLinkVerified; Counter::kLinkMismatch; Counter::kLinkVerifyError | Link scope; error is distinct from a byte mismatch |
| Display labels | link verified; link mismatch; link verify error | Stable meanings for reports and soak scripts |
| Decision log family | link verify: | Distinguishes real-link verification from link hit |
| Existing comparison boundary | AllOutputs; MaterializeOutputs; PlaceVerifiedClone | Reuse existing output-set and sidecar validation rules |
| Historical epic identity | vcache-trk | Bead IDs cannot be renamed |

Run every build, test and benchmark through ~/bin/build-limited, including commands in sibling repositories. Remove ccache/sccache directories from PATH before compiler suites; do not override wrapper limits or increase parallelism. Put new scratch, fixtures and logs under /build/$USER/codex-1000/<task>/; new worktrees under /build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/<repo>/<name>, from the appropriate integration ref (origin/fbg for vcache). Attach sunbird worktrees to a beads session before br or commits. Preserve existing work and follow AGENTS.md removal/overwrite approval rules.

For each new or changed regression assertion, show the defect against the pre-fix revision or a targeted mutation, then show the corrected result. Record the named failing assertion and revision/mutation in the implementation commit's Fails first line. Keep detailed command, configuration, status, counter deltas and VCACHE_LOG evidence; timing alone is not proof. Run the full make test gate before pushing. Binary-changing commits end with Deploy: vcache and rebuild dist/host, dist/el10 and dist/dc-build.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] vcache-trk.1 delivers verified fresh-link behavior, failures, side outputs, counters, logs, tests and deployment.
- [ ] vcache-trk.2 delivers the tested devtools switch with default off and a recorded compatible deployment.
- [ ] vcache-trk.3 records at least 14 clean days and hundreds of verifications per host/el10 store, audited controls and controlled ordinary-hit validation.
- [ ] The owner records the rollout decision; any enabled rollout has its own sunbird bead and off setting. No rollout is inferred from implementation completion.

Child map: vcache-trk.1 owns core implementation, vcache-trk.2 owns the devtools integration handoff (blocked by .1), and vcache-trk.3 owns the timed soak and owner decision (blocked by .1 and .2). Parent-child links prevent premature epic completion. Related measurement work is intentionally not a prerequisite.

Naming: tests/link_verify_worktrees.py is the manual real-build runner; tests/link_verify_worktrees_test.py owns evidence-gate tests; tests/link_verify_compiler.sh is the optional compile-normalization/link-wrapper helper, exported as LINK_VERIFY_COMPILER with LINK_VERIFY_ROOT per tree. title: link verification: compare fresh links with valid cached candidates
description:

Eligible candidates are validated but never placed over the caller's outputs before a real traced link. A mismatch may replace the candidate only through the existing fully validated storage path. read_only never repairs; recache bypasses the candidate; failed tracing cannot authorize a replacement.
