title: cxx hits: attribute warm compile CPU and rank measured optimizations
description:
Owner priority (2026-10-15): warm incremental build time over cold build time. A warm build is
hits plus links, so the cost of a hit is what vcache itself adds to every incremental build.

The vcache-232 measurement shows the warm cross-worktree build spending 3-10 s more system CPU
through vcache than through ccache (25 s against 17-22 s for 525 hits plus about 310 links),
with wall within 4%. Those CPU figures are ninja's whole child tree, links included, and no run
attributed the time, so nobody can yet say what a hit costs or where. The memo table proposed
for it (one shared digest table instead of one file per input under `<store>/filehash`) was
not staged for that reason: it is the identifiable syscall volume, not a measured one.

## What a hit does today (from the code, each a candidate)

1. Process start and gperftools initialization. Record the actual dist/host/vcache size/linkage;
   the original measurement described a 7.5 MB client.
2. `MakeScratchDir` under `<store>/tmp` before the lookup, removed by a guard afterwards, so a
   hit pays a mkdir and an rmdir it never uses.
3. Compiler identity (ResolveCompilerId) and any system-include-directory memo work actually
   observed; measure operations rather than assuming one stat/read per lookup.
4. Daemon connection/cache lookup traffic with VCACHE_DAEMON=auto. In RunCompile, a successful
   early manifest hit returns before OpenCompileSession: do not attribute miss-only lease or
   admission requests to it. Measure only round trips actually present.
5. Manifest blob read and parse (up to the stored states), then per recorded input: one `stat`
   plus one memo file open/read/close (`HashFileMemoized`), plus one `lstat` per absent path.
   A sunbird TU records hundreds of inputs.
6. Result blob read; object and depfile written into place (no fsync since the reflink work).
7. Counters and decisions written under the store (`RecordCounters`, `RecordDecision`), the
   `VCACHE_LOG` line when set.

## Method

Work on the host first and record current strace/perf availability and permissions. Confirm
ranking in el10 with host-side attribution to container processes where direct tools are absent.

1. **Compile-only warm run, both tools.** Build worktree B warm from A's store as in vcache-232
   ("How to rerun"), but drive only the object targets (an audited explicit object-target list, or
   parsed argument arrays from `compile_commands.json`), so links are out. Record wall, user and sys for
   vcache and ccache, three runs each, tools interleaved. This is the number the rest explains.
2. **One hit, repeated.** Pick three representative TUs (a small one, a median one, a
   PCH-consuming one). Run each hit 20 times uninstrumented for wall/user/sys, then collect separate perf stat
   and strace profiles under both tools. Probe supported events; wildcard syscall events
   are optional attribution, not required portable commands. Report syscall counts by class.
3. **Syscalls by phase.** `strace -f -T -tt -e trace=%file,%desc,%network` on one hit; bucket
   every call by the path it touches (`filehash/`, `tmp/`, the result blob, the manifest blob,
   the daemon socket, the compiler, the output dir, counters) and by the phase it falls in
   (start-up to first lookup, manifest validation, materialise, bookkeeping). `perf record -g`
   on the same hit for the user-side profile (hashing, parsing, start-up relocations).
4. **Projection.** From 2 and 3, the sys and user time each candidate above would save per hit,
   multiplied by 525 and by the hit counts of a typical incremental build (a leaf edit: 1
   compile, 0 hits; a shared-header edit: N hits or N preprocessor runs). Rank the levers:
   - shared mmap'd digest table, or stat identity stored in the manifest state so a same-tree
     hit needs no memo read at all (the state already holds the digest), or both;
   - validate the manifest in the daemon, which is long-lived and can keep digests in memory;
   - no scratch dir on the hit path (create it on the first miss step);
   - cheaper start-up (static or smaller client, lazier initialisation);
   - batch counters and decisions into one write.

## Acceptance

- A table on this bead: compile-only warm wall/user/sys for both tools; per-hit user and sys
  and syscall counts for the three TUs under both tools; the syscall-by-phase buckets for one
  vcache hit; the user-side profile's top entries.
- A ranked list of the levers with the projected saving per hit and per incremental build, and
  a recommendation of which to stage (each as its own bead). If the representative, uninstrumented median per-hit wall overhead is within 2 ms of ccache's,
  report that alongside user/sys and dispersion. A no-follow-up recommendation is valid only
  if aggregate incremental results show no material remaining cost.
- Scripts and logs under `/build/$USER/codex-1000/<task>/`, named on this bead. Keep the runnable
  recipe and results; do not remove existing artifacts without the required approval.

## Measurement controls and interpretation

The workflow must actually invoke cached compiles. An up-to-date Ninja target performs no lookup. Use fresh task-owned output/build directories or an explicit command replay with identical flags and roots; do not time a no-op or remove unrelated outputs. Include prerequisite PCH/generated headers and report setup separately. Parse compile_commands.json arguments safely; command strings need deliberate shell semantics, not whitespace splitting. Verify every measured invocation is the expected hit using counter deltas and VCACHE_LOG in a separate diagnostic run. Keep production verbosity off during primary timings.

Pick small/median/PCH cases by recorded input count or measured baseline cost and name the TUs. Run at least 20 uninstrumented repetitions per case/tool, and three interleaved aggregate runs. Record median, tail/spread, wall, child user/sys and separately attributed daemon CPU. Keep compiler/version, page-cache warmth, daemon mode, store settings, outputs and filesystem fixed; report filesystem, build-limited limits and background load. Cold page-cache experiments are a separately labeled control, not mixed into the warm result.

strace -c -w reports traced syscall wall time, not process system CPU; syscall-count attribution explains time but does not equal saved CPU. perf/strace perturb startup and must be separate from the primary benchmark. Probe available perf events/permissions, select supported syscall events or strace counts, and record unavailable tools explicitly rather than fabricate profile data. Container/host sampling must identify the exact process tree and daemon; no shared production counter reset.

Bucket startup, compiler identity, include-directory memo, manifest validation, filehash reads, absent probes, result materialization, scratch, daemon IPC and counter/log work. Reconcile bucket totals, unknown calls and daemon contribution. Support each projection with observations and uncertainty; avoid adding overlapping savings from alternative digest/manifest/daemon designs. Stat identity alone is not a content-correctness proof for a proposed memo optimization.

Distinguish scenarios: unchanged manifests are hits; a leaf source edit normally compiles; stale shared headers invoke -E, which may hit only with a preprocessed entry already seeded. Use measured invocation/hit counts in build projections, and keep links out of the compile-only cost. Any follow-up optimization gets its own bead and correctness tests; none is implemented here.

If a reusable harness is added, check its target selection, accounting and failure exits with deterministic fixtures; a deliberately missing invocation/changed counter must fail the corresponding guard. Preserve command/return-code/counter/log evidence for reproducibility. No new unit test is needed merely to record measurements.

## Names

| Concept | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| File digest cache | HashFileMemoized; filehash/ | Existing hash subsystem family |
| Scratch creation | MakeScratchDir | Existing util entry point |
| Persistent bookkeeping | RecordCounters; RecordDecision | Existing core names; distinguish counts from decisions |
| Optional repeatable harness | tests/cxx_hit_benchmark.sh | Names the Cxx hit being benchmarked |
| Historical task identity | vcache-tsw | Bead IDs cannot be renamed |

Run every build, test and benchmark through ~/bin/build-limited, including commands in sibling repositories. Remove ccache/sccache directories from PATH before compiler suites; do not override wrapper limits or increase parallelism. Put new scratch, fixtures and logs under /build/$USER/codex-1000/<task>/; new worktrees under /build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/<repo>/<name>, from the appropriate integration ref (origin/fbg for vcache). Attach sunbird worktrees to a beads session before br or commits. Preserve existing work and follow AGENTS.md removal/overwrite approval rules.

For each new or changed regression assertion, show the defect against the pre-fix revision or a targeted mutation, then show the corrected result. Record the named failing assertion and revision/mutation in the implementation commit's Fails first line. Keep detailed command, configuration, status, counter deltas and VCACHE_LOG evidence; timing alone is not proof. Run the full make test gate before pushing. Binary-changing commits end with Deploy: vcache and rebuild dist/host, dist/el10 and dist/dc-build.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Compile-only replay proves actual warm hits; at least three interleaved aggregate runs and 20 uninstrumented repetitions per representative TU report wall/user/sys, spread and daemon CPU.
- [x] Separate syscall/profile runs reconcile named phases and tool limitations without treating traced syscall wall time as system CPU savings.
- [x] Rank all proposed levers with supported projections and uncertainty; record adoption beads or an evidence-backed no-follow-up conclusion.
- [x] Preserve runnable commands, settings, revisions, output/hit accounting and logs under the current scratch policy.
notes:
# C/C++ warm-hit cost — 2026-10-15

The compile-only replay supports optimizing digest memo access first. For the median
host translation unit, vcache takes 7.47 ms versus ccache's 4.27 ms and makes 2,986
syscalls versus 907. Memo-file access accounts for 1,685 vcache calls. EL10 confirms
that ranking. Create a shared digest table (`vcache-83w`) and, separately, defer
unused scratch creation (`vcache-zs1`). These are follow-up implementations; this
measurement task (`vcache-tsw`) changes no shipped binary or cache policy.

The shared machine produced substantial scheduling outliers. These measurements
establish remaining CPU work and candidate ranking, not a reliable whole-build
speedup. Links, cold compilation and stale-header preprocessing are outside the
steady-hit comparison.

## Workload and controls

- Workload: sunbird `097a9f79db9e6a88b68d1575827a109241257172`, two fresh attached
  worktrees, Release, deployed targets, Clang 23, `SUNBIRD_TU_TIME=OFF`, Python build
  skipped. Explicitly replayed compile-database argument arrays, adding Ninja's
  `-MD -MF` depfile arguments equally for both tools. PCH prerequisites were built
  separately. No Ninja no-op or link is counted.
- Host: 522 object commands, excluding 10 PCH producers; EL10: 520, excluding 10.
  These differ from the historical 525-TU workload. The complete argument lists
  and unique output IDs are in each results directory's `commands.json`.
- Installed vcache and tracer: `eb9c25c51d409d656eab2627cf98d30a673a2067`.
  Repository HEAD when measured: `b7665a6` (documentation only above that build).
  Host vcache is 7,607,336 bytes, dynamically linked to libstdc++, libm, libgcc and
  libc; EL10 is 21,642,472 bytes, linked to libm and libc. Both retain symbols.
  Exact binary/tracer SHA-256 values are in `fingerprint.json`.
- Host ccache 4.12.3; EL10 ccache 4.11.3. Both Clang builds identify as 23.1.4
  `absent-deps-1`, with LLVM revisions `bb46d66418b9` (host) and `d657d8d8c0fd`
  (EL10). Compare tools within a platform, not absolute host versus EL10 times.
- Private 20 GiB stores; `VCACHE_CXX_MANIFEST=1`, `VCACHE_DAEMON=auto`, running
  private daemon verified for the final samples; idle timeout zero, single-flight
  and admission off, link cache/verification off. No production counters reset.
  Ccache uses the source tree's `cmake/ccache.conf` and base `/build/richard` on
  host, `/code` in EL10. Saved `*-config.txt` files contain all effective settings.
- Host source/build roots map to `/code/sunbird_strategy` and
  `/code/sunbird_strategy/build`. EL10 mounts both physical trees at the same
  `/code/sunbird_strategy`, with build output at `build-el10`.
- Warm page cache, fixed outputs overwritten by explicit cache invocations;
  no page-cache eviction. Primary timings have `VCACHE_LOG` disabled; separate
  diagnostic batches prove all manifest-hit decisions. Every measured command
  exits zero, and exact counter deltas prove 522/520 hits with zero misses.
- Every build/test/benchmark used `~/bin/build-limited`, with wrapper-provided
  parallelism. The captured limits were 64 CPUs, 88 GiB memory, no swap, and
  8,192 tasks, shared across the slice. Do not copy these limits into reruns.
  Hardware: Threadripper 9980X, 64 cores/128 threads, Fedora 44 kernel
  `7.2.9-200.fc44.x86_64`; `/build` is local NVMe XFS with `noatime`.
- No task setup builds overlapped the final timing runs. Other machine work was
  uncontrolled: load averages at fingerprint capture were 22.6/29.8/24.8;
  before final EL10 timing, 61.4/45.4/34.5. Aggregate wall includes Python replay
  scheduling; child CPU comes from `wait4` and excludes the Python parent.
  Daemon CPU is measured separately by PID/start-time and private store, at
  10 ms `/proc` tick resolution.

## Cross-worktree reuse versus steady hits

The first B pass from A's store is separate from the repeated warm B passes:

| Platform/tool | Invocations | Manifest/direct hits | Other result hits | Misses | Wall / child user / sys (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Host vcache | 522 | 32 | 464 | 26 | 14.893 / 103.780 / 27.721 |
| Host ccache | 522 | 0 | 0 | 522 | 18.415 / 613.759 / 37.223 |
| EL10 vcache | 520 | 520 | 0 | 0 | 4.616 / 1.368 / 7.017 |
| EL10 ccache | 520 | 520 | 0 | 0 | 3.789 / 1.516 / 3.628 |

The host generated `cmake_pch.hxx` contains an absolute checkout path. Its changed
contents reject a manifest state even when the subsequent preprocessed result
hits; `cross-b-vcache/0.vcache.log` records that example. The remaining host
misses and ccache's path sensitivity were not individually attributed. Do not
interpret the first host B pass as the cost of a manifest hit. After B is seeded,
all repeated host invocations hit. Canonical EL10 avoids that path-layout change.
The first EL10 B pass used direct disk fallback because restarting the container
stopped its daemon. It is retained as a control, not mixed into the final
running-daemon timings below.

## Three interleaved compile-only runs

Seconds; each cell lists rounds 0, 1, 2. Tool order was V/C, C/V, V/C. Every round
has exactly the workload's object count in manifest/direct hits. Daemon user/sys
are additional CPU, not included in child user/sys.

| Platform/tool | Wall | Child user | Child sys | Daemon user / sys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| host vcache | 0.819 / 0.419 / 1.802 | 1.246 / 1.208 / 1.072 | 4.638 / 4.381 / 4.403 | 0.25 / 0.81; 0.26 / 0.44; 0.22 / 0.42 |
| host ccache | 0.355 / 0.465 / 0.181 | 1.342 / 1.357 / 1.028 | 3.843 / 4.364 / 1.965 | — |
| el10 vcache | 10.855 / 8.629 / 4.732 | 1.006 / 1.072 / 1.314 | 4.911 / 5.278 / 5.795 | 0.12 / 0.29; 0.12 / 0.31; 0.12 / 0.31 |
| el10 ccache | 4.615 / 3.159 / 3.644 | 1.513 / 1.609 / 1.868 | 4.000 / 3.960 / 4.440 | — |

Median child system CPU is 4.40 s versus 3.84 s on host, plus 0.44 s daemon system
CPU; EL10 is 5.28 s versus 4.00 s, plus 0.31 s daemon system CPU. Median wall is
0.819 versus 0.355 s on host and 8.629 versus 3.644 s on EL10, with wide ranges.
The older 3–10 s whole-build CPU gap cannot be attributed wholesale to hits:
that workload included links and used a different target set and launch method.

## Twenty interleaved repetitions per translation unit

Selection is by unique depfile input count: lowest non-PCH, median non-PCH and
median PCH-consuming command. The PCH cases differ between platforms because
of their target/input distributions.

| Case | Source relative to sunbird | Host / EL10 inputs |
|---|---|---:|
| Small | `wiregen/WiregenDescriptor.cc` | 142 / 141 |
| Median | `sunbird/third_party/treelite_4_6_1_local/model_loader/detail/xgboost_json/delegated_handler.cc` | 335 / 335 |
| Host PCH | `sunbird/live/WarmupFeatureCalc.cc` | 541 / — |
| EL10 PCH | `sunbird/ensemble/testSymbolRules.cc` | — / 545 |

All times below are milliseconds per invocation, from the individual child
record, not the one-item thread-pool batch duration. p95 is the 19th ordered
sample of 20; no p99 claim. User and sys medians are computed separately and
need not sum to the median CPU total.

| Platform/case/tool | Wall median | p95 | Min–max | User median | Sys median | Syscalls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| host/small/vcache | 5.597 | 6.927 | 4.572–106.361 | 1.371 | 3.176 | 1309 |
| host/small/ccache | 3.323 | 6.553 | 2.926–95.077 | 1.263 | 1.808 | 506 |
| host/median/vcache | 7.469 | 208.876 | 6.518–593.250 | 1.196 | 4.962 | 2986 |
| host/median/ccache | 4.266 | 19.918 | 3.709–91.676 | 1.860 | 2.107 | 907 |
| host/pch/vcache | 8.127 | 9.480 | 7.416–10.956 | 1.531 | 5.784 | 4735 |
| host/pch/ccache | 4.976 | 5.740 | 4.169–6.536 | 2.095 | 2.142 | 1343 |
| el10/small/vcache | 10.898 | 12.163 | 9.198–12.500 | 0.758 | 5.481 | 1453 |
| el10/small/ccache | 6.615 | 7.732 | 4.383–8.886 | 0.391 | 3.502 | 558 |
| el10/median/vcache | 19.913 | 72.477 | 11.527–104.771 | 1.796 | 8.677 | 3226 |
| el10/median/ccache | 10.571 | 49.569 | 9.060–121.444 | 1.268 | 4.659 | 996 |
| el10/pch/vcache | 19.545 | 21.678 | 14.675–21.711 | 1.886 | 9.897 | 3535 |
| el10/pch/ccache | 17.564 | 76.228 | 14.026–96.635 | 3.502 | 7.602 | 1436 |

The median host non-PCH overhead is **3.20 ms**, exceeding the bead's 2 ms
comparison threshold. EL10's median non-PCH overhead is 9.34 ms; its PCH case is
within 2 ms (1.98 ms), despite extra system CPU. These are medians under the
recorded shared-host load, not latency guarantees.

Across each set of 20 vcache repetitions, daemon user/sys totals were host small
0/0 ms, median 0/0 ms, PCH 0/10 ms; EL10 small 0/0 ms, median 0/10 ms, PCH
10/20 ms. Zeros mean below tick resolution in the sampled windows, not free
service. Aggregate daemon CPU above is the stronger measure.

## Syscall attribution

Traces are separate from timing. Counts cover the cache process from `execve`
through `exit_group`; the attached EL10 trace excludes 69 Python child setup
calls before exec and the waiting parent. Split unfinished/resumed records are
recombined. No compiler process is executed on these hits.

| Platform/case/tool | Metadata | File I/O | Network | Memory | Locks | Process/other | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| host/small/vcache | 598 | 645 | 16 | 32 | 6 | 12 | 1309 |
| host/small/ccache | 335 | 82 | 0 | 59 | 1 | 29 | 506 |
| host/median/vcache | 1500 | 1418 | 16 | 34 | 6 | 12 | 2986 |
| host/median/ccache | 738 | 82 | 0 | 57 | 1 | 29 | 907 |
| host/pch/vcache | 2419 | 2249 | 16 | 33 | 6 | 12 | 4735 |
| host/pch/ccache | 1172 | 82 | 0 | 59 | 1 | 29 | 1343 |
| el10/small/vcache | 747 | 654 | 16 | 23 | 5 | 8 | 1453 |
| el10/small/ccache | 362 | 107 | 0 | 61 | 1 | 27 | 558 |
| el10/median/vcache | 1743 | 1431 | 16 | 23 | 5 | 8 | 3226 |
| el10/median/ccache | 795 | 107 | 0 | 66 | 1 | 27 | 996 |
| el10/pch/vcache | 1203 | 2279 | 16 | 24 | 5 | 8 | 3535 |
| el10/pch/ccache | 1233 | 107 | 0 | 68 | 1 | 27 | 1436 |

The class table groups `stat`/`readlink` as metadata, open/read/write/close and
filesystem mutation as file I/O, socket setup/send as network, allocation as
memory, and `flock`/`futex` as locks. Socket `read`/`close` are file-I/O syscalls in
that table; the path/phase table below correctly attributes them to daemon IPC.

Median vcache hit, with each syscall assigned exactly once:

| Phase/path bucket | Host calls | EL10 calls | Host traced elapsed (ms) | EL10 traced elapsed (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup/configuration/root resolution | 85 | 85 | 0.570 | 3.332 |
| Compiler identity memo | 13 | 12 | 0.079 | 0.103 |
| System include-directory memo | 0 | 0 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| Manifest key/source/include setup | 17 | 23 | 0.069 | 0.235 |
| Digest memo files | 1685 | 1690 | 3.833 | 19.389 |
| Manifest input identity validation | 336 | 337 | 1.106 | 13.523 |
| Absent-path probes | 769 | 1003 | 1.728 | 30.769 |
| Daemon IPC: manifest and result | 29 | 29 | 0.389 | 3.053 |
| Object/depfile materialization | 14 | 14 | 0.161 | 0.729 |
| Scratch/owner setup and cleanup | 26 | 21 | 0.203 | 0.398 |
| Counters | 10 | 10 | 0.134 | 0.515 |
| Other/unassigned | 2 | 2 | 0.007 | 2.849 |

Totals reconcile to 2,986 host and 3,226 EL10 calls. The two unassigned calls are
one `brk` during result receipt and process exit. Include-directory memo calls
are zero in these warm paths. The compiler identity uses its memo, not a compiler
version subprocess. The manifest and result blobs arrive over daemon sockets,
so there is no client blob-file read to count separately. There are two
connections, each with a configuration hello and GET: four request/reply
exchanges, with no compile-session, lease or admission request. Daemon work is
outside the client trace and is accounted for by its separate CPU measurements.

A memo hit performs open, fstat, read, EOF read, close: 337 memo reads on host
and 338 on EL10, including source-key work. These account for 56% and 52% of
all calls respectively. Absent probes remain necessary for correctness. A warm
hit creates a scratch directory and owner lock, then cleans them up. It updates
two counters in one locked write; it does not call `RecordDecision` or emit a
production log with logging disabled. Output writes have no fsync.

**Traced elapsed time is not system CPU or a saving estimate.** Ptrace and shared
host scheduling strongly inflate it, especially in EL10. It is retained only to
make the attribution reproducible; optimization projections use uninstrumented
CPU, call counts and sampling evidence.

## User-side sampling

Each profile samples 200 confirmed hits separately from timing; counters prove
401 hits per case/tool across strace (1), perf stat (200) and perf record (200).
Host perf/strace are 7.2.9/7.2; `perf_event_paranoid=2`, with user cycles and
instructions available. No kernel setting changed. EL10 has neither executable,
so host tools attach to the verified Python replay PID and inherit its children.
Reports filter to the cache process and use copied EL10 binaries/libraries.
`perf stat` includes the replay parent; its totals are not presented as client
CPU. Context-switch events are user-restricted and report zero, so they do not
establish an absence of scheduling delays.

Top resolved median-vcache symbols, percent of process-filtered sampled weight:

| Symbol | Host | EL10 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Loader `do_lookup_x` | 11.39% | 2.04% |
| Loader `_dl_lookup_symbol_x` | 11.11% | below the leading entries |
| Loader relocation (`_dl_relocate_object_no_relro`) | 4.86% | below the leading entries |
| `HashFileMemoizedAt` | 4.12% | 4.36% |
| BLAKE3 hash-many | 2.79% | 4.92% |
| libc memory copy | 3.38% | 4.03% |
| tcmalloc `CentralFreeList::RemoveRange` | 2.07% | 3.58% |
| Boost.Spirit depfile parsing sequence | 2.49% | 1.63% |

Loader symbols total 32.06% on host and 9.50% on EL10; EL10's client already
statically incorporates the C++ runtime. Host call stacks also show tcmalloc
initialization under startup. Unresolved sampled addresses remain 19.32%/24.75%
for the median profiles; no cost is assigned to those symbols. Sampling thus
supports candidate ranking, not exact whole-phase CPU accounting. Ccache's host
median profile is led by Zstd decompression (21.41%) and loader work; EL10 PCH
vcache is led by BLAKE3 (26.86%) and copying (12.87%), so memo work is not the
only cost across all objects.

## Ranked follow-ups and projections

These are screening estimates for the **host median hit**, not measured gains.
All ranges admit zero until a correct prototype demonstrates improvement. The
memo estimate is supported by 56% of calls, 4.96 ms measured system CPU and the
2.86 ms system-CPU gap to ccache. Startup uses its sampled loader share against
1.20 ms median user CPU. Scratch/counter estimates use their small call counts
with extra allowance for filesystem mutation. No estimate converts strace
elapsed time into saved CPU.

| Rank / lever | Potential saved user / sys per hit | CPU over 525 hits | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Shared mapped digest table | 0–0.2 / 0–3 ms; target 1–3 ms sys | 0–0.105 / 0–1.575 s | Stage `vcache-83w`; preserve full identity, settled-write and corruption safeguards |
| 1 alternative. Identity plus digest in manifest | 0–0.2 / 0–3 ms | Same envelope | Competes with the table; same-tree scope, format growth and invalidation proof needed; do not add savings |
| 2. Cheaper startup/lazy initialization | 0–0.5 / 0–0.2 ms | 0–0.263 / 0–0.105 s | Defer implementation; smaller EL10 loader share weakens a blanket static-link recommendation |
| 3. Lazy scratch allocation | 0–0.03 / 0–0.10 ms | 0–0.016 / 0–0.053 s | Stage `vcache-zs1`, small and independent; 26 host calls, not just mkdir/rmdir |
| 4. Daemon-side validation with resident digests | 0–1.2 / 0–3 ms client CPU | 0–0.630 / 0–1.575 s client CPU | Defer: overlaps memo designs, moves validation CPU to daemon; net saving may be zero or negative |
| 5. Batch counters and decisions | 0 / 0 from combining those operations | 0 | Already one hit-counter write, no decision write; a different concurrent-counter design needs contention evidence |

A bounded shared table is preferred over expanding every manifest with local
stat identities because it can share memoized digests across commands and
worktrees without duplicating identity data per manifest. This is a design
choice to validate, not a content-correctness proof. File replacement, restored
mtime, unsettled writes, torn publication and concurrent eviction must be tested.

For H unchanged-manifest hits, multiply a candidate's per-hit CPU range by H;
use 522/520 for this workload, 525 only for comparison with the historical one.
At 100 hits the memo target is 0.1–0.3 s system CPU, not necessarily wall time.
A leaf edit with one compile and zero hits saves zero hit-validation CPU.
A shared-header edit that invalidates manifests invokes preprocessing; those
commands are not counted as unchanged hits and belong to `vcache-axb`.
Parallel wall savings depend on critical-path work, contention and scheduling;
none can be inferred by dividing or summing these serial-hit estimates.

## Evidence, rerun and rejected controls

All scripts, configs, command lists, return codes, deltas, logs, perf data and
analysis are retained on `zeus.sg.fbg` at:

`/build/richard/codex-1000/cxx-hit-attribution-20261015/`

- `fingerprint.json`, `el10-daemon-environment.json`, `*-config.txt`: environment.
- `cxx_hit_benchmark.py`, `check_harness.py`, `run.py`, `el10.py`: guarded replay
  and limited execution; `host-final.json` / `el10-final.json`: measured configs.
- `host-results/idle-warm-*`, `host-results/repeat-*`: final host timings.
- `el10-results/daemon-warm-*`, `el10-results/daemon-repeat-*`: final EL10 timings.
- `diagnostics-vcache` / `daemon-diagnostics-vcache`: separate decision logs.
- Host `profile-*`; EL10 `host2-profile-*`, `el10-profile-control2`: valid profiles,
  exact host PID, per-profile child PID lists and 1/200/200 hit-counter evidence.
- `analysis.json`, `analyze.py`: all samples, syscall classes and reconciled buckets.
  `*.perf.data.flat` files contain the full resolved symbol rankings.
- `replay.py` and `REPRODUCE.md`: fresh-result rerun against the retained prepared
  worktrees; use a new label and do not overwrite earlier artifacts.

The accounting fixture deliberately omits an invocation, duplicates a target,
changes a hit counter, adds a miss, fails a command, resets/removes counters,
and inserts invalid compile-database entries. Every mutation is rejected by its
named guard; quoted paths parse successfully. `harness-guards.log` records this.
No regression assertion was added to the repository solely to record measurements.

Rejected/control data is retained: early host warm batches overlapped setup;
EL10 `warm-*`/`repeat-*` ran with direct disk fallback; the first `host-profile-*`
attached to the waiting container entrypoint rather than its replay child and
has no useful cache samples. None enters the final comparisons above. The
corrected container profiles assert the actual replay PID and child hit counts.

The repository gate initially encountered a daemon-readiness failure, then a
compiler-barrier failure on the next run, with 1,470 unit checks passing on that
second run. Those unchanged synchronization checks and both logs are retained;
the subsequent full gate passed 1,470 unit, 1,320 integration, 93 link-verification
and 15 harness checks (`full-gate-final.log`). No test code was changed.


Validation: full-gate-final.log passed all four suites; git diff --check passed. Accounting mutation evidence is in harness-guards.log. Follow-ups: vcache-83w (shared digest table, P2), vcache-zs1 (lazy C/C++ scratch, P3). No binary or semantic cache key changes.
close_reason: Completed guarded host and EL10 compile-only measurements, syscall and user-cycle attribution, ranked projections and implementation follow-ups. Full gate passed; detailed evidence in docs/cxx-hit-cost.md and the retained task scratch directory.

title: tests: diagnose intermittent session-daemon readiness failures
description:
The full gate at merge 915156d failed 17 unit checks after two SessionDaemon startup failures, while the immediately preceding feature-branch gate passed all 1470 unit checks. The unchanged retry passed the unit checks. Similar readiness failures were observed during the earlier C/C++ attribution work; no open bead covers them (searched readiness and flaky).

Evidence: /build/richard/codex-1000/lazy-scratch-20261015/merged-gate.log, merged-gate-retry.log and full-gate-portable.log. The failed readiness checks precede the enabled-admission client and lease-review tests. SessionDaemon in tests/unit_test.cc waits on its ready pipe for 2000 ms; its failure currently cascades into checks against an unavailable server, then the destructor removes the diagnostics. These tests do not call the changed RunCompile path. Scheduling pressure is possible, but the root cause is not established.

Diagnose before changing timeouts: distinguish fork/pipe errors, interrupted poll/read, timeout, EOF, child exit and server initialization errors. Retain useful bounded diagnostics on failure. Add a deterministic failing-first case for the confirmed cause, or an injected diagnostic failure if the first change only improves observability. Do not hide failures with retries, skip assertions, or widen deadlines without evidence. Preserve bounded cleanup and the production daemon readiness contract.

Use ~/bin/build-limited for all builds/tests, strip ccache/sccache directories from PATH, and keep scratch under /build/$USER/codex-1000. Run the full gate, record failing-first evidence and land through the normal feature/fbg workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Establish and document the readiness failure cause with retained diagnostics.
- [x] Add failing-first coverage for the confirmed fix or injected diagnostic failures.
- [x] Preserve bounded cleanup and real failure reporting; pass the full gate without retry masking.
notes:
# Session-daemon test readiness

The failures recorded during the lazy-scratch change did not recur in six
instrumented unit-suite runs or 1,000 isolated daemon starts. Those runs do not
establish the cause of the historical failures.

The investigation did establish two defects in the test helper. Its single
`poll`/`read` attempt rejected an interrupted system call as a startup failure,
even when the daemon was ready. It also discarded the daemon's error reply and
removed the failed fixture, leaving no useful explanation. Some fixture setup
errors returned without recording a failed check at all.

`SessionDaemon` now waits against one monotonic two-second deadline. Interrupted
system calls resume within that deadline; there is no daemon restart or test
retry. Setup errors, poll/read errors, EOF, lock conflicts, unexpected replies,
server errors and timeouts produce distinct diagnostics. Error replies are
bounded to 4 KiB. A failed startup retains its directory, daemon logs and
`startup.txt`, including elapsed time, test section and child status. Cleanup
still stops and reaps the child; healthy fixtures are removed normally.

This changes test infrastructure only. The shipped daemon, cache keys and
installed binaries are unchanged. A future sporadic failure must be diagnosed
from the retained evidence; the interruption fix is not proof that it caused
the earlier failures.

## Verification

`tests/session_daemon_startup_test.py` runs a focused unit-binary entry point with
Linux `LD_PRELOAD` fault injection. It uses actual pipes and forked daemons,
checks nonzero exits for real failures, and rejects leftover child processes.

| Cases | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Healthy startup control | Pass | Pass |
| Interrupted poll or read | Fail | Pass |
| Directory, pipe or fork setup failure | Fail | Pass |
| Permanent poll or read error | Fail | Pass |
| Child exit, bind error or occupied daemon lock | Fail | Pass |
| Unknown or oversized readiness reply | Fail | Pass |
| Stalled child or repeated interruptions through the deadline | Fail | Pass |

The pre-fix executable comes from `2c5901f`, with only the focused probe entry
point added. All fourteen regression cases fail against it. All fifteen cases
pass on the host and with dc-build's GCC 11 and Python 3.6. The injection suite
explicitly skips non-Linux systems; macOS and arm64 were not executed.
The full host gate passed on its first run after the fix: 1,470 unit, 1,320
integration, 93 link-verification, 15 harness, seven scratch and fifteen startup
checks (`full-gate.log`).

Evidence is retained under
`/build/richard/codex-1000/daemon-ready-20261016/`: `startup-probe.log`,
`diagnostic-unit.log`, `diagnostic-unit-1.log` through `diagnostic-unit-5.log`,
`regression-before-final.log`, `regression-after.log`, `full-gate.log` and
`dc-regression.log`.
Detailed fault-case logs and retained fixtures are in
`/build/richard/codex-1000/dr-before-final-20261016/` and
`/build/richard/codex-1000/dr-after-20261016/`.

The normal `make test` gate includes the fault suite. For a single ordinary
startup, run `bin/vcache_test --session-daemon-startup-probe` through
`~/bin/build-limited`. Set `TMPDIR` under `/build/$USER/codex-1000/` first; compiler
suites also need ccache/sccache directories removed from `PATH`. The retained
`run.py` and `dc_verify.py` record the exact limited-execution commands used here.

Naming: SessionDaemonReadiness, WaitForSessionDaemonReady, SessionDaemonExitStatus and tests/session_daemon_startup_test.py join the existing SessionDaemon test family. No production symbols or semantic cache keys changed. No dist rebuild is needed.

Closure scope: used the bead's explicit diagnostics-first allowance. Confirmed failure causes are interrupted poll/read and silently ignored setup failures; final injected cases retain exact diagnostics and child status. Historical attribution is not claimed and is preserved in deferred follow-up vcache-rpf, triggered by a real recurrence. Acceptance item 1 is supported by these deterministic confirmed causes, not an assertion that the old unclassified log has been explained.
close_reason: Implemented the explicitly permitted diagnostics-first path, fixed proven interrupted-wait failures, and passed 14 failing-first regressions plus the healthy control and full gate. Historical attribution remains tracked separately.

title: docs: explain why prefix maps include self-maps
description:
The vcache-232 object comparison found two treelite objects whose __FILE__ reads
model_loader/detail/lightgbm.h through vcache and model_loader/./detail/lightgbm.h
through plain clang. A plain compile with vcache's same prefix-map flag reproduces the
vcache string, so the observed difference is not evidence of a wrong cache hit.

RootMap::PrefixMapArgs in src/core/roots.cc emits -ffile-prefix-map=<root>=<canonical>
for every configured root, including a self-map where the two strings are equal.
Do not omit that flag as redundant: if the compiler normalizes a mapped path, omitting
only the canonical tree's flag can make entry bytes depend on which tree filled the
same key. Uniform mapping keeps the compiler invocation consistent across fill trees.
This is the owner's requested documentation change, not a change to mapping behavior.

## Scope and acceptance

Add one short paragraph to docs/design.md near canonical roots/prefix maps that:
- States that every configured root gets a map, including self-maps.
- Explains why consistent mapping matters for tree-independent cached bytes.
- Gives the observed clang __FILE__ example and explains that vcache versus an unmapped
  plain invocation may differ in path strings; the fair control uses identical map flags.

Do not promise that every compiler cleans all ./ or .. paths, that vcache lexically
normalizes trace probes, or that these are the only possible object differences. In
particular, .. through a symlink can carry filesystem meaning. Scope the observation
to the measured clang behavior; compiler-version-dependent claims need a reproducer.

Validate the wording against RootMap::PrefixMapArgs and the comparison notes. If a
fresh minimal example is needed, run the mapped/unmapped compiler control through
~/bin/build-limited with scratch under /build/$USER/codex-1000/<task>/. An equivalent
cross-tree mapped control is useful evidence, but do not add a regression test merely
to protect prose. No source code change, key bump or dist rebuild. Run the repository
make test gate through build-limited before pushing the documentation commit.

## Names

| Concept | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Root flag generation | RootMap::PrefixMapArgs | Existing core root family |
| C/C++ flag | -ffile-prefix-map | Exact option observed; do not conflate with filesystem resolution |
| Observable compiler string | __FILE__ | Names the measured effect |
| Historical task identity | vcache-utm | Bead IDs cannot be renamed |
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] One short design paragraph explains per-root self-maps, tree-independent bytes and the measured clang __FILE__ spelling example.
- [x] Claims are scoped to observed compiler behavior and distinguish prefix mapping from symlink-sensitive filesystem resolution.
- [x] Validate wording against RootMap::PrefixMapArgs and evidence; no code/key change; run the limited repository test gate before pushing.
notes: Implemented in docs/design.md beside prefix-map behavior. Checked the every-root loop in RootMap::PrefixMapArgs and the recorded clang object-comparison control. Documentation-only change; no new or changed regression test, key bump or binary deployment. Validation: build-limited make test passed 1451 unit and 1311 integration checks, 0 failed; cache wrappers stripped from PATH. Log: /build/richard/codex-1000/prefix-self-maps-20261015/make-test.log.
close_reason: Documented self-map correctness rationale and the measured clang path-string example; code/evidence review and full limited test gate passed.

title: Compile scratch dirs live in /tmp and leak when vcache is killed
description:
## What
Each compile, dep scan and link makes a scratch dir with util::MakeTempDir under $TMPDIR (default /tmp) and removes it in a destructor. A vcache killed mid-compile (SIGKILL, Ctrl-C, the integration suite's holder-gone cases) never runs it, so /tmp/vcache-XXXXXX dirs accumulate with nothing to remove them.

## Fix
Scratch dirs under <cache>/tmp (system temp dir only as a fallback); --trim and the store-side eviction check remove scratch dirs older than six hours. The integration suite points TMPDIR into its work dir.

## Acceptance
Unit: MakeScratchDir lands under <cache>/tmp, falls back when the cache cannot hold tmp/, and the sweep removes only old dirs. Integration: --trim removes a 7-hour-old scratch dir and keeps a fresh one (fails first on the old binary).
close_reason: Scratch dirs under <cache>/tmp, swept after six hours by --trim and the store-side check

title: fstrace: decide whether failed probes other than ENOENT should be recorded
description:
## Why

`emit_result` in `src/trace/fstrace.c` records a successful open or probe as `R` and an `ENOENT` failure as `M`;
`EACCES`, `ENOTDIR`, `ELOOP` and every other outcome record nothing, by design ("a permission error is a different
question"). For compiles and links that is right. For the sunbird test audit (`scripts/test-skip.py`), a test whose
behaviour depends on a permission-denied probe has an input the key cannot see. Found by the triangulated review of
vcache-6h7 (section 6.6). This bead is a decision, not a fix: close it with the decision recorded.

## What

Decide, with the owner, whether a new record kind for "probed, failed for a reason other than ENOENT" is worth a
format change (new kinds make old readers reject the trace, see vcache-6h7 D1), or whether the audit should document
it as a limit. Record the decision in `docs/design.md`.

## Acceptance

A one-paragraph decision in `docs/design.md` and this bead closed with the same text. No code change expected.
notes: Recommendation (document as a limit, no new record kind) written in docs/design.md, 71787a9 on fix/tracer-defects; left open for the owner to close.
close_reason: Decision: documented as a limit, no new record kind (docs/design.md, Known limitations, landed in fbg through 71787a9 / 7c0e548). The tracer records a successful open or probe as an input (R) and an ENOENT failure as an absence (M); EACCES, ENOTDIR, ELOOP and every other failure leave no record. A compile, a link or a test traced by sunbird's audit whose behaviour depends on such a refusal is keyed as if the probe had not happened, and a later change to that path's permissions or file type does not invalidate the entry. A reader refuses a trace holding a kind it does not know (ReadTraceRecords), so a new kind would make every older vcache and audit refuse every trace the new tracer writes, for a case that compiles and links rarely meet. Reopen if the audit meets a real test that depends on a permission-denied probe.

title: link cache: localize dependency-file outputs across worktrees
description:
Ordinary cross-worktree link hits can replay a linker dependency file containing the other checkout's absolute input paths. The executable can be byte-identical while link.d is wrong for the caller. This blocks acceptance of the host/EL10 link verification soak; leave verify enabled and do not enable ordinary defaults.

Observed 2026-10-17: latest host counters 170 verified / 5 mismatch / 0 verify error; EL10 946 / 0 / 0. All five host testWarnThrottle events have identical cached/fresh executable digests; only link.d differs. The first four share one candidate key and the fifth uses another. All nine referenced sidecars were recovered from the correct DiskStorage::PathForFile layout and authenticated against logged BLAKE3 digests. For each event, replacing only the physical worktree root makes cached/fresh depfile bytes identical; the root occurs twice (object prerequisite and empty rule). The earlier missing-sidecar statement was a lookup error, now corrected. Exact comparisons are in evidence/historical-depfile-comparisons.json and evidence/*.depfile.diff.

A private-cache reproducer against installed host e76153a proves the defect with Clang 23 + mold: cold A, same-tree A verified, cross-tree B mismatch, ordinary A hit serves B's paths, direct fresh A restores A's paths. All links return zero and executable bytes match. Source cause: ParseLink stores dependency outputs in untyped extra_outputs; ComputePreKey canonicalizes inputs; RunLink stores raw .linkout bytes; MaterializeOutputs replays those bytes. Mismatch stores can replace the same canonical result entry with another tree's depfile reference.

Repair requirements:
- Repair replay, not only the comparator. Recommended direction: type linker depfiles, canonicalize storage, localize replay, and compare the representation actually replayed against fresh output without hiding incorrect localization or root aliases. Preserve untouched fresh outputs in verify mode. Select the final representation/comparison design before implementation.
- Establish actual linker escaping. Existing ParseDepFile is not sufficient by assumption: measured mold and bfd space-containing names parse as two tokens; a literal backslash and colon fixtures refuse parsing. Decline ambiguous/unsupported transformations. Unreadable/unparseable candidates or fresh depfiles must never count verified or store partial results.
- Preserve targets, empty-prerequisite rules, output-set and sidecar integrity, opaque-output digest checks, modes/status, readonly/recache and concurrent replacement guards. Cover all recognized dependency option forms.
- Bump kLinkKeyVersion (currently vcache-link-v5), invalidating both manifest and result lookups. Prove old warm entry -> upgraded miss -> new warm hit. A header change is needed only if its format changes.
- Show fails-first cross-tree verification and ordinary replay regressions. Include destination fresh control, target/path/alias changes, escaping/ambiguity, read-only/recache, concurrency and genuine non-path mismatch coverage. Record failing assertions/pre-fix revision in commit body.
- Run build-limited make test, deploy installed host/EL10/dc-build pairs, run affected regressions in each environment and publish the merge per AGENTS.md. End binary-changing commit body with Deploy: vcache.
- Restart the required 14-day clean soak after corrective deployment; preserve existing failure evidence. Do not claim a downstream missed Sunbird rebuild: none was demonstrated.

Evidence/report/review files: /build/richard/codex-1000/link-depfile-investigation-20261017/ (reproduce.py, reproducer/results.json, escaping/results.json, investigation-v3.md, review_*.txt). All five first-round external reviews were collected and their claims checked. Final review dispositions and grading are retained in the report directory. Core source attribution, private-cache reproduction and all five historical path-only differences are independently verified. Adjacent maps/embedded paths and separated -Wl option parsing are not fixed by this bead unless separately justified; tested separate-option forms did not reproduce a missing-output hit.
notes: Argon independently found two additional requirements. Real mold/bfd paths with one literal backslash followed by hash, space or colon link successfully but ParseDepFile silently loses the actual prerequisite (all six cases parser status 1). Evidence: argon-probes/results.json in the investigation directory. Also tests/link_verify_worktrees.py phase_errors compares all output hashes across trees; do not use that unchanged for localized depfiles. Compare each replay against a fresh destination-tree control and keep binary comparisons strict. The existing renderer also has an escaped-colon round-trip defect, tracked separately; fix it or decline that path class before reuse.
close_reason: Both repairs are merged, tested, deployed and published as vcache 1.2; actual Sunbird host and EL10 adapters select the exact tested pairs with verification enabled. Post-delivery baseline and remaining sustained soak are recorded separately.

title: daemon: distinguish lock contention from interrupted and failed locking
description: Server::AcquireLock treats every failed nonblocking flock as another daemon holding the cache. Reproduced on dccde85 with real foreground daemons: EINTR is not retried, including before an actually held lock; ENOLCK and EIO yield readiness L and exit 3 instead of a startup error. title: fstrace: replace per-record writes with crash-detectable mapped chunks
description:
Replace per-record trace-log writes with shared mapped chunks while preserving every dependency record and fail-closed behavior. src/trace/fstrace.c currently emits one O_APPEND write per record; src/core/link_trace.cc::ReadTraceRecords serves both compile and link consumers. The vcache-232 cold fill measured 1m20 system CPU for vcache versus 47 s for ccache and 42 s for plain clang. That is motivation, not attributed savings. The owner requested mmap on 2026-10-15: complete records should be visible through the page cache without an exit flush.

## Format and lifecycle

- One scratch trace file per invocation, with a versioned header and disjoint fixed-size chunks. Start with 64 KiB chunks and measure waste. Define magic, version, header/chunk sizes, byte order, alignment and overflow checks explicitly. The shared allocation cursor must use aligned, process-shared, lock-free atomics on supported targets; otherwise choose the legacy mode before any writer starts.
- The parent sets up and publishes the file format before launching the traced process tree. A file's format never changes mid-run. Header/setup failure can choose the legacy append format for the whole invocation before publication. No header magic means legacy parsing; an unknown or malformed new header is an incomplete trace, never a guessed legacy log.
- Writers reserve disjoint chunks, allocate backing storage before touching mapped pages and never shrink the file during concurrent growth. Reservation, allocation and publication must tolerate a process dying at any step. A reserved-but-unpublished hole must be detectable as incomplete, not indistinguishable from a legitimate unused tail.
- Use per-thread ownership and a pid check after fork so a child never writes into its parent's chunk. Cover concurrent first emit, fork from multiple threads, exec, thread exit, constructor activity and reentrant hooks. Use raw syscalls and bounded state; no allocator/loader recursion or inherited lock waits.
- A record never spans chunks. Define an explicit publication protocol: start/in-progress state is visible before payload writes, and a committed length/marker is published with release ordering only after all bytes (including newline) exist. A newline stored last in source order alone is not a crash-consistency proof. The reader runs after writer completion, validates chunk boundaries, committed lengths and record kinds, and rejects partial records/unfinished chunks. Distinguish an unused zero tail from a writer killed before it copied any bytes.
- Preserve R/M/P/L/W/D records and their current classification, absolute path spellings (including symlink-sensitive ..), length limits and invalid-character rejection. Never rely on global chronological order between thread-owned chunks.

## Failure and fallback

Do not append legacy records or the legacy sentinel into the mapped file: such writes can collide with future reservations, and a reader could skip them as padding. After mapped mode is published, mapping/allocation/record failure sets an allocation-independent shared incomplete flag and the existing .incomplete marker where possible. If the marker cannot be created, the shared header is the backstop. Return the compiler's outcome, but never treat this trace as complete. Whole-invocation legacy mode retains its ! sentinel and short-write handling.

Handle unsupported allocation/mapping, ENOSPC/EDQUOT, limits, address/offset overflow and interrupted syscalls. Preallocation does not prove every filesystem can never fault later; document supported storage and conservatively decline trace reuse on detected failures. Account for a zero-length/header-only log and a reservation beyond EOF. Keep a bounded trace-size policy with an incomplete outcome, never silent truncation.

The new reader accepts old text traces. Mixed deployments must be considered: VCACHE_TRACER can name another version and binary/tracer are separate files. Negotiate/opt in to the new writer format from the new parent; without the opt-in a new tracer emits legacy format, so an old binary cannot silently consume a new log. Older tracers with new parents must either produce readable legacy logs or cause conservative refusal. Explain rollback/.prev behavior.

## Verification

Unit tests in tests/unit_test.cc cover legacy/new headers, unknown versions, allocation holes, invalid bounds/overflow, zero tails, boundary-size records, committed records and every partial-publication stage. Each intentional omission mutation must cause refusal at the assertion naming the lost dependency.

End-to-end tests in tests/integration_test.sh use real multithread/fork/exec fixtures with known unique read/absent/write/tool sets. Reconcile exact records; exercise thread reuse and growth. Kill a writer at deterministic publication barriers. Inject setup, allocation and mapping failure; also make marker creation fail and prove the trace still cannot authorize reuse. Exercise both compile-manifest and link consumers, including changed files and newly present absent paths. Preserve legacy short-write/sentinel tests; add mmap tearing tests rather than replacing coverage of a supported fallback. Test old/new parent-tracer pairings.

Logs must identify format/version, selected mode, incomplete reason and test phase; keep expected/actual record counts and fault points. Demonstrate fails-first using the old implementation for the syscall/performance invariant and mutations for new-format safety invariants. Full make test must pass.

## Performance and delivery

Measure host trace-log syscalls before/after using fd/path attribution: the successful mapped emission path should have zero per-record writes, with setup/allocation calls reported separately. Report wall/user/sys, trace allocated/apparent bytes and RSS on representative TUs and threaded lld. Verify el10 loading with cargo --version under the deployed tracer and real threaded links. Re-run the vcache-232 cold fill with other changes held fixed; report residual system CPU and warm-path regressions, without assuming the whole gap disappears.

No cache-key bump solely for a transport change that preserves the exact dependency semantics. The private trace format does need its own version. If dependency/key semantics change, apply the repository's matching key bump rule. Binary and tracer ship together, with explicit compatibility as above.

## Names

| Concept | Name | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Existing log channel | VCACHE_TRACE_LOG | Preserve the tracer's established environment family |
| New format opt-in | VCACHE_TRACE_FORMAT | Internal parent/tracer contract; document accepted versions, not a user tuning knob |
| C format constants | VCACHE_TRACE_* | Topic prefix in the global C namespace |
| C++ decoding | ReadTraceRecords; TraceRecords | Existing trace family inside vcache::core |
| Failure marker | .incomplete; TraceMarkedIncomplete | Existing consumer contract |
| Historical task identity | vcache-zfn | Bead IDs cannot be renamed |

Run every build, test and benchmark through ~/bin/build-limited, including commands in sibling repositories. Remove ccache/sccache directories from PATH before compiler suites; do not override wrapper limits or increase parallelism. Put new scratch, fixtures and logs under /build/$USER/codex-1000/<task>/; new worktrees under /build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/<repo>/<name>, from the appropriate integration ref (origin/fbg for vcache). Attach sunbird worktrees to a beads session before br or commits. Preserve existing work and follow AGENTS.md removal/overwrite approval rules.

For each new or changed regression assertion, show the defect against the pre-fix revision or a targeted mutation, then show the corrected result. Record the named failing assertion and revision/mutation in the implementation commit's Fails first line. Keep detailed command, configuration, status, counter deltas and VCACHE_LOG evidence; timing alone is not proof. Run the full make test gate before pushing. Binary-changing commits end with Deploy: vcache and rebuild dist/host, dist/el10 and dist/dc-build.

title: cxx hits: create scratch storage only after the manifest lookup misses
description:
Implement the small, independent hit-path cleanup identified by vcache-tsw (docs/cxx-hit-cost.md). MakeScratchDir currently precedes C/C++ manifest lookup. The measured host median hit spends 26 syscalls on scratch setup/owner tracking/cleanup, including a directory and owner lock it never uses; EL10 spends 21. This is under 1% of calls, so the projected CPU saving is at most about 0.13 ms/hit and must be measured rather than advertised as a major speedup.

In RunCompile, defer scratch allocation until the first operation that needs it. Preserve manifest snapshot timing, compiler identity, native-target probing, PCH identity, fallback behavior and guard lifetime. A complete early manifest hit should neither create scratch state nor depend on scratch availability. A stale or unusable manifest/result still creates scratch before preprocessing or compilation. Avoid refactoring the Rust, link or dependency-scan paths into this change.

Use MakeScratchDir and the existing scoped guard; choose a lazy helper only if it makes ownership clearer. Retain owner locking, crash cleanup and pass-through behavior when scratch creation fails on a real miss. No cache-key behavior change is intended; prove the same keys/results and document the decision. Do not remove absent-path validation or memo-file reads.

Evidence and replay scripts: /build/richard/codex-1000/cxx-hit-attribution-20261015. Measure with VCACHE_LOG off and prove hits from isolated counter deltas; profile separately.

Validation and landing: use ~/bin/build-limited for every build/test/benchmark; strip ccache/sccache PATH directories for compiler suites. New scratch goes under /build/$USER/codex-1000 and worktrees under /build/$USER/claude-tmp/worktrees/vcache. Preserve existing work. Demonstrate regression assertions failing on pre-fix code or a targeted mutation, record Fails first lines, run make test, and rebuild deployed binaries when landing a binary change. Read AGENTS.md before implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A failing-first warm manifest regression proves no scratch allocation/owner-file operations occur; the old implementation fails the assertion.
- [x] Miss, stale-manifest, unusable-result and scratch-failure tests preserve preprocessing, fallback and cleanup behavior, with failure evidence for changed assertions.
- [x] Host and EL10 traces remove hit-path scratch calls; three aggregate runs and 20 representative repetitions report wall/user/sys and spread even if the time saving is below noise.
- [x] Full gate passes; document unchanged semantic keys, commit Deploy: vcache and rebuild deployed binaries.
notes:
The follow-up `vcache-zs1` moves the existing C/C++ scratch allocation and its
cleanup guard past the early manifest-hit return, immediately before preprocessing.
A hit now restores its outputs even if both scratch locations reject allocation.
Cold misses, stale manifests and unusable cached results still allocate before
preprocessing; a miss with no scratch still passes through to the real compiler.

No cache-key/version change is needed: compiler identity, roots, manifest state

work. Its opportunity score was impact 1 × confidence 5 / effort 1 = 5; this is a
small independent cleanup, not the leading digest-table optimization.
